title: 正德十一年陝西鄉試錄
text:
第壹場
四書
文莫吾猶人也躬行君子則吾未之有得
劉序
同考試官教諭陳　批　此題似易而實難閒
卷絕無當人意者是作平正明白不怪不
腐寫出孔子謙已誨人之意故錄之以範
來學
同考試官教諭王　批　聖人從容不迫詞氣
顧欲發之文字閒吾見其難矣此篇體認
親切下語快徤且一結尤能推原立言本
意錄之
考試官教諭李　批　此題以道字立說方
有歸著是篇識見卓然蓋用心於理學者
考試官學正周　批　峻整明潔
道顯於言者疑其同於人道著於行者歉其無
於已聖人自謙之詞也蓋聖人言行皆極其至
者也今以言自附而不以行自居其欲人之勉
punctuated:
第壹場

四書

「文莫吾猶人也，躬行君子，則吾未之有得。」

劉序

同考試官教諭陳批：此題似易而實難，閒卷絕無當人意者。是作平正明白，不怪不腐，寫出孔子謙已誨人之意，故錄之以範來學。

同考試官教諭王批：聖人從容不迫詞氣，顧欲發之文字閒，吾見其難矣。此篇體認親切，下語快徤，且一結尤能推原立言本意，錄之。

考試官教諭李批：此題以道字立說，方有歸著。是篇識見卓然，蓋用心於理學者。

考試官學正周批：峻整明潔。

道顯於言者，疑其同於人；道著於行者，歉其無於已。聖人自謙之詞也。蓋聖人言行皆極其至者也，今以言自附，而不以行自居，其欲人之勉
translation_en:
First Session

Four Books

“In literary cultivation, perhaps I am the equal of others; but as for putting the conduct of a gentleman into practice, I have not yet attained it.”

Liu Xu

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: This topic seems easy but is actually difficult. Among the papers [?], none at all were satisfactory. This composition is balanced, straightforward, and clear, neither eccentric nor stale. It brings out Confucius’s intention of humbling himself and instructing others. We therefore record it as a model for future students.

Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor: The sage’s language and manner are composed and unhurried; yet to convey these in writing strikes me as difficult indeed. This essay grasps them intimately and expresses them with fluency and vigor. Its conclusion is especially able to trace the statement back to its original intention. We record it.

Comment by Examiner Li, Instructor: Only by grounding the argument for this topic in the word “Way” can it have a definite direction. This essay displays outstanding discernment; its author is evidently someone who has devoted himself to the Learning of Principle.

Comment by Examiner Zhou, School Instructor: Rigorous, orderly, lucid, and clean.

As for the Way manifested in words, he tentatively suggests that he equals others; as for the Way made evident in conduct, he expresses regret that he lacks it himself. These are the sage’s words of self-deprecation. The sage’s words and conduct alike reach the utmost perfection. Yet here he counts himself among others in speech, while making no claim for himself in conduct. His wish is that people should exert themselves …

title: 正德十一年陝西鄉試錄
text:
其實也固如是夫且其意以爲道之在人顯於
言者易爲力著於行者難爲功蓋言之無文行
之不遠文固所當尚也彼以君子性命之懿發
諸談論者皆能中其肯綮而秩然其順理以君
子德義之善見諸詞說者咸能揭其蘊奧而蔚
乎其成章是道之顯於言者人固能之我或亦
能之若詩書執禮形諸雅言雖不能超乎等夷
也尚可以企而及焉人固優爲我或亦可爲若
文行忠信舉以敎人雖未至拔乎儔匹也猶可
===
以比而同焉是何也以言闡道甚易吾故可以
猶乎人耳然力行不遠空言何補行尤所當勉
也凡措之躬行皆君子性命之眞得之天者體
于我而不虧見之踐迪舉君子德義之實脩于
我者質諸天而不愧是道之見於行者雖嘗發
夜以慨慕矣顧心欲其然而力有不足理與身
猶爲二物如君子道者三何有於我哉雖嘗強
勉以脩爲矣但志欲其然而力有弗逮人與道
終爲兩事如君子之道四何能於已哉是何也
punctuated: 其實也，固如是夫！且其意以爲，道之在人，顯於言者易爲力，著於行者難爲功。蓋言之無文，行之不遠，文固所當尚也。彼以君子性命之懿發諸談論者，皆能中其肯綮，而秩然其順理；以君子德義之善見諸詞說者，咸能揭其蘊奧，而蔚乎其成章。是道之顯於言者，人固能之，我或亦能之。若詩書執禮，形諸雅言，雖不能超乎等夷也，尚可以企而及焉。人固優爲，我或亦可爲。若文行忠信，舉以敎人，雖未至拔乎儔匹也，猶可以比而同焉。是何也？以言闡道甚易，吾故可以猶乎人耳。然力行不遠，空言何補？行尤所當勉也。凡措之躬行，皆君子性命之眞，得之天者體于我而不虧；見之踐迪，舉君子德義之實，脩于我者質諸天而不愧。是道之見於行者，雖嘗發夜以慨慕矣，顧心欲其然而力有不足，理與身猶爲二物，如君子道者三，何有於我哉？雖嘗強勉以脩爲矣，但志欲其然而力有弗逮，人與道終爲兩事，如君子之道四，何能於已哉？是何也？
translation_en:
…its actual practice: surely this is indeed his purpose! Moreover, his meaning is that, when the Way resides in a person, expressing it in words is easy to work at, while manifesting it in conduct is difficult to accomplish. For words without refinement do not travel far; literary refinement certainly deserves esteem. Those who express in discussion the excellence of the gentleman’s nature and Heaven’s mandate can all hit upon the essential points and follow principle in an orderly fashion. Those who express in discourse the goodness of the gentleman’s virtue and righteousness can all disclose their profound significance and compose splendidly patterned writings. Thus, as for expressing the Way in words, others certainly can do it, and perhaps I can too. In such matters as giving voice in correct speech to the Odes, the Documents, and the observance of ritual, although I cannot surpass my peers, I may still aspire to reach their level. Others certainly perform these things admirably, and perhaps I too can perform them. In such matters as teaching others through cultural learning, conduct, loyalty, and trustworthiness, although I have not risen above my companions, I may still stand alongside them as their equal. Why is this? Expounding the Way in words is very easy; thus I can be like other people in this respect.

Yet if earnest practice does not extend far, what use are empty words? Conduct especially demands effort. Everything put into personal practice is the authentic substance of the gentleman’s nature and Heaven’s mandate: what is received from Heaven is embodied in me without impairment. What is manifested in practical observance comprises the substance of the gentleman’s virtue and righteousness: what is cultivated in me can be submitted to Heaven without shame. As for the Way manifested in conduct, although I have at times yearned fervently for it at night [?], my heart desires it but my strength is insufficient; principle and my person remain two separate things. As with the gentleman’s threefold Way, what of it do I possess? Although I have at times exerted myself strenuously in cultivation and practice, my resolve desires it but my strength falls short; the person and the Way remain two separate things. As with the four aspects of the gentleman’s Way, which can I accomplish in myself? Why is this? …

title: 正德十一年陝西鄉試錄
text:
以身體道甚難吾故全末之有得耳夫言爲世
法而謂之猶人行爲世則而謂之末得聖人自
謙如此無非欲人知言行之難易緩急而自勉
也歟考之他章有曰君子耻其言而過其行又
曰君子欲訥於言而敏於行聖人之不貴言者
何哉蓋放言易而常失之有餘力行難而常失
之不足况周末專事彌文而不知力行爲何事
故聖人垂世立教每每以是爲防焉若六經之
文昭如日星而斯道頼以不墜果言之終可少
===
邪
時使薄斂所以勸百姓也
劉仕
同考試官教諭潘　批
時使薄斂處士子類
能言之至勸百姓處便窘澁不舒且率多
以效入講殊不知此言勸百姓非百姓勸
也此作說理詳明行文通暢允宜錄出
考試官教諭李　批
時薄字說得明快而
勸百姓上尤能發揮殆邃於本領者傑作
punctuated:
以身體道甚難，吾故全末之有得耳。夫言爲世法而謂之猶人，行爲世則而謂之末得，聖人自謙如此，無非欲人知言行之難易緩急而自勉也歟？考之他章，有曰：「君子耻其言而過其行。」又曰：「君子欲訥於言而敏於行。」聖人之不貴言者何哉？蓋放言易而常失之有餘，力行難而常失之不足。况周末專事彌文，而不知力行爲何事，故聖人垂世立教，每每以是爲防焉。若六經之文昭如日星，而斯道頼以不墜，果言之終可少邪？

時使薄斂，所以勸百姓也。
劉仕

同考試官教諭潘批：時使薄斂處，士子類能言之；至勸百姓處，便窘澁不舒，且率多以效入講。殊不知此言勸百姓，非百姓勸也。此作說理詳明，行文通暢，允宜錄出。

考試官教諭李批：時、薄字說得明快，而勸百姓上尤能發揮，殆邃於本領者傑作。
translation_en:
…To embody the Way in one's own person is exceedingly difficult; thus I have attained nothing at all [?]. His words serve as a model for the world, yet he says that he is merely like other people; his conduct serves as a standard for the world, yet he says that he has not attained it. In humbling himself thus, was the Sage not simply seeking to make people understand the relative difficulty and urgency of speech and action, and so exert themselves? Examining other chapters, we find: “The gentleman is ashamed when his words exceed his deeds.” It also says: “The gentleman wishes to be slow in speech and prompt in action.” Why does the Sage not prize words? Because speaking freely is easy, and one commonly errs through excess; putting things into practice is difficult, and one commonly errs through insufficiency. Moreover, in the closing years of the Zhou, people devoted themselves exclusively to elaborate outward forms and did not understand what earnest practice meant. Thus, in establishing teachings for later generations, the Sage repeatedly guarded against this. Yet the writings of the Six Classics shine like the sun and stars, and this Way depends upon them for its preservation. Can words, after all, really be dispensed with?

“Employing them at the proper seasons and levying light taxes: this is how to encourage the common people.”
Liu Shi

Comment by Associate Examiner Pan, Instructor: Candidates can generally discuss employing the people at the proper seasons and levying light taxes. When they reach the matter of encouraging the common people, however, their exposition becomes strained and halting; moreover, most bring the resulting effects into their explanation. They fail to understand that this passage speaks of encouraging the common people, rather than of the common people's being encouraged. This composition explains the principles fully and clearly, and its prose flows smoothly. It certainly deserves to be included in the record.

Comment by Examiner Li, Instructor: The words “proper seasons” and “light” are explained clearly and briskly, while the discussion of encouraging the common people is especially well developed. This is surely an outstanding work by someone deeply versed in the fundamentals.

title: 正德十一年陝西鄉試錄
text:
傑作一
考試官學正周　批　整潔可誦
不盡民之力不盡民之財勸民之道在是矣蓋
民之所賴以生者財與力也苟使之盡其力而
斂之盡其財豈勸民之道哉孔子以九經之事
告哀公而此言子庶民也其意若曰有天下國
家者不患百姓之不勸惟患仁政之不行彼國
有興作不能不使乎民也使之不時如民力之
弗堪何必也視農功之餘而爲力役之舉城郭
===
可脩也而版築之施無所妨宮室可興也而經
營之計有所待乃若春之耕夏之耘秋之收不
一槩而擾之焉國有經用不能不斂於民也斂
之不薄如民財之弗繼何必也計歲出之數而
爲歲入之常布縷粟米之征定以中正而不過
鄉遂都鄙之制取以什一而不違所謂夏之貢
殷之助周之徹皆率循而行之焉夫人情莫不
欲逸若勞之而盡其力非所以勸之也今也明
而使之則畎畝之中無舍我穡事之嘆而政之
punctuated:
傑作一。
考試官學正周批：整潔可誦。
不盡民之力，不盡民之財，勸民之道在是矣。蓋民之所賴以生者，財與力也。苟使之盡其力，而斂之盡其財，豈勸民之道哉？孔子以九經之事告哀公，而此言子庶民也。其意若曰：有天下國家者，不患百姓之不勸，惟患仁政之不行。彼國有興作，不能不使乎民也；使之不時，如民力之弗堪何？必也視農功之餘，而爲力役之舉。城郭可脩也，而版築之施無所妨；宮室可興也，而經營之計有所待。乃若春之耕、夏之耘、秋之收，不一槩而擾之焉。國有經用，不能不斂於民也；斂之不薄，如民財之弗繼何？必也計歲出之數，而爲歲入之常。布縷粟米之征，定以中正而不過；鄉遂都鄙之制，取以什一而不違。所謂夏之貢、殷之助、周之徹，皆率循而行之焉。夫人情莫不欲逸，若勞之而盡其力，非所以勸之也。今也明而使之，則畎畝之中無舍我穡事之嘆，而政之
translation_en:
… an outstanding composition—one [?].
Examiner Zhou, School Instructor, comments: “Neat and polished, and well worth reciting.”
Do not exhaust the people’s strength; do not exhaust their wealth: herein lies the way to encourage the people. For wealth and strength are what the people depend upon for their livelihood. If employing them exhausts their strength, and taxing them exhausts their wealth, how could this be the way to encourage them? Confucius explained the nine guiding principles to Duke Ai, and these words concern treating the common people as one’s children. Their meaning is as follows: those who possess the realm or a state should not worry that the people lack encouragement, but only that benevolent government is not practiced. When the state undertakes construction, it cannot avoid employing the people. But if it employs them at inappropriate seasons, what is to be done when their strength cannot bear it? It must undertake labor services only when agricultural work leaves time to spare. City walls may be repaired, but the work of building with rammed earth must not interfere with farming; palaces and buildings may be erected, but plans for their construction must await the proper time. As for spring plowing, summer weeding, and autumn harvesting, these must not be indiscriminately disrupted.
The state has regular expenses and cannot avoid taxing the people. But if its levies are not light, what is to be done when the people’s wealth cannot sustain them? It must calculate annual expenditure and establish a regular level of annual revenue. Levies of cloth, thread, and grain must be fixed at a fair and proper level, without excess; under the institutions of the xiang and sui districts and the du and bi settlements, one tenth must be taken, without departing from that rate. The systems called gong under the Xia, zhu under the Yin, and che under the Zhou are all to be followed and put into practice.
It is human nature to desire ease. To work the people until their strength is exhausted is no way to encourage them. Now, if they are employed discerningly [?], there will be no lament among the fields that ‘we must abandon our farming,’ and the government’s …

title: 正德十一年陝西鄉試錄
text:
所發藹然爲民父母之心所謂勸民之道不在
是歟人情莫不欲富若取之而傷其財非所以
勸之也今薄而斂之則閭閻之下無室如縣磬
之憂而仁之所施宛然如保赤子之念所謂勸
民之道不在斯歟是則不外乎順民之情而自
得乎勸民之道哀公宜知所務矣抑考之易曰
損上益下曰益損下益上曰損又曰說以先民
民忘其勞其意正與此合蓋上下相須之政莫
有切於此者顧惟盡其在我者而已初何容心
===
於人之勸而人自無不勸矣使哀公果能體而
行之尚何有築臺囿用田賦之過舉哉惜其不
足以語此
居惡在仁是也路惡在義是也居仁由義
大人之事備矣
同考試官訓導林　批〔作此義者於居路二字〕
率多組織陳言冗雜厭觀且於尚志本旨漫
無所見獨此篇措詞明潔認理精到並無宏
管律
punctuated:
所發，藹然爲民父母之心。所謂勸民之道，不在是歟？人情莫不欲富，若取之而傷其財，非所以勸之也。今薄而斂之，則閭閻之下無室如縣磬之憂，而仁之所施，宛然如保赤子之念。所謂勸民之道，不在斯歟？是則不外乎順民之情，而自得乎勸民之道，哀公宜知所務矣。抑考之《易》曰：「損上益下曰益，損下益上曰損。」又曰：「說以先民，民忘其勞。」其意正與此合。蓋上下相須之政，莫有切於此者，顧惟盡其在我者而已，初何容心於人之勸，而人自無不勸矣。使哀公果能體而行之，尚何有築臺囿、用田賦之過舉哉？惜其不足以語此！

居惡在？仁是也。路惡在？義是也。居仁由義，大人之事備矣。

同考試官訓導林　批〔作此義者於居路二字〕率多組織陳言，冗雜厭觀，且於尚志本旨漫無所見。獨此篇措詞明潔，認理精到，並無宏

管律
translation_en:
…what issues forth reveals the kindly heart of one who acts as father and mother to the people. Does not the way to encourage the people lie in this? Everyone desires wealth. To take from them and thereby damage their resources is no way to encourage them. If levies are light, households will have no fear of being as empty as a suspended chime stone; and the benevolence bestowed will clearly express the solicitude of one protecting an infant. Does not the way to encourage the people lie in this? Thus, simply by following the people's feelings, one naturally finds the way to encourage them. Duke Ai should know what to make his priority.

Moreover, examining the Book of Changes, we find: “To diminish those above and increase those below is called Increase; to diminish those below and increase those above is called Decrease.” It also says: “Lead the people with joy, and the people forget their toil.” Its meaning accords precisely with this. In governing, where those above and below depend upon one another, nothing is more essential. One need only fulfill what lies within one's own responsibility. Why deliberately concern oneself with encouraging others? They will naturally all be encouraged. Had Duke Ai truly embodied and practiced this, how could he have committed such errors as building terraces and parks and imposing a land levy? Alas, he was not fit to be instructed in this!

“Where is one's dwelling? It is benevolence. Where is one's road? It is righteousness. Dwell in benevolence and follow righteousness, and the work of a great man is complete.”

Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Assistant Instructor: 〔Those who compose essays on this passage, in treating the two words ‘dwelling’ and ‘road,’〕mostly weave together stale expressions, producing a tedious jumble wearisome to read. Moreover, they show no understanding of the fundamental purport of ‘exalting one's aspirations.’ This essay alone is clear and clean in its wording and precise and thorough in its grasp of principle, and has no grand… [?]

Guan Lü 管律.

title: 正德十一年陝西鄉試錄
text:
遠宜錄以範多士
同考試官教諭黃　批〔尚志一題正見亞聖之發氣象此作得之而達以雄健之詞宛然如〕
〔聆當時之謦欬矣子其尚志之士歟〕
考試官教諭李　批〔仁義之用甚大孟子意〕
〔正如此〕
考試官學正周　批〔說得明盡〕
盡脩已之道全治人之道大賢論士之尚志也
蓋脩已治人其道一而已矣孰謂士之脩乎已
===
者而非大人之事乎昔孟子告王子墊之意謂
夫士之爲士論其勢大人之事若無與於已論
其志大人之事實已具於身是故非仁之事士
固不爲也而志之所之果惡在邪曰仁而已仁
而曰居必其存主之間無一念而非惻隱之心
矣譬諸室廬然蓋須臾而不離也非義之事士
固不爲也而志之所向又惡在邪曰義而已義
而曰路必其趨向之際無一念而非羞惡之心
矣譬如道路然蓋往來而不違也夫居仁則心
punctuated:
遠，宜錄以範多士。

同考試官教諭黃批〔尚志一題，正見亞聖之發氣象。此作得之，而達以雄健之詞，宛然如〕〔聆當時之謦欬矣。子其尚志之士歟？〕

考試官教諭李批〔仁義之用甚大，孟子意〕〔正如此。〕

考試官學正周批〔說得明盡。〕

盡脩已之道，全治人之道，大賢論士之尚志也。蓋脩已治人，其道一而已矣。孰謂士之脩乎已者，而非大人之事乎？昔孟子告王子墊之意，謂夫士之爲士，論其勢，大人之事若無與於已；論其志，大人之事實已具於身。是故非仁之事，士固不爲也，而志之所之，果惡在邪？曰仁而已。仁而曰居，必其存主之間，無一念而非惻隱之心矣。譬諸室廬然，蓋須臾而不離也。非義之事，士固不爲也，而志之所向，又惡在邪？曰義而已。義而曰路，必其趨向之際，無一念而非羞惡之心矣。譬如道路然，蓋往來而不違也。夫居仁，則心
translation_en:
…far-reaching [?]. It merits inclusion as a model for the many candidates.

Associate Examiner Huang, Instructor, comments: 〔The topic of exalting one’s aspirations reveals precisely the bearing displayed by the Second Sage [?]. This composition grasps it and conveys it in vigorous language, just as though〕〔one were hearing his voice in those days. Are you perhaps a scholar who exalts his aspirations?〕

Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: 〔The application of benevolence and righteousness is very great. Mencius’s meaning〕〔is precisely this.〕

Examiner Zhou, Instructor, comments: 〔The explanation is clear and exhaustive.〕

To fulfill the way of cultivating oneself is to complete the way of governing others: this is what the great worthy meant in discussing a scholar’s exaltation of his aspirations. For cultivating oneself and governing others follow but one way. Who would say that a scholar’s cultivation of himself is not the business of a great man? The meaning of what Mencius once told Prince Dian was this: considering a scholar’s position, the business of a great man might seem to have nothing to do with him; considering his aspirations, the business of a great man is already fully present in his own person. Thus, a scholar certainly does nothing contrary to benevolence. But where, indeed, do his aspirations lead? To benevolence alone. To speak of benevolence as a dwelling means that, in what he holds fast within himself, there must be no thought that does not spring from a heart of compassion. It is like a house: he does not leave it even for an instant. A scholar certainly does nothing contrary to righteousness. But toward what, then, are his aspirations directed? Toward righteousness alone. To speak of righteousness as a road means that, in the direction he takes, there must be no thought that does not spring from a heart that feels shame at evil and detests it. It is like a road: in all his comings and goings, he does not depart from it. Now, when one dwells in benevolence, the heart…

title: 正德十一年陝西鄉試錄
text:
地高明而萬善之原以具由義則志趨正大而
萬事之榦以立士之所志如此是雖未得公卿
之位也而公卿之事醞藉於未遇之中者綽綽
而有餘裕雖未有大夫之責也而大夫之事藏
脩於未達之時者恢恢而無不足蓋育萬民莫
大乎仁也今所居之仁充之足以育之矣大人
所施之事不于是而完具矣乎正萬民莫先乎
義也今所由之義擴之足以正之矣大人所達
之道不于是而全備矣乎是則無與天下之事
===
而已具天下之理士之尚志如斯而已若夫小
人之事則固非所當為也彼王子墊者烏足以
知此耶大抵道在天下不以易地而有顯晦士
之體道不以易地而有加損致廊廟之經綸即
江湖之志節初非二物也戰國之時名為士者
如淳于髡公孫丑之徒率不知此無怪乎王子
墊之問也世之輕吾士而小吾仁義一至此哉
嗚呼孟子之辯其亦不得已也噫
易
punctuated:
地高明，而萬善之原以具；由義，則志趨正大，而萬事之榦以立。士之所志如此，是雖未得公卿之位也，而公卿之事醞藉於未遇之中者，綽綽而有餘裕；雖未有大夫之責也，而大夫之事藏脩於未達之時者，恢恢而無不足。蓋育萬民莫大乎仁也，今所居之仁，充之足以育之矣，大人所施之事不于是而完具矣乎？正萬民莫先乎義也，今所由之義，擴之足以正之矣，大人所達之道不于是而全備矣乎？是則無與天下之事，而已具天下之理，士之尚志如斯而已。若夫小人之事，則固非所當為也。彼王子墊者，烏足以知此耶？大抵道在天下，不以易地而有顯晦；士之體道，不以易地而有加損。致廊廟之經綸，即江湖之志節，初非二物也。戰國之時，名為士者，如淳于髡、公孫丑之徒，率不知此，無怪乎王子墊之問也。世之輕吾士而小吾仁義，一至此哉！嗚呼！孟子之辯，其亦不得已也！噫！

易
translation_en:
…the ground of the heart becomes lofty and luminous, and the source of every goodness is thereby fully present. By following righteousness, one’s aspirations become upright and great, and the foundation of all affairs is thereby established. Such are the aspirations of the scholar. Thus, although he has not yet attained the position of a duke or minister, his capacity for their work, nurtured while he awaits recognition, is more than ample. Although he does not yet bear the responsibilities of a grand master, his capacity for a grand master’s work, stored up and cultivated before he attains office, is abundant and lacks nothing. For nurturing the myriad people, nothing is greater than benevolence. The benevolence in which he now dwells, brought to its fullness, suffices to nurture them. Are not the undertakings of a great man thus fully provided for? For setting the myriad people right, nothing takes precedence over righteousness. The righteousness he now follows, extended to its fullest reach, suffices to set them right. Is not the Way that a great man puts into effect thus fully complete? Thus, although he takes no part in the affairs of the world, he already possesses its principles in full. This is all that is meant by a scholar’s exalting his aspirations. As for the work of petty men, it is certainly not what he ought to undertake. How could that Prince Dian understand this?

In general, the Way’s presence in the world does not become manifest or obscure with a change in one’s station; nor does a scholar’s embodiment of the Way increase or diminish with such a change. The ability to order affairs at court is precisely the resolve and integrity maintained in retirement among rivers and lakes: these were never two different things. During the Warring States period, those called scholars, such as Chunyu Kun and Gongsun Chou, generally failed to understand this. No wonder, then, that Prince Dian asked his question. Has the world’s belittling of us scholars and disparagement of our benevolence and righteousness reached such a pass! Alas! Mencius, too, could hardly avoid making his argument. Ah!

Book of Changes

title: 正德十一年陝西鄉試錄
text:
女正位乎內男正位乎外男女正天地之
大義也家人有嚴君焉父母之謂也父父
子子兄兄弟弟夫夫婦婦而家道正正家
而天下定矣
王獻
同考試官教諭陳　批　〔家人題不難於措辭而〕〔難於整潔場中作者不腐則雜令人厭觀是〕
〔作理既詳明辭亦典則蓋邃於易者也三嘆〕〔之餘為予欽禮〕
===
同考試官教諭王　批　〔歛華就實關鍵自明與〕〔專騁浮辭者異矣是宜錄出〕
考試官教諭李　批　〔宛然正家氣象〕
考試官學正周　批　〔簡潔可愛〕
彖傳釋卦辭而指正家之本象卦畫而推正家
之化蓋女貞之辭由於卦體之二五而一卦六
畫一家之人象焉彖傳指言其本而推言其化
豈復有餘蘊哉昔吾夫子傳家人之彖意謂男
女乃人道之始閨門實風化之原故內正則外
punctuated:
女正位乎內，男正位乎外。男女正，天地之大義也。家人有嚴君焉，父母之謂也。父父，子子，兄兄，弟弟，夫夫，婦婦，而家道正。正家而天下定矣。
王獻
同考試官教諭陳批：〔家人題不難於措辭，而〕〔難於整潔。場中作者不腐則雜，令人厭觀。是〕〔作理既詳明，辭亦典則，蓋邃於易者也。三嘆〕〔之餘，為予欽禮。〕
同考試官教諭王批：〔歛華就實，關鍵自明，與〕〔專騁浮辭者異矣。是宜錄出。〕
考試官教諭李批：〔宛然正家氣象。〕
考試官學正周批：〔簡潔可愛。〕
彖傳釋卦辭而指正家之本，象卦畫而推正家之化。蓋女貞之辭，由於卦體之二五，而一卦六畫，一家之人象焉。彖傳指言其本，而推言其化，豈復有餘蘊哉？昔吾夫子傳家人之彖，意謂男女乃人道之始，閨門實風化之原，故內正則外
translation_en:
“The woman takes her proper place within; the man takes his proper place without. That man and woman should be correctly placed is the great principle of Heaven and Earth. The Family has stern rulers: this refers to the father and mother. When the father acts as a father, the son as a son, the elder brother as an elder brother, the younger brother as a younger brother, the husband as a husband, and the wife as a wife, the way of the family is correctly ordered. When families are correctly ordered, all under Heaven is settled.”
Wang Xian
Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: “With a topic on the Family hexagram, the difficulty lies less in phrasing than in achieving orderly clarity. Writers in the examination hall produce work that is either stale or cluttered, making it tiresome to read. This composition explains the principles fully and clearly, and its diction accords with classical standards. Its author must be deeply versed in the Book of Changes. After repeatedly sighing in admiration, I accord him my respect [?].”
Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor, comments: “By restraining ornament and attending to substance, he makes the crucial points clear of themselves. This differs from work devoted entirely to the display of empty phrases. It deserves to be selected for inclusion.”
Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: “It vividly conveys the spirit of correctly ordering the family.”
Examiner Zhou, School Instructor, comments: “Concise, clear, and pleasing.”
The Commentary on the Judgments explains the hexagram statement and points out the foundation of correctly ordering the family; it interprets the imagery of the hexagram’s lines and extends the discussion to the transforming influence of correctly ordering the family. The phrase concerning the woman’s constancy derives from the second and fifth lines of the hexagram’s structure, while the six lines of the whole hexagram symbolize the members of a family. The Commentary on the Judgments identifies this foundation and develops the implications of this transforming influence: could any meaning remain unexplored? When our Master of old composed his commentary on the judgment of the Family hexagram, his meaning was that man and woman constitute the beginning of the human order, and that the inner household is indeed the source of moral transformation. Thus, when what is within is correctly ordered, what is without…

title: 正德十一年陝西鄉試錄
text:
無不正矣彼辭之所謂利女貞者何哉蓋以家
必資女以治乎內也而卦之六二以陰居內體
之中得婦道之正而位乎內家必資男以治乎
外也而卦之九五以陽居外體之中得夫道之
正而位乎外夫男正於外而屬乎陽天之經也
女正乎內而屬乎陰地之義也今男女既正則
陰陽之大分明矣非天地之大義乎內外既正
則陰陽之大義明矣又非天地之大義乎然五
正乎外非徒有家而已也爲嚴君以統治於外
===
而爲父之尊焉二正乎內非徒中饋而已也爲
嚴君以統治於內而爲母之尊焉是則家道之
正非有本於是乎以卦畫推之上父初子父子
之象也五兄三弟兄弟之象也五三夫四二婦
夫婦之象也夫一家之中彝倫攸繫今父父子
子而尊卑之有倫兄兄弟弟而長幼之有序夫
夫婦婦而內外之有別是家道以之而齊閨閫
以之而正既正其家則天下之爲父子兄弟者
莫不各安其分矣天下豈有不定哉一家既正
punctuated: 無不正矣。彼辭之所謂利女貞者何哉？蓋以家必資女以治乎內也，而卦之六二以陰居內體之中，得婦道之正而位乎內；家必資男以治乎外也，而卦之九五以陽居外體之中，得夫道之正而位乎外。夫男正於外而屬乎陽，天之經也；女正乎內而屬乎陰，地之義也。今男女既正，則陰陽之大分明矣，非天地之大義乎？內外既正，則陰陽之大義明矣，又非天地之大義乎？然五正乎外，非徒有家而已也，爲嚴君以統治於外，而爲父之尊焉；二正乎內，非徒中饋而已也，爲嚴君以統治於內，而爲母之尊焉。是則家道之正，非有本於是乎？以卦畫推之，上父初子，父子之象也；五兄三弟，兄弟之象也；五三夫，四二婦，夫婦之象也。夫一家之中，彝倫攸繫。今父父子子而尊卑之有倫，兄兄弟弟而長幼之有序，夫夫婦婦而內外之有別，是家道以之而齊，閨閫以之而正。既正其家，則天下之爲父子兄弟者莫不各安其分矣，天下豈有不定哉？一家既正
translation_en:
…nothing will fail to be properly ordered. What does the statement that “it is beneficial for the woman to be steadfast and correct” mean? A household must rely on the woman to govern its internal affairs. The hexagram’s six in the second place, a yin line occupying the center of the inner trigram, attains the proper way of the wife and takes its position within. A household must rely on the man to govern its external affairs. The nine in the fifth place, a yang line occupying the center of the outer trigram, attains the proper way of the husband and takes its position without. That the man is correctly placed without and belongs to yang is Heaven’s constant principle; that the woman is correctly placed within and belongs to yin is Earth’s proper order. Now, when man and woman are correctly placed, the fundamental distinction between yin and yang becomes clear. Is this not the great principle of Heaven and Earth? When the inner and outer are correctly ordered, the great principle of yin and yang becomes clear. Is this not, again, the great principle of Heaven and Earth? Yet the fifth line’s correct position without signifies more than simply having a household: it acts as a stern ruler governing external affairs and thus possesses the dignity of a father. The second line’s correct position within signifies more than simply preparing the household’s food: it acts as a stern ruler governing internal affairs and thus possesses the dignity of a mother. Does not the proper ordering of the family’s way have its foundation here?

If we infer from the hexagram’s lines, the top line is the father and the first line the son: these are the images of father and son. The fifth is the elder brother and the third the younger: these are the images of elder and younger brothers. The fifth and third are husbands, and the fourth and second wives: these are the images of husbands and wives. Within a single household are bound up the enduring human relationships. When fathers act as fathers and sons as sons, higher and lower rank stand in their proper relationship; when elder brothers act as elder brothers and younger brothers as younger brothers, senior and junior have their proper order; when husbands act as husbands and wives as wives, the inner and outer spheres have their proper distinction. Through this, the family’s way is brought into harmony and the inner household is properly ordered. Once one’s family is properly ordered, all fathers, sons, elder brothers, and younger brothers throughout the world will rest content in their respective stations. How could the world fail to be settled? Once a single family is properly ordered…

title: 正德十一年陝西鄉試錄
text:
則天下之爲兄弟夫婦者莫不各得其所矣天
下之有不定哉是則正家之化不有在於是乎
吁夫子以是傳家人之彖則利女貞之義盡於
是矣大抵家之本在身身脩而家齊國治天下
平刑于寡妻至于兄弟以御于家邦同是理也
故男女正而爲天地之大義者卽造端乎夫婦
而察乎天地之意也正家而天下定者卽關雎
之風行而江漢汝墳之化成也有家有國之君
子盍於是乎求之
===
愼斯術也以往其无所失矣
劉夲
同考試官教諭陳　批　揭書出題無分難易第
作者類俗冗可厭明暢精切無踰此篇錄之
以爲易學式
同考試官教諭王　批　過愼无咎意人皆能言
之就題說理明盡無遺如此作者絕少可與
言易矣
考試官教諭李　批　善體認有發揮
punctuated:
則天下之爲兄弟夫婦者莫不各得其所矣，天下之有不定哉？是則正家之化，不有在於是乎？吁！夫子以是傳家人之彖，則利女貞之義盡於是矣。大抵家之本在身，身脩而家齊，國治天下平。「刑于寡妻，至于兄弟，以御于家邦」，同是理也。故男女正而爲天地之大義者，卽造端乎夫婦而察乎天地之意也；正家而天下定者，卽關雎之風行而江漢汝墳之化成也。有家有國之君子，盍於是乎求之？

愼斯術也以往，其无所失矣。
劉夲

同考試官教諭陳　批：揭書出題，無分難易，第作者類俗冗可厭。明暢精切，無踰此篇，錄之以爲易學式。

同考試官教諭王　批：過愼无咎意，人皆能言之；就題說理，明盡無遺，如此作者絕少，可與言易矣。

考試官教諭李　批：善體認，有發揮。
translation_en:
…then all brothers and spouses throughout the realm will find their proper places. How could the realm fail to be settled? Does not the transforming influence of setting the family right lie precisely here? Ah! In explaining the Judgment of the hexagram The Family, the Master fully elucidated the meaning of “it is beneficial for the woman to remain correct.” In general, the foundation of the family lies in the person: when the person is cultivated, the family is ordered, the state is governed, and the realm is at peace. “He set an example for his wife, extended it to his brothers, and thereby governed his family and state”: this expresses the same principle. Thus, the statement that men and women occupying their proper positions constitutes the great right order of Heaven and Earth means that the Way begins with husband and wife and is manifest throughout Heaven and Earth. The statement that setting the family right settles the realm means that the influence of “The Ospreys” spreads, and moral transformation is accomplished in the regions of the Jiang and Han rivers and along the banks of the Ru. Should not gentlemen who preside over households and states seek the principle here?

“If one proceeds with this cautious method, one will incur no loss.”
Liu Ben 劉夲

Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: When a question is drawn from the book, it matters little whether it is difficult or easy; the resulting compositions are mostly commonplace, prolix, and tiresome. In clarity, fluency, precision, and aptness, none surpasses this essay. It is included as a model for the study of the Book of Changes.

Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor, comments: Anyone can explain the idea that excessive caution brings no blame. But writers who elucidate the principle of the set topic with such complete clarity, leaving nothing unexplained, are exceedingly rare. This is someone with whom one can discuss the Book of Changes.

Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: He grasps the meaning well and develops it further.

title: 正德十一年陝西鄉試錄
text:
考試官學正周　批　理明詞整
持過愼之道以有爲則可以无過矣盖敬愼不
敗自然之理也能持是道以往尚何過之有哉
大傳舉大過初六爻義而釋之以示擬議之例
也其意若曰人固不可以无術而擇術不可以
不愼彼易所謂藉用白茅者愼之至術之善也
人能假在易之愼爲吾心之愼所以防微而杜
漸者必欲有周悉之圖決過愼之術爲吾身之
術所以謹始而慮終者必欲有萬全之計戒懼
===
存矣而隱微之地不可忽以之發言以之處事
无往而非兢業之心也涵養敬矣而體驗之功
不可少以之待人以之行己无適而非敬畏之
念也夫於術既无不愼則所往自无不宜非是
一念之謹百爲之機括所關覆緇蹈矩種種周
密自无滲漏之可言一敬之立萬事之根本攸
繫循途守轍在在順適自无罅隙之可議以靜
制動周旋有中禮之機言滿天下无口過行滿
天下无怨惡矣果何從而指其失邪以簡御煩
punctuated:
考試官學正周批：「理明詞整。」

持過愼之道以有爲，則可以无過矣。盖敬愼不敗，自然之理也。能持是道以往，尚何過之有哉？大傳舉大過初六爻義而釋之，以示擬議之例也。其意若曰：人固不可以无術，而擇術不可以不愼。彼易所謂「藉用白茅」者，愼之至、術之善也。人能假在易之愼爲吾心之愼，所以防微而杜漸者，必欲有周悉之圖；決過愼之術爲吾身之術，所以謹始而慮終者，必欲有萬全之計。戒懼存矣，而隱微之地不可忽，以之發言，以之處事，无往而非兢業之心也。涵養敬矣，而體驗之功不可少，以之待人，以之行己，无適而非敬畏之念也。夫於術既无不愼，則所往自无不宜。非是，一念之謹，百爲之機括所關，覆緇蹈矩，種種周密，自无滲漏之可言；一敬之立，萬事之根本攸繫，循途守轍，在在順適，自无罅隙之可議。以靜制動，周旋有中禮之機，言滿天下无口過，行滿天下无怨惡矣，果何從而指其失邪？以簡御煩，
translation_en:
Examiner Zhou, School Instructor, comments: “The principles are clear and the language well ordered.”

If one undertakes action while maintaining the way of exceeding caution, one can be without fault. That reverent caution averts failure is a principle inherent in the nature of things. If one can proceed while maintaining this way, what fault could there still be? The Great Commentary takes up and explains the meaning of the initial six line of the hexagram Great Exceeding, thereby illustrating how to model oneself on the Changes and deliberate upon them. Its meaning is as follows: people certainly cannot do without methods, and they cannot be incautious in choosing them. What the Changes calls “using white cogongrass as a mat beneath” represents the utmost caution and an excellent method.

If people can borrow the caution found in the Changes and make it the caution of their own hearts, then, in guarding against the slightest beginnings of error and forestalling their development, they will insist upon comprehensive plans. If they determine to make the method of exceeding caution their own method, then, in taking care at the outset and considering the outcome, they will insist upon wholly secure arrangements. Even when vigilance and apprehension are present, the hidden and subtle recesses must not be neglected. Applying this to speech and to the handling of affairs, wherever one goes one will maintain a watchful and diligent heart. Even when reverence has been cultivated, the work of examining it in experience must not be lacking. Applying this to dealings with others and to one’s own conduct, wherever one turns one will maintain thoughts of reverence and awe.

Once one is cautious in every method, whatever one undertakes will naturally be fitting. “Not this” [?]: vigilance in a single thought is what the workings of a hundred actions depend upon. “Covering the black cloth” [?] and treading within the rules, one is thorough in every particular, and naturally there can be no question of anything leaking through. The establishment of reverence is what the foundation of all affairs depends upon. Following the path and keeping to the tracks, one proceeds fittingly everywhere, and naturally there can be no question of gaps. By using stillness to govern movement, one’s every motion has the potential to accord with ritual propriety. Though one’s words fill the world, there will be no faults of speech; though one’s actions fill the world, they will provoke no resentment or hatred. Where, indeed, could anyone find a failing to point out? By using simplicity to govern complexity …

title: 正德十一年陝西鄉試錄
text:
左右有逢原之妙爲己也順而祥爲人也愛而
公矣抑何由而舉其過邪是則術之取乎易者
爲甚近而道之利乎用者爲甚周君子於此可
不知所擬議也哉抑論天下之事成於慎而敗
於忽故其亡其亡卒致苞桑之固而繻有衣袽
不可无終日之戒也古之聖賢未嘗不以懈惰
荒寧爲懼勤勵不息自強况其下者可不慎乎
然則君子宜何如亦曰觀象玩辭觀變玩占斯
得之矣此固聖人傳易之意也
===
同考試官教諭黃　批　寫出虞廷慎重典禮氣
氣象眞大方家作手也甯錄以式後學
此作不鑿不混詞意兩得模寫出當時雍容
本意顧於典禮伯夷處繫入寅清充覺疎謬
咨岳僉曰處忽略殊失虞廷君臣致重求賢
同考試官訓導林　批　題平易甚作者多於
管律
帝曰咨四岳有能典朕三禮僉曰伯夷
書
punctuated:
左右有逢原之妙，爲己也順而祥，爲人也愛而公矣，抑何由而舉其過邪？是則術之取乎易者爲甚近，而道之利乎用者爲甚周。君子於此，可不知所擬議也哉？抑論天下之事，成於慎而敗於忽，故「其亡其亡」，卒致苞桑之固，而「繻有衣袽」，不可无終日之戒也。古之聖賢，未嘗不以懈惰荒寧爲懼，勤勵不息，自強，况其下者可不慎乎？然則君子宜何如？亦曰觀象玩辭，觀變玩占，斯得之矣。此固聖人傳易之意也。

同考試官教諭黃批：寫出虞廷慎重典禮氣氣象，眞大方家作手也，甯錄以式後學。

此作不鑿不混，詞意兩得，模寫出當時雍容本意。顧於典禮伯夷處繫入寅清，充覺疎謬；咨岳僉曰處忽略，殊失虞廷君臣致重求賢。

同考試官訓導林批：題平易甚，作者多於

管律

帝曰：「咨，四岳！有能典朕三禮？」僉曰：「伯夷。」

書
translation_en:
…On every side there is the marvelous capacity to encounter the source: in acting for oneself, one is compliant and auspicious; in acting for others, loving and impartial. How, then, could anyone point out a fault? Thus, the method drawn from the Changes is readily accessible, while the Way’s usefulness in practice is thoroughly comprehensive. Can the gentleman fail to understand what to consider and deliberate upon here? Moreover, affairs under Heaven succeed through care and fail through neglect. Thus, the thought, “It may perish! It may perish!” ultimately brings the firmness of a clump of mulberry trees; and “for fine silk, have cloth rags ready” means that one must never dispense with vigilance throughout the day. The sages and worthies of antiquity invariably feared indolence and heedless ease, diligently exerting themselves without respite and strengthening themselves. How much more must those below them exercise care! What, then, should the gentleman do? Simply contemplate the images and ponder the statements, contemplate the changes and ponder the prognostications: thereby he will attain it. This was indeed the sage’s intention in transmitting the Changes.

Comment by Associate Examiner Huang, Instructor: This brings out the atmosphere of solemn care for ritual at the court of Yu [the transcription repeats “atmosphere,” 氣氣象; ?]. It is truly the work of an accomplished master. Let it be selected [?] as a model for later students.

This composition is neither forced nor muddled, and succeeds in both expression and meaning, portraying the original spirit of dignified composure at that time. Yet attaching “reverent purity” to the passage about Bo Yi’s supervision of ritual seems decidedly careless and erroneous [?]. Its cursory handling of “addressing the Four Mountains” and “they all said” seriously fails to convey the importance that ruler and ministers at the court of Yu attached to seeking worthy men.

Comment by Associate Examiner Lin, Assistant Instructor: The topic is exceedingly straightforward; writers mostly …

Guan Lü

The emperor said: “Ah, Four Mountains! Is there anyone capable of overseeing my three rites?” They all said: “Bo Yi.”

Book of Documents

title: 正德十一年陝西鄉試錄
text:
象宛然在目且詞語紆徐爾雅愈讀而愈不
厭有味之文固若是耶
考試官教諭李　批　虞廷命官之重薦賢之
公此作摸寫殆盡宜錄之
考試官學正周　批　簡明可愛錄之
聖君之簡禮官也慎廷臣之舉禮官也公蓋知
禮而後可以典禮也聖君慎簡其職廷臣得不
公所舉以對之哉昔帝舜當即位之時求典禮
之職意以職之仍舊者可以不咨矣事之或輕
===
者可以逕咨矣顧茲典禮之重適當新命之初
容可不咨于四岳耶誠以人君為天地之主祀
禮在所必行事莫有重焉者可無人以典之乎
天子為人鬼依歸祀典不可或廢禮莫有大焉
者寧無人以主之乎爾四岳也必遴選大小臣
工果有誠足以格神可典朕禮者其為我明揚
之凡坎壇昭穆之類一付之綜理焉慎簡內外
寮案果有明足以究禮克堪是責者其為我登
庸之若牲帛祝號之儀悉委之敘次焉帝舜簡
punctuated:
象宛然在目，且詞語紆徐爾雅，愈讀而愈不厭。有味之文固若是耶！
考試官教諭李批：虞廷命官之重、薦賢之公，此作摸寫殆盡，宜錄之。
考試官學正周批：簡明可愛，錄之。
聖君之簡禮官也慎，廷臣之舉禮官也公。蓋知禮而後可以典禮也。聖君慎簡其職，廷臣得不公所舉以對之哉？昔帝舜當即位之時，求典禮之職，意以職之仍舊者可以不咨矣，事之或輕者可以逕咨矣。顧茲典禮之重，適當新命之初，容可不咨于四岳耶？誠以人君為天地之主，祀禮在所必行，事莫有重焉者，可無人以典之乎？天子為人鬼依歸，祀典不可或廢，禮莫有大焉者，寧無人以主之乎？爾四岳也，必遴選大小臣工，果有誠足以格神、可典朕禮者，其為我明揚之。凡坎壇昭穆之類，一付之綜理焉。慎簡內外寮案，果有明足以究禮、克堪是責者，其為我登庸之。若牲帛祝號之儀，悉委之敘次焉。帝舜簡
translation_en:
…the scene stands vividly before one’s eyes. Moreover, the wording is unhurried, refined, and elegant: the more one reads, the less one tires of it. Surely this is what writing with lasting savor is like!
Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: This composition captures almost completely the gravity with which officials were appointed at Shun’s court and the impartiality with which worthy men were recommended. It deserves inclusion.
Examiner Zhou, School Instructor (xuezheng), comments: Concise, clear, and pleasing. Include it.
The sage ruler was circumspect in selecting an official responsible for ritual; his court ministers were impartial in recommending one. For only someone who understands ritual can preside over it. When the sage ruler selected someone for this office so carefully, could his court ministers respond with anything less than impartial recommendations? When Emperor Shun first ascended the throne, he sought someone to hold the office responsible for ritual. His thought was that offices whose incumbents continued unchanged required no consultation, while matters of lesser consequence could be put directly to those concerned. Yet responsibility for ritual was weighty, and this was precisely the beginning of a new reign: could he possibly omit consulting the Four Marchmounts? Indeed, the ruler serves as the chief sacrificer to Heaven and Earth. Sacrificial rites must be performed, and no undertaking is weightier. Could there be no one to preside over them? The Son of Heaven is the one upon whom both the living and the spirits of the dead depend. The prescribed sacrifices must never be neglected, and no rites are greater. Could there be no one to take charge of them? You Four Marchmounts must carefully select from among the officials, great and small. If there is indeed someone whose sincerity suffices to move the spirits and who can preside over my rites, make him known and commend him to me. Entrust to him the overall management of such matters as sacrificial pits and altars and the zhao and mu ordering of ancestral generations. Carefully choose from among the officials within and outside the court [?]. If there is indeed someone whose discernment suffices to fathom ritual and who can bear this responsibility, promote him to service for me. Entrust to him the ordering of all ceremonies involving sacrificial animals, silk offerings, invocations, and ritual appellations. Emperor Shun’s selection…

title: 正德十一年陝西鄉試錄
text:
典禮之官其愼也如此於是齊濟群臣拱聽於
淸問之下籲謀與論同聲於師錫之時謂求賢
君之盛心爲賢臣之重責容可不協諸公論乎
誠以三禮之典天地賴之以感格茍非其人必
至於黷矣典禮之官人鬼賴之以歆享不得其
人則幾於慢矣有伯夷者德無愧於天地有以
洞達禮之本原以之典三禮也必足以感格神
祇大小臣工孰有出其右乎行素合於神明有
以深喻禮之大體以之充是官也必足以歆享
===
人鬼內外資望莫能或之先也群臣舉典禮之
官莫公也如此吁虞廷於一典禮之官必簡之
愼而舉之公尚何不得人之有哉抑伯夷之賢
舜豈待問而後知耶蓋不自用其聰明而付之
公論此舜之所以聖也後世乃有不博謀於卿
相獨以私意用人或以讖兆或以資格而不察
其賢否之實者視舜之用人公私何如也有虞
之治卓乎不可及者以此
自成湯咸至于帝乙成王畏相惟御事厥
punctuated:
典禮之官，其愼也如此。於是齊濟群臣，拱聽於淸問之下；籲謀與論，同聲於師錫之時。謂求賢，君之盛心；爲賢，臣之重責，容可不協諸公論乎？誠以三禮之典，天地賴之以感格，茍非其人，必至於黷矣；典禮之官，人鬼賴之以歆享，不得其人，則幾於慢矣。有伯夷者，德無愧於天地，有以洞達禮之本原，以之典三禮也，必足以感格神祇，大小臣工孰有出其右乎？行素合於神明，有以深喻禮之大體，以之充是官也，必足以歆享人鬼，內外資望莫能或之先也。群臣舉典禮之官，莫公也如此。吁！虞廷於一典禮之官，必簡之愼而舉之公，尚何不得人之有哉？抑伯夷之賢，舜豈待問而後知耶？蓋不自用其聰明，而付之公論，此舜之所以聖也。後世乃有不博謀於卿相，獨以私意用人，或以讖兆，或以資格，而不察其賢否之實者，視舜之用人，公私何如也？有虞之治卓乎不可及者，以此。

自成湯咸至于帝乙，成王畏相，惟御事，厥
translation_en:
…an official in charge of ritual: such was his care in choosing one. Thereupon the assembled ministers, dignified and capable, listened respectfully to his discerning inquiry. Consulting and deliberating together, they spoke with one voice when collectively recommending a candidate. They held that seeking worthy men was the ruler’s noble aspiration, while serving as worthy men was the ministers’ weighty responsibility: how could they fail to accord with public judgment? Indeed, the rites of the three categories were the means of moving Heaven and Earth to respond. If entrusted to the wrong man, they would inevitably become profanation. The official in charge of ritual enabled the spirits of the departed to receive and enjoy offerings. If the right man were not obtained, the rites would verge upon disrespect. There was Bo Yi, whose virtue stood without reproach before Heaven and Earth and enabled him to comprehend thoroughly the foundations of ritual. Entrusted with the three categories of rites, he would surely be able to move the spirits of Heaven and Earth to respond. Who among the ministers, great or small, could surpass him? His conduct had always accorded with the spirits, and he deeply understood the essential principles of ritual. Appointed to this office, he would surely enable the spirits of the departed to receive and enjoy offerings. Among officials within and outside the court, none could take precedence over him in standing and reputation. Such was the unsurpassed impartiality [?] with which the ministers recommended an official to take charge of ritual.

Ah! At the court of Yu, even for a single official in charge of ritual, selection had to be careful and recommendation impartial. How, then, could they fail to obtain the right man? Yet did Shun have to wait until he asked before knowing Bo Yi’s worth? He refrained from relying solely on his own intelligence and discernment, entrusting the matter instead to public judgment: this was what made Shun a sage. In later ages, there were rulers who failed to consult widely with their high ministers and chief councillors, appointing men solely according to personal preference—sometimes on the basis of prophetic omens, sometimes on formal qualifications—without examining whether they were truly worthy. Compared with Shun’s appointments, how did theirs stand in impartiality or partiality? This is why the government of Yu was so outstanding as to be beyond the reach of later ages.

From Cheng Tang all the way down to Di Yi, the accomplished kings revered their ministers; as for those who managed affairs, their …

title: 正德十一年陝西鄉試錄
text:
梁有恭　　　　　　胡宗聘
同考試官訓導林　批　此作重湯之垂統最是〔且頭緒許多子能不費詞說語明意盡其於君臣盡道辯析不爽佳士也〕
同考試官教諭黃　批　題意重有商盛時湯以〔迪畏垂統于前而歷世君臣無不維持其統蔡註甚明但場中作者多昧深得此意辭足以達之無踰是篇故録〕
考試官教諭李　批　精當可録
考試官學正周　批　得旨
===
有商君皆盡其道臣亦盡其道先王垂統所致
也蓋迪畏天民商先王之垂統也則夫歷世君
臣之盡道夫豈無所自邪宜武王述之為康叔
告也吾想其意謂夫今之所宜法者不外於古
周之所宜監者莫近于商誠以畏天畏民之心
見於繼德象哲之際者湯之垂統然也豈惟湯
哉自成湯至于帝乙中間賢聖之君蓋六七作
punctuated:
梁有恭、胡宗聘。

同考試官訓導林批：此作重湯之垂統，最是。〔且頭緒許多，子能不費詞說，語明意盡，其於君臣盡道，辯析不爽，佳士也。〕
同考試官教諭黃批：題意重有商盛時，湯以〔迪畏垂統于前，而歷世君臣無不維持其統，蔡註甚明。但場中作者多昧，深得此意，辭足以達之，無踰是篇，故録。〕
考試官教諭李批：精當可録。
考試官學正周批：得旨。

有商君皆盡其道，臣亦盡其道，先王垂統所致也。蓋迪畏天民，商先王之垂統也，則夫歷世君臣之盡道，夫豈無所自邪？宜武王述之，為康叔告也。吾想其意謂：夫今之所宜法者，不外於古；周之所宜監者，莫近于商。誠以畏天畏民之心，見於繼德象哲之際者，湯之垂統然也。豈惟湯哉？自成湯至于帝乙，中間賢聖之君，蓋六七作
translation_en:
Liang Yougong; Hu Zongpin.

Associate Examiner Lin, Assistant Instructor, comments: This composition places its emphasis on Tang’s establishment of a tradition for his successors, which is entirely correct. 〔Moreover, despite the many strands of the argument, you avoid wasting words: the language is clear and the meaning fully expressed. Your analysis of rulers and ministers each fully performing their proper duties is unerring. You are an excellent scholar.〕
Associate Examiner Huang, Instructor, comments: The topic’s emphasis is on the flourishing age of Shang, when Tang 〔established a tradition for his successors through reverent observance, and rulers and ministers in successive generations all upheld it. Cai’s commentary makes this very clear, but many candidates in the examination hall fail to understand it. No essay surpasses this one in grasping this meaning deeply and expressing it adequately; hence its inclusion.〕
Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: Precise and apt; worthy of inclusion.
Examiner Zhou, Director of Studies, comments: It grasps the essential meaning.

That the rulers of Shang all fully performed their proper duties, and their ministers likewise fully performed theirs, resulted from the tradition established by the former kings for their successors. For reverently observing the claims of Heaven and the people was the tradition established by Shang’s former kings. Could the full performance of their duties by rulers and ministers through successive generations have had no source? It was fitting that King Wu should recount this in his admonition to Kangshu. I imagine his meaning to have been as follows: the models appropriate to the present are to be found in antiquity; and among the precedents from which Zhou should learn, none is closer than Shang. Truly, the reverence for Heaven and the people manifested in continuing the virtue of their predecessors and emulating wise men arose from the tradition Tang established for his successors. Yet was it Tang alone? From Cheng Tang down to Di Yi, some six or seven worthy and sagely rulers arose…

title: 正德十一年陝西鄉試錄
text:
也皆知人君一身上爲天命攸繫下爲民心所
關莫不憂勤惕厲無間其脩德之功晉接謙恭
每隆其敬臣之禮或楙德法祖也或成德允協
也脩己之道盡而德不愧于天一經德之矩度
焉或不背師保也或夢賚良弼也親賢之道得
而澤自下于民一秉哲之家法焉所謂君盡其
道也如此豈惟君哉自成湯至于帝乙當時御
事之臣非一二計也皆知人臣一身爲上而爲
德爲下而爲民莫不夙夜匪懈養君德於密勿
===
內外交脩保王躬於左右恐君不能經德也有
道以楙乃德者有啓以懷求圖者責難陳善之
恭曷嘗斯須替邪恐君不能秉哲也有戒以遠
耆德者有訓以若先民者任賢去邪之防曷嘗
頃刻置邪所謂臣盡其道也如此吁君盡君道
是君以遜畏爲心臣盡臣道是臣以迪畏爲心
皆不敢自暇逸也況敢崇飲乎抑觀武王告康
叔共懲而舉舉于商之君臣何哉蓋天下甫定
民方思慕商先王之德而未艾使康叔之□
punctuated: 也。皆知人君一身，上爲天命攸繫，下爲民心所關，莫不憂勤惕厲，無間其脩德之功；晉接謙恭，每隆其敬臣之禮。或楙德法祖也，或成德允協也，脩己之道盡，而德不愧于天，一經德之矩度焉；或不背師保也，或夢賚良弼也，親賢之道得，而澤自下于民，一秉哲之家法焉。所謂君盡其道也如此。豈惟君哉？自成湯至于帝乙，當時御事之臣，非一二計也。皆知人臣一身，爲上而爲德，爲下而爲民，莫不夙夜匪懈，養君德於密勿，內外交脩，保王躬於左右。恐君不能經德也，有道以楙乃德者，有啓以懷求圖者，責難陳善之恭，曷嘗斯須替邪？恐君不能秉哲也，有戒以遠耆德者，有訓以若先民者，任賢去邪之防，曷嘗頃刻置邪？所謂臣盡其道也如此。吁！君盡君道，是君以遜畏爲心；臣盡臣道，是臣以迪畏爲心。皆不敢自暇逸也，況敢崇飲乎？抑觀武王告康叔共懲而舉舉于商之君臣，何哉？蓋天下甫定，民方思慕商先王之德而未艾，使康叔之□
translation_en:
…All understood that the ruler’s person was, above, that upon which Heaven’s Mandate depended and, below, that to which the people’s hearts were attached. All were anxiously diligent and vigilantly cautious, never interrupting their efforts to cultivate virtue. Humble and respectful when receiving their ministers, they constantly enhanced the courtesies by which they honored them. Some fostered virtue and modeled themselves on their ancestors; others perfected their virtue and attained true harmony. They fully practiced self-cultivation, so that their virtue gave them no cause for shame before Heaven, all following the standards for making virtue their constant guide. Some never turned their backs on their preceptors and guardians; others were granted worthy assistants in dreams. They attained the proper way of drawing close to the worthy, so that their beneficence naturally descended to the people, all adhering to the ancestral rule of upholding wisdom. Such was what is meant by rulers fully performing their proper role.

Was this true only of the rulers? From Cheng Tang to Di Yi, the ministers who managed affairs could hardly be counted as merely one or two. All understood that a minister, in serving those above, must work for virtue, and in serving those below, must work for the people. All labored tirelessly day and night, nurturing their ruler’s virtue through devoted service. Within and without, they jointly worked at cultivation, attending the king on either side to safeguard his person. Fearing that their ruler might fail to make virtue his constant guide, some guided him with the injunction to “foster your virtue,” while others instructed him to “cherish, seek, and deliberate” [?]. When did their reverent duty of demanding difficult achievements and setting forth what was good ever lapse, even for an instant? Fearing that their ruler might fail to uphold wisdom, some admonished him concerning “distancing the aged and virtuous” [?], while others instructed him to “follow the men of old.” When did they ever set aside, even for a moment, their vigilance in employing the worthy and removing the wicked? Such was what is meant by ministers fully performing their proper role.

Ah! When rulers fully performed the ruler’s role, they took humility and reverence to heart; when ministers fully performed the minister’s role, they took the practice of reverence to heart. None dared indulge in leisure and ease; how much less would they dare esteem drinking! Yet consider King Wu’s admonition to Kang Shu concerning shared restraint [?]: why did he repeatedly cite the rulers and ministers of Shang? The realm had only just been pacified, and the people’s longing for the virtue of Shang’s former kings had not yet abated. If Kang Shu, at his [illegible] …

title: 正德十一年陝西鄉試錄
text:
初遽更爲一切之法以整齊之民將駭而不信
且不從矣洶洶之情何時已邪武王知其然一
則曰商先王一則曰商御事蓋欲以商法化商
民也卒之湎酒之俗革而允升于大猷有由然
哉
詩
鶴鳴于九皐聲聞于天魚在于渚或潛在
淵樂彼之園爰有樹檀其下維穀他山之
石可以攻玉
===

punctuated:
初，遽更爲一切之法以整齊之，民將駭而不信，且不從矣。洶洶之情何時已邪？武王知其然，一則曰商先王，一則曰商御事，蓋欲以商法化商民也。卒之湎酒之俗革，而允升于大猷，有由然哉！

詩
鶴鳴于九皐，聲聞于天。魚在于渚，或潛在淵。樂彼之園，爰有樹檀，其下維穀。他山之石，可以攻玉。

劉仕

同考試官教諭潘批：拈出「誠明兩立，愛惡不偏」作破講者，殊與朱傳不合。士子乃翕然趣之，何哉？獨是作力矯其弊，宜刻之以洗群謬。

考試官教諭李批：組織傳註爲文，法度森嚴，語意峻潔，胷中所養槩可見已。他日居在諫垣，必能進言如此詩矣。明經待用，非此謂邪？

考試官學正周批：縝密潔淨，無踰此篇。
translation_en:
…at the outset, abruptly replacing the existing arrangements with sweeping laws to bring the people into uniform order would alarm them and leave them distrustful; moreover, they would not obey. When would their agitation cease? King Wu understood this. At one point he spoke of the former kings of Shang, and at another of Shang’s officials: his intention was to transform the Shang people through Shang’s own laws. That the custom of excessive drinking was ultimately reformed, and they truly advanced toward the great Way, surely had its reasons!

Book of Odes
A crane cries in the deep marshes;
its voice is heard in heaven.
Fish are by the islet,
or hide in the deep pool.
Delightful is that garden,
where sandalwood trees grow,
and beneath them are paper mulberries.
Stones from other mountains
can be used to work jade.

Liu Shi

Comment by Associate Examiner Pan, Instructor: Those who select “sincerity and understanding established together, love and aversion without partiality” as their opening exposition depart markedly from Zhu Xi’s commentary. Yet the candidates flock unanimously to this interpretation. Why? This composition alone vigorously corrects that fault. It should be printed to sweep away the many mistaken interpretations.

Comment by Examiner Li, Instructor: He weaves the commentaries and annotations into a composition whose structure is rigorously ordered and whose language and meaning are elevated and clean. From this one can broadly discern what he has cultivated within himself. If one day he holds a post in the remonstrance service, he will surely be able to offer counsel as this ode does. Is this not what is meant by mastering the Classics and awaiting employment?

Comment by Examiner Zhou, School Instructor: In meticulous coherence and clarity, nothing surpasses this piece.

title: 正德十一年陝西鄉試錄
text:
詩人歷喻以告君無非陳善納誨之意也蓋諫
君之道亦多端矣不直指其事而惟託物以喻
之周之臣子可謂善於進言者歟此詩之作不
可知其所由然必陳善納誨之辭也且人君固
以從諫爲貴人臣實以進諫爲難直指其事則
徑情而不可入託喻以物則有味而或可悟周
人之陳于王者何如哉蓋以鶴一羽族耳九皐
之地至深邃也鶴鳴於其中而不期乎外之聞
九天之高至穹窿也鶴聲聞于上而不以其地
===
之遠然實有諸中必形諸外誠之不可揜也非
此類乎魚一鱗屬耳水岐成渚魚之以游以泳
或在于渚而非常止之處深水曰淵魚之或隱
或伏又潛于淵而無一定之方然因革靡常損
益達變理之無定在也非此類乎以至樂彼之
園樹檀森欝固嘉植也載瞻其下有穀交加寔
惡木焉是人必有愛愛之而當知其惡也實如
之他山之石物之粗屬若無用也玉之爲器資
以磨礱則有成焉是人必有憎憎之而當知其
punctuated: 詩人歷喻以告君，無非陳善納誨之意也。蓋諫君之道亦多端矣，不直指其事，而惟託物以喻之，周之臣子可謂善於進言者歟！此詩之作，不可知其所由，然必陳善納誨之辭也。且人君固以從諫爲貴，人臣實以進諫爲難。直指其事，則徑情而不可入；託喻以物，則有味而或可悟。周人之陳于王者何如哉？蓋以鶴，一羽族耳。九皐之地至深邃也，鶴鳴於其中，而不期乎外之聞；九天之高至穹窿也，鶴聲聞于上，而不以其地之遠。然實有諸中，必形諸外，誠之不可揜也，非此類乎？魚，一鱗屬耳。水岐成渚，魚之以游以泳，或在于渚，而非常止之處；深水曰淵，魚之或隱或伏，又潛于淵，而無一定之方。然因革靡常，損益達變，理之無定在也，非此類乎？以至樂彼之園，樹檀森欝，固嘉植也；載瞻其下，有穀交加，寔惡木焉。是人必有愛，愛之而當知其惡也，實如之。他山之石，物之粗屬，若無用也；玉之爲器，資以磨礱，則有成焉。是人必有憎，憎之而當知其
translation_en:
The poet presents successive analogies to instruct his ruler, all with the intention of setting forth what is good and offering admonition. There are indeed many ways to remonstrate with a ruler. Rather than pointing directly to the matter at issue, he conveys his meaning solely through analogies drawn from things. May we not call the subjects of Zhou skilled in offering counsel? We cannot know what occasioned the composition of this poem, but its words surely set forth what is good and offer admonition. Moreover, although a ruler is esteemed for accepting remonstrance, a subject truly finds it difficult to remonstrate. To point directly to the matter is to express one's feelings bluntly, so that the counsel cannot gain acceptance; to convey an analogy through things gives the words a savor that may bring understanding. What, then, did the man of Zhou set before his king?

Consider the crane: it is merely a feathered creature. The ninefold marsh lies in the deepest recesses. The crane cries within it, without expecting to be heard outside. The ninth heaven forms the highest vault, yet the crane's voice is heard above, undeterred by the remoteness of its location. Whatever truly exists within must manifest itself without: is this not an instance of sincerity's being impossible to conceal? The fish is merely a scaled creature. Where the water branches, an islet forms. As the fish swims about, it may be beside the islet, but this is no place where it always remains. Deep water is called a pool. The fish may hide or lie concealed, submerging again in the pool, without any fixed location. Yet continuity and change follow no constant pattern; through subtraction and addition one accommodates change. Is this not an instance of principle's having no fixed abode?

Then there is the delight afforded by that garden: its densely flourishing sandalwood trees are surely fine plants. Yet look beneath them, and paper mulberry trees intertwine—these are indeed inferior trees. People necessarily have those whom they love; in loving them, they ought to recognize their faults. This is precisely analogous. Stones from another mountain are coarse things and seem useless. Yet when jade is fashioned into an object, it is through their grinding and polishing that the work is accomplished. People necessarily have those whom they hate; in hating them, they ought to recognize their …

title: 正德十一年陝西鄉試錄
text:
善也實似之夫誠不可揜則身不可以不誠理
無定在則善不可以不明愛當知惡憎當知善
則好惡又可以或偏邪由是四者引而伸之觸
類而長之天下之理其庶幾乎則人以是陳善
納誨於君可謂微而不露婉而不迫深得諷諫
之道者矣大抵人君居安富尊榮之地侈心易
縱逸心易生自非賢智大有過人抑鳥能聽言
納善如轉圜哉故旁入曲諭者或可以感其心
而折廷諍者徒逆耳而無益也鶴鳴詩人不顯
===
言其事而惟託物以俟其自喻前無乃得於是邪
且其所陳者皆聖賢大學之教蓋亦周召之流
亞也豈後世能言之士所敢望哉
食之飲之君之宗之
盧昂
同考試官教諭潘　批　食飲君宗作者多牽合
纏繞且旁引立后立宗入講殊戾本旨觀朱
傳亦自可見是作體認獨真且言意爾雅而
當時氣象模寫殆盡故錄以為業葩經者式
punctuated:
善也，實似之。夫誠不可揜，則身不可以不誠；理無定在，則善不可以不明；愛當知惡，憎當知善，則好惡又可以或偏邪？由是四者，引而伸之，觸類而長之，天下之理，其庶幾乎？則人以是陳善納誨於君，可謂微而不露，婉而不迫，深得諷諫之道者矣。大抵人君居安富尊榮之地，侈心易縱，逸心易生。自非賢智大有過人，抑鳥能聽言納善如轉圜哉？故旁入曲諭者，或可以感其心，而折廷諍者，徒逆耳而無益也。《鶴鳴》詩人不顯言其事，而惟託物以俟其自喻，前無乃得於是邪？且其所陳者，皆聖賢大學之教，蓋亦周召之流亞也，豈後世能言之士所敢望哉？

食之飲之，君之宗之。
盧昂

同考試官教諭潘批：食飲君宗，作者多牽合纏繞，且旁引立后立宗入講，殊戾本旨。觀朱傳，亦自可見。是作體認獨真，且言意爾雅，而當時氣象模寫殆盡，故錄以為業葩經者式。
translation_en:
…the good in it: this is indeed analogous. Since what is genuine cannot be concealed, one must make oneself sincere; since principle has no fixed location, one must clearly discern goodness. Since one should recognize faults in what one loves and merits in what one hates, how could one allow one’s likes and dislikes to be biased? By extending these four points and developing them through analogy, might one not approach an understanding of the principles of all under Heaven? To present goodness and offer instruction to a ruler in this way may be called subtle without being overt, tactful without being insistent: it profoundly grasps the way of indirect remonstrance.

Generally, a ruler occupies a position of security, wealth, honor, and glory, where extravagant impulses are easily indulged and a desire for ease readily arises. Unless his worth and wisdom far surpass those of others, how could he [?] heed advice and accept what is good as readily as a round object turns? Thus, an oblique approach and indirect admonition may move his heart, whereas confronting and remonstrating with him at court merely offends his ears and achieves nothing. The poet of “The Crane Cries” (He ming) does not state the matter explicitly, but entrusts his meaning to things and waits for the ruler to understand for himself. Might this not exemplify the approach just described [?]? Moreover, everything he sets forth belongs to the sages’ and worthies’ teaching of Great Learning. He was surely of a stature approaching that of the Duke of Zhou and the Duke of Shao. How could eloquent men of later ages dare hope to equal him?

“He fed them and gave them drink; he became their ruler and their clan head.”
Lu Ang

Comment by Associate Examiner Pan, Instructor: In treating “feeding,” “giving drink,” “ruling,” and “heading the clan,” writers mostly force connections and become entangled in their explanations. They also introduce extraneous references to establishing a sovereign and establishing a clan head, seriously departing from the original meaning. This is evident from Zhu Xi’s commentary itself. This composition alone grasps the meaning truly. Its language and ideas are elegant and correct, and it portrays the circumstances and spirit of that time almost exhaustively. It is therefore included as a model for those studying the Classic of Poetry.

title: 正德十一年陝西鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭李　批〔詞氣舂容具見公劉篤〕
〔民之意要非苟作者〕
考試官學正周　批〔作雅義是如此〕
賢君之燕臣有以洽乎情而嚴乎分也蓋食飲
所以洽乎情而君宗所以嚴乎分也賢君落成
之燕何其恩禮之兼至也哉昔召康公以成王
將涖政當戒以民事故詠公劉之事以告之及
此謂夫我公劉之遷豳也宮室之制旣成燕勞
之恩斯溥于是進我群臣而食之執之於牢豕
===
以御也或肆或將而牲禮之旣備或燔或炙而
嘉殽之載陳使凡濟濟登筵者皆荷旣飽之恩
昔事營度之勞今享鼎俎之奉矣逮我群臣而
飲之酌之以匏酒以行也獻酬交錯而上下之
相歡勸侑慇懃而主賓之胥慶使凡蹌蹌依几
者舉承旣醉之惠向親經理之勤今適壺觴之
樂矣然非徒燕以勞之而已彼貴賤具在于几
筵統之必以君也君焉而公劉爲之則大夫仰
承而等威以辨士庶欽若而名分以立是雖几
punctuated:
考試官教諭李，批〔詞氣舂容，具見公劉篤〕〔民之意，要非苟作者。〕

考試官學正周，批〔作雅義是如此。〕

賢君之燕臣，有以洽乎情而嚴乎分也。蓋食飲所以洽乎情，而君宗所以嚴乎分也。賢君落成之燕，何其恩禮之兼至也哉！昔召康公以成王將涖政，當戒以民事，故詠公劉之事以告之。及此，謂夫我公劉之遷豳也，宮室之制旣成，燕勞之恩斯溥。于是進我群臣而食之，執之於牢，豕以御也。或肆或將，而牲禮之旣備；或燔或炙，而嘉殽之載陳。使凡濟濟登筵者，皆荷旣飽之恩。昔事營度之勞，今享鼎俎之奉矣。逮我群臣而飲之，酌之以匏，酒以行也。獻酬交錯，而上下之相歡；勸侑慇懃，而主賓之胥慶。使凡蹌蹌依几者，舉承旣醉之惠。向親經理之勤，今適壺觴之樂矣。然非徒燕以勞之而已。彼貴賤具在于几筵，統之必以君也。君焉而公劉爲之，則大夫仰承而等威以辨，士庶欽若而名分以立。是雖几
translation_en:
Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: “The language and cadence are stately and unhurried, fully revealing Gong Liu’s devoted concern for his people. This is certainly no carelessly composed work.”

Examiner Zhou, School Director, comments: “This is how an exposition of the meaning of the Odes of the Court should be written.”

When a worthy ruler feasts his ministers, he deepens their affection while maintaining strict distinctions of rank. Providing food and drink deepens affection; acting as their ruler and lineage head maintains those distinctions. At the worthy ruler’s feast celebrating the completion of his buildings, how fully both gracious favor and ritual propriety are realized! Formerly, because King Cheng was about to assume the government and needed to be admonished concerning the people’s affairs, Duke Kang of Shao sang of Gong Liu’s deeds to instruct him. At this point, the ode says that when our Gong Liu moved to Bin, once the palaces and dwellings were completed, the favor of a feast rewarding service was extended widely. He then brought forward all our ministers and fed them: an animal was taken from the pen, a pig being supplied for the occasion. Some laid out the carcass and others presented it, so that the sacrificial provisions were fully prepared; some roasted meat and others broiled it, so that fine dishes were set forth. All who ascended to the banquet in dignified array received the favor of eating their fill. Formerly they had labored over planning and surveying; now they enjoyed the offerings from cauldrons and meat stands. He also offered all our ministers drink, pouring it into gourds and passing the wine around. Toasts and answering toasts followed one another, as superiors and inferiors shared their pleasure; solicitous urgings to eat and drink were offered, as host and guests rejoiced together. All who moved with measured steps to their armrests received the bounty of drinking to satisfaction. Earlier they had personally undertaken the toil of organizing the work; now they enjoyed the pleasures of wine vessels and cups.

Yet he did not merely feast them to reward their service. Since noble and lowly alike were present among the banquet tables and mats, a ruler was indispensable to their governance. Gong Liu acted as that ruler: the great officers looked up to him and obeyed, so that distinctions of rank and dignity were made clear; the servicemen and common people reverently complied, so that their proper statuses and duties were established. title: 正德十一年陝西鄉試錄
text:
廂之上凜乎堂陛之嚴矣豈復草創之初而渙
然無制也邪觀時成饗于宗依沍之必以宗也
宗焉而公劉爲之則尊處於上而兄弟依歸主
臨於下而族黨繫屬是雖燕享之間截然冠履
之分矣寧復胥原之始而涣然無紀也邪吁一
燕飲之間洽其情而不泯其勞嚴其分而不溺
於恩公劉之厚民有如是哉抑嘗因是詩而知
周道興隆之漸矣蓋自不窋失官至公劉始脩
其業觀其遷國之謀經國之務營建之美燕勞
===
之情而規模宏遠固已駸駸乎帝王之治矣有
周王業此其基也召康公以成王將涖政而繼
成業告諭諄諄焉其亦有所感也夫其亦有
所警也夫
春秋
公及邾儀父盟于蔑　及宋人盟于宿
隱公元年庚辰公及戎盟于唐　紀子伯
莒子盟于密俱隱公二年齊侯鄭伯盟于
石門隱公三年春王正月公如齊　公至
punctuated:
廂之上，凜乎堂陛之嚴矣，豈復草創之初而渙然無制也邪？觀時成饗于宗，依沍之必以宗也。宗焉而公劉爲之，則尊處於上而兄弟依歸，主臨於下而族黨繫屬。是雖燕享之間，截然冠履之分矣，寧復胥原之始而涣然無紀也邪？吁！一燕飲之間，洽其情而不泯其勞，嚴其分而不溺於恩，公劉之厚民有如是哉！抑嘗因是詩而知周道興隆之漸矣。蓋自不窋失官，至公劉始脩其業。觀其遷國之謀、經國之務、營建之美、燕勞之情，而規模宏遠，固已駸駸乎帝王之治矣。有周王業，此其基也。召康公以成王將涖政而繼成業，告諭諄諄焉。其亦有所感也夫！其亦有所警也夫！
春秋
公及邾儀父盟于蔑，及宋人盟于宿，隱公元年。庚辰，公及戎盟于唐；紀子伯、莒子盟于密，俱隱公二年。齊侯、鄭伯盟于石門，隱公三年。春，王正月，公如齊；公至
translation_en:
…above the hall’s side chambers [?], the imposing distinction between the hall and its steps was already manifest. How could this still have been an initial period of foundation, loose and without institutions? Consider how the feast was held in the ancestral temple: those seeking support [?] necessarily depended upon a lineage head. With Gong Liu serving as their lineage head, he occupied the honored position above, and his brothers looked to him; he presided over those below, and his clansmen were bound to him. Thus, even amid feasting, the distinction between superior and inferior was as clear as that between cap and shoes. How could this still have been the beginning, when they surveyed the plain, loose and without order?
Ah! Within a single feast, he nurtured their mutual affection without letting their labors go unrecognized; he maintained strict distinctions of rank without allowing kindness to overwhelm them. Such was Gong Liu’s generous care for his people! Moreover, through this poem I have come to understand the gradual rise and flourishing of the Zhou way. After Bu Zhu lost his office, only with Gong Liu did the restoration of his ancestral undertaking begin. Consider his plans for relocating the state, his work of governing it, the excellence of his construction, and the sentiments expressed in feasting those who had labored: his designs were expansive and far-reaching, already advancing rapidly toward the government of true kings and emperors. Here lay the foundation of Zhou’s royal enterprise. As King Cheng was about to take up government and carry on the established undertaking, Duke Kang of Shao earnestly admonished him. Surely something had moved him to speak! Surely there was also something against which he wished to warn!
Spring and Autumn Annals
The duke and Yifu of Zhu made a covenant at Mie. He made a covenant with men of Song at Su. These entries are from the first year of Duke Yin.
On the gengchen day, the duke and the Rong made a covenant at Tang. Zibo of Ji [?] and the Viscount of Ju made a covenant at Mi. Both entries are from the second year of Duke Yin.
The Marquis of Qi and the Earl of Zheng made a covenant at Shimen. This entry is from the third year of Duke Yin.

Associate Examiner Peng, an Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔Who does not know the distinctions between Hua and Yi, or ruler and minister? Yet accounts that are rigorous and orderly, with exposition that is clear and incisive, seem exceptionally rare. This essay alone〕〔integrates the correct meanings of the two commentaries, with neither redundancy nor extraneous matter. In its treatment of the recording of days and months, it vividly conveys〕 the Sage’s voice: treating the Hua as insiders and the Yi as outsiders, exalting the ruler and subordinating the minister. title: 正德十一年陝西鄉試錄
text:
莒子爲于密之歃而石門之歃又齊鄭之合黨
也夫數盟皆成於日各書其日宜矣經於他盟
畧之獨詳於唐盟者何蓋魯以東蒙之國華也
戎本西方之類夷也華之於夷猶君子之於小
人其辨可不謹乎隱乃謬從戎使之請輕結魯
地之盟混衣冠於左衽雜侏儺於載書不知孰
爲華孰爲夷矣若列國之盟雖曰命不請於天
子約不由於周官然猶以類相從無損於國體
之尊也比諸交外者不有間哉故他盟不書日
===
獨於唐盟之上日以庚辰若曰戎入春秋以來
盟誓未同於中國是日也大防決矣其罪隱公
而謹華夷之辨爲何如哉魯宣之中邦交不絕
九年之春一朝齊也而返國之夏仲孫將命以
如京十年之春再朝齊也而旋軫之餘齊惠割
地以歸魯夫兩朝皆成於月各書其月宜矣經
於十年畧之獨詳於九年者何蓋周室雖衰君
也齊侯雖强臣也君之於臣猶天之於地其分
可不嚴乎宣乃春焉躬駕以朝齊夏焉遣使以
punctuated: 莒子爲于密之歃，而石門之歃又齊鄭之合黨也。夫數盟皆成於日，各書其日宜矣。經於他盟畧之，獨詳於唐盟者何？蓋魯以東蒙之國，華也；戎本西方之類，夷也。華之於夷，猶君子之於小人，其辨可不謹乎？隱乃謬從戎使之請，輕結魯地之盟，混衣冠於左衽，雜侏儺於載書，不知孰爲華、孰爲夷矣。若列國之盟，雖曰命不請於天子，約不由於周官，然猶以類相從，無損於國體之尊也。比諸交外者，不有間哉？故他盟不書日，獨於唐盟之上日以庚辰，若曰：戎入春秋以來，盟誓未同於中國，是日也，大防決矣。其罪隱公而謹華夷之辨，爲何如哉？魯宣之中，邦交不絕。九年之春，一朝齊也，而返國之夏，仲孫將命以如京；十年之春，再朝齊也，而旋軫之餘，齊惠割地以歸魯。夫兩朝皆成於月，各書其月宜矣。經於十年畧之，獨詳於九年者何？蓋周室雖衰，君也；齊侯雖强，臣也。君之於臣，猶天之於地，其分可不嚴乎？宣乃春焉躬駕以朝齊，夏焉遣使以
translation_en: …the Viscount of Ju in taking the blood oath at Mi, while the blood oath at Shimen was another partisan alliance, between Qi and Zheng. Each of these covenants was concluded on a particular day, so it would have been fitting to record the day of each. Why does the Classic omit this detail for the other covenants, yet give it specifically for the covenant at Tang? Lu, as the state of Dongmeng, belonged to the Hua, whereas the Rong were originally a western people and belonged to the Yi. The relationship of Hua to Yi is like that of gentlemen to petty men: could the distinction between them be left unguarded? Yet Duke Yin misguidedly acceded to the request of the Rong envoy and rashly concluded a covenant on Lu territory. He mingled those wearing ceremonial caps and robes with those whose garments fastened on the left, and mixed barbarian speech [?] into the covenant document, until one could no longer tell who was Hua and who was Yi. As for covenants among the other states, although their authorization was not sought from the Son of Heaven and their agreements were not arranged through Zhou officials, they still brought together those of the same kind and did no injury to the dignity of the state. Was there not a difference between these and establishing relations with outsiders? Thus the other covenants have no day recorded, but above the covenant at Tang the day is specifically given as gengchen. It is as though the text were saying: since the Rong first appeared in the Spring and Autumn Annals, they had never shared covenant oaths with the central states; on this day, the great barrier was breached. How forcefully it condemns Duke Yin and guards the distinction between Hua and Yi! During the reign of Duke Xuan of Lu, relations between states continued without interruption. In the spring of his ninth year, he made his first court visit to Qi; in the summer following his return, Zhongsun carried his commission to the royal capital. In the spring of his tenth year, he made a second court visit to Qi; after his carriage had turned homeward, Hui of Qi [?] ceded territory to Lu. Each visit took place in a particular month, so it would have been fitting to record the month of each. Why does the Classic omit this detail for the tenth year, yet give it specifically for the ninth? Although the house of Zhou had declined, it remained the sovereign; although the Marquis of Qi was powerful, he remained a subject. The relationship of sovereign to subject is like that of Heaven to Earth: could their respective stations be left unenforced? title: 正德十一年陝西鄉試錄
text:
聘周尊同列如共主等萬乘於庶邦不知孰爲
君孰爲臣矣若十年之朝雖曰魯不以道而得
地齊不以道而歸地然不過以利相結出於人
欲之私耳比諸慢上者不有間哉故十年不書
月獨於九年之下月以王正正若曰周自文武以
來正朔加於天下是歲也大統昧矣其罪宣公
而嚴君臣之分又何如吖謹華夷所以爲世道
慮嚴君臣所以爲王道憂謂春秋爲經世大法
信夫抑是傳之訓夾輔之勳周公家法具在而
===
其子孫壞之殆盡此尤可慨也雖然亦王靈不
振故耳使周有帝王之威德則四夷來王群后
四朝矣詎至此極乎端本澄源吾於周有望焉
秦人伐晉文公三年
劉大綸
同考試官訓導彭　批　作者徒知以責備爲言
而不體所以責備本意往往直寫傳文令人
厭觀曉得此卷原秦穆始終之美以發明聖
人責備之意其必精於是經者用是録之
punctuated:
聘周，尊同列如共主，等萬乘於庶邦，不知孰爲君、孰爲臣矣。若十年之朝，雖曰魯不以道而得地，齊不以道而歸地，然不過以利相結，出於人欲之私耳。比諸慢上者，不有間哉？故十年不書月，獨於九年之下月以王正，正若曰：周自文武以來，正朔加於天下，是歲也，大統昧矣。其罪宣公而嚴君臣之分，又何如吖？謹華夷，所以爲世道慮；嚴君臣，所以爲王道憂。謂春秋爲經世大法，信夫！抑是傳之訓、夾輔之勳，周公家法具在，而其子孫壞之殆盡，此尤可慨也。雖然，亦王靈不振故耳。使周有帝王之威德，則四夷來王，群后四朝矣，詎至此極乎？端本澄源，吾於周有望焉。
秦人伐晉，文公三年。
劉大綸。
同考試官訓導彭批：作者徒知以責備爲言，而不體所以責備本意，往往直寫傳文，令人厭觀。曉得此卷原秦穆始終之美，以發明聖人責備之意，其必精於是經者，用是録之。
translation_en:
…to pay a formal visit to Zhou. He honored a ruler of equal rank as though he were the common sovereign, and ranked the ruler of ten thousand chariots with the other states, no longer recognizing who was sovereign and who was subject. As for the court visit in the tenth year, although Lu acquired territory improperly and Qi returned it improperly, this amounted only to forming ties through profit, arising from selfish human desires. Compared with disrespect toward one’s sovereign, was there not a difference? Thus no month is recorded for the tenth year, whereas under the ninth year the month is specifically designated as the king’s first month. It is as though the text were saying: since Kings Wen and Wu, Zhou’s calendar had prevailed throughout the realm, but in this year the supreme succession was obscured. How, then, does its condemnation of Duke Xuan enforce the distinction between sovereign and subject? Maintaining the distinction between the Chinese states and the outsiders expresses concern for the moral order of the age; enforcing the distinction between sovereign and subject expresses concern for the Kingly Way. How true it is to call the Spring and Autumn Annals the great model for ordering the world! Moreover, the transmitted teachings [?], the achievements in supporting the royal house, and the Duke of Zhou’s ancestral rules were all still there, yet his descendants had almost completely destroyed them. This is especially lamentable. Even so, this also resulted from the failure of royal authority to assert itself. Had Zhou possessed the awe-inspiring power and virtue of a true emperor or king, the outsiders of the four quarters would have come to acknowledge its sovereignty, and the assembled lords would have attended court in the four seasons [?]. How could matters have reached such an extreme? To set the root right and cleanse the source—this is what I hope for from Zhou.
“The men of Qin attacked Jin.” Third year of Duke Wen.
Liu Dalun.
Comment by Associate Examiner Peng, Assistant Instructor: Writers merely know to speak of demanding perfection, without grasping the underlying intention of that demand. They often simply copy out the commentary, making their work tiresome to read. This essay understands the matter: it traces Duke Mu of Qin’s admirable qualities from beginning to end in order to elucidate the Sage’s intention in demanding perfection. Its author must be deeply versed in this Classic; for this reason, I have selected it for inclusion.

穆伐晉一役爲全德之累也春秋備責之者豈
非論其人哉且晉之伐何爲乎秦穆公懷三戰
三北之耻而有是舉耳先之以濟河焚舟之誓
而志在必遂繼之以王官及郊之取而怒猶未
�King及晉人畏其勢避其鋒然後自茅津而濟封
===
殽尸而還焉春秋貶而稱人說者曰責備賢者
何歟觀大易損卦之象則知忿慾之在人克之
足以脩其德反之有以成其過也春秋諸侯求
其過而悔悔而改而能進於德者穆公其庶乎
自其始而論之殽函見敗之後歸作誓書追咎
共門之計宜若過而知悔有脩德之機矣然悔
不終悔尋有今日之伐寧不負初心邪自其終
而論之新城被圍之後力踐誓言遂絕東侵之
念宜若悔而能改有脩德之實矣然改□□遂改

考試官學正周批：繳書法，甚有生意。

春秋於强國報怨，必原其賢而責之備焉。此秦穆伐晉一役，爲全德之累也。春秋備責之者，豈非論其人哉？且晉之伐何爲乎？秦穆公懷三戰三北之耻，而有是舉耳。先之以濟河焚舟之誓，而志在必遂；繼之以王官及郊之取，而怒猶未�King。及晉人畏其勢，避其鋒，然後自茅津而濟，封殽尸而還焉。春秋貶而稱人，說者曰：「責備賢者。」何歟？觀大易損卦之象，則知忿慾之在人，克之足以脩其德，反之有以成其過也。春秋諸侯，求其過而悔、悔而改，而能進於德者，穆公其庶乎？自其始而論之，殽函見敗之後，歸作誓書，追咎共門之計，宜若過而知悔，有脩德之機矣。然悔不終悔，尋有今日之伐，寧不負初心邪？自其終而論之，新城被圍之後，力踐誓言，遂絕東侵之念，宜若悔而能改，有脩德之實矣。然改□□遂改
translation_en:
Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: “Tracing the beginning and examining the outcome, weaving them together into a composition—this is how it should be written.”

Examiner Zhou, Instructor, comments: “The concluding treatment of the annalistic wording is especially lively.”

When the Spring and Autumn Annals treats a powerful state's requital of a grievance, it invariably considers the ruler's worthiness and demands perfection of him. This campaign in which Duke Mu of Qin attacked Jin was a blemish upon his otherwise complete virtue. Was it not in consideration of the man himself that the Spring and Autumn Annals demanded perfection of him? Moreover, why did he attack Jin? Duke Mu of Qin undertook this action simply because he harbored shame over three battles and three defeats. First came his oath as he crossed the Yellow River and burned his boats, his resolve fixed upon success; next came his capture of Wangguan and Jiao, yet his anger had still not [subsided?; text corrupt]. Only when the people of Jin feared his might and avoided the edge of his attack did he cross at Maojin, raise burial mounds over the dead at Yao, and return. The Spring and Autumn Annals demeans him by calling him merely a “man.” Commentators say: “It demands perfection of the worthy.” Why is this?

Looking at the Image commentary on the hexagram Decrease in the great Book of Changes, we understand that overcoming the anger and desires within a person suffices to cultivate his virtue, while doing the reverse brings his faults to fruition. Among the feudal lords of the Spring and Autumn period, if we seek one who regretted his faults, reformed through regret, and thereby advanced in virtue, did Duke Mu not come close? Considering his beginnings, after his defeat at Yao and Han, he returned and composed the Oath, retrospectively blaming the plan concerning Gongmen [?]. It would seem that he recognized his fault and regretted it, possessing the beginnings of moral cultivation. Yet his regret did not endure: before long there was the attack now under discussion. Did this not betray his original intention?

Considering his eventual conduct, after Xincheng was besieged, he earnestly fulfilled his oath and finally abandoned the thought of invading eastward. It would seem that he could reform through regret and had achieved genuine moral cultivation. Yet his reform □□ carried through reform [?]…

title: 正德十一年陝西鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭李　批　原始要終錯綜成文當
如此作
考試官學正周　批　繳書法甚有生意
春秋於强國報怨必原其賢而責之備焉此秦
穆伐晉一役爲全德之累也春秋備責之者豈
非論其人哉且晉之伐何爲乎秦穆公懷三戰
三北之耻而有是舉耳先之以濟河焚舟之誓
而志在必逞繼之以王官及郊之取而怒猶未
饜及晉人畏其勢避其鋒然後自茅津而濟封
===
殽尸而還焉春秋貶而稱人說者曰責備賢者
何歟觀大易損卦之象則知忿慾之在人克之
足以脩其德反之有以成其過也春秋諸侯求
其過而悔悔而改而能進於德者穆公其庶乎
自其始而論之殽函見敗之後歸作誓書追咎
北門之計宜若過而知悔有脩德之機矣然悔
不終悔尋有今日之伐寧不負初心邪自其終
而論之新城被圍之後力踐誓言遂絕東侵之
念宜若悔而能改有脩德之實矣然改不遠改
punctuated:
考試官教諭李批：原始要終，錯綜成文，當如此作。

考試官學正周批：繳書法甚有生意。

春秋於强國報怨，必原其賢而責之備焉。此秦穆伐晉一役，爲全德之累也。春秋備責之者，豈非論其人哉？且晉之伐，何爲乎？秦穆公懷三戰三北之耻，而有是舉耳。先之以濟河焚舟之誓，而志在必逞；繼之以王官及郊之取，而怒猶未饜。及晉人畏其勢，避其鋒，然後自茅津而濟，封殽尸而還焉。春秋貶而稱人，說者曰：「責備賢者。」何歟？觀大易損卦之象，則知忿慾之在人，克之足以脩其德，反之有以成其過也。春秋諸侯，求其過而悔，悔而改，而能進於德者，穆公其庶乎！自其始而論之，殽函見敗之後，歸作誓書，追咎北門之計，宜若過而知悔，有脩德之機矣。然悔不終悔，尋有今日之伐，寧不負初心邪？自其終而論之，新城被圍之後，力踐誓言，遂絕東侵之念，宜若悔而能改，有脩德之實矣。然改不遠改
translation_en:
Comment by Examiner Li, an Instructor: “Tracing the beginning and examining the end, weaving these together into a composition—this is how it should be written.”

Comment by Examiner Zhou, a School Director: “The way the conclusion draws together the wording of the classic is especially lively.”

When a powerful state avenges a grievance, the Spring and Autumn Annals invariably considers the ruler’s worthiness and demands perfection of him. This campaign in which Duke Mu of Qin attacked Jin was a blemish upon his otherwise complete virtue. Was it not because of its assessment of the man himself that the Spring and Autumn Annals demanded perfection of him? Moreover, why did he attack Jin? Duke Mu of Qin undertook this campaign simply because he harbored shame over three defeats in three battles. First came his oath upon crossing the Yellow River and burning his boats: he was determined to have his way. Next came the capture of Wangguan and Jiao, yet his anger was still unsatisfied. Only when the men of Jin, fearing his power, avoided the edge of his attack did he cross at Maojin, heap earth over the corpses at Yao, and return. The Spring and Autumn Annals demotes him by calling him merely a “man.” Commentators say: “It demands perfection of the worthy.” Why is this?

Looking at the Image of the hexagram Decrease in the great Book of Changes, we learn that overcoming the anger and desires within oneself suffices to cultivate virtue, whereas the reverse brings one’s faults to fruition. Among the feudal lords of the Spring and Autumn period, who sought out their faults and repented, then reformed and advanced in virtue? Duke Mu perhaps came close! Considering his conduct from the beginning: after his defeat at Yaohan, he returned and composed an oath, retrospectively finding fault with the plan concerning the northern gate. It would seem that he knew to repent of his error and thus had an opportunity to cultivate virtue. Yet his repentance did not endure, and before long came the campaign under discussion. Did this not betray his original intention? Considering his conduct at the end: after Xincheng was besieged, he earnestly fulfilled his oath and abandoned all thought of invading eastward. It would seem that he could reform after repenting and had actually cultivated virtue. Yet his reform did not extend far [?]…

title: 正德十一年陝西鄉試錄
text:
必有今日之伐豈得爲盡善邪以玆役一事之
非爲始終全德之累是猶連抱之材而有寸朽
連城之璧而掩微瑕不亦深可惜哉聖人脩經
至此將以常情待之歟而其素行也可取將以
自棄絕之歟而其晚節也可稱原始要終誠賢
君也以賢君而爲此可不備責之乎故貶而人
之以此所以然者無非欲其亟於改過而爲全
德之君也望之深者責之備其是之謂夫抑仲
虺告成湯不稱其無過而稱其改過可見王者
===
不以過爲嫌而以改爲貴也太甲之覆典刑成
王之惑流言非不有過矣然怨艾以聽伊尹之
訓感悟而迎周公以歸卒成王德爲商周令主
改過之功豈不大哉此穆公之所以爲賢也此
春秋之所以責備也此秦誓之所以附於四代
之書也
禮記
爲人君者謹其所好惡而已矣
王準
punctuated:
必有今日之伐，豈得爲盡善邪？以玆役一事之非，爲始終全德之累，是猶連抱之材而有寸朽，連城之璧而掩微瑕，不亦深可惜哉！聖人脩經至此，將以常情待之歟？而其素行也可取。將以自棄絕之歟？而其晚節也可稱。原始要終，誠賢君也。以賢君而爲此，可不備責之乎？故貶而人之以此。所以然者，無非欲其亟於改過而爲全德之君也。望之深者責之備，其是之謂夫！抑仲虺告成湯，不稱其無過而稱其改過，可見王者不以過爲嫌，而以改爲貴也。太甲之覆典刑，成王之惑流言，非不有過矣。然怨艾以聽伊尹之訓，感悟而迎周公以歸，卒成王德，爲商周令主，改過之功豈不大哉！此穆公之所以爲賢也，此春秋之所以責備也，此秦誓之所以附於四代之書也。

禮記
爲人君者，謹其所好惡而已矣。
王準
translation_en:
…there was nevertheless this present attack: how could his conduct be considered wholly good? To let the fault of this single campaign blemish the integrity of his virtue over his entire life is like a timber many armspans in girth containing an inch of rot, or a jade disk worth several cities concealing a slight flaw. Is this not deeply regrettable? When the Sage reached this point in compiling the Classic, was he to judge him by ordinary standards? Yet his customary conduct was worthy of approval. Was he to reject him as one who had abandoned himself? Yet his conduct in later life deserved praise. Considering his beginning and examining his end, he was truly a worthy ruler. For a worthy ruler to act thus—could one fail to hold him fully accountable? Thus, on this occasion, the Sage demoted him by referring to him merely as a “man.” His reason was simply that he wished him to hasten to correct his faults and become a ruler of complete virtue. The deeper one's expectations of someone, the more exacting one's demands: surely this is what the saying means!

Moreover, when Zhonghui admonished Cheng Tang, he praised him not for being without faults but for correcting them. This shows that a king does not regard having faults as a disgrace, but prizes their correction. Taijia overturned established norms, and King Cheng was misled by rumors: neither was without fault. Yet the former reproached himself and heeded Yi Yin's instruction, while the latter came to his senses and welcomed the Duke of Zhou back. In the end, they perfected their kingly virtue and became excellent rulers of Shang and Zhou. Was not the achievement of correcting their faults great indeed? This is why Duke Mu was deemed worthy; this is why the Spring and Autumn Annals held him to the fullest standard; and this is why the “Oath of Qin” was appended to the documents of the four dynasties.

Book of Rites
“All that one who rules others need do is be careful about what he likes and dislikes.”
Wang Zhun

title: 正德十一年陝西鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭李　批　謹好惡字提掇精采是
能斟酌輕重者可取
考試官學正周　批　題意自明白但士子筆
粗氣猛一直寫去殊無啓發人意處求其婉
曲詳盡能會子夏當時規戒之意者無踰此
篇宜錄之以爲讀禮者式
居臨下之位愼感下之機賢者告時君然也蓋
音之邪正最易感人也然則人君之好惡可不
致其謹乎昔子夏因魏文侯厭古樂而好新樂
===
故告之及此意謂感化之邪正雖繫於樂音好
惡之公私實由於君上故爲人君者統馭四方
匪崇高以爲樂也而臣民之觀法攸存主宰萬
姓匪富貴以爲榮也而風俗之轉移攸繫以一
心而應萬事宜乎無所不謹矣必于其先者而
是務焉以一身而萃百責宜乎無所不愼矣必
于其要者而是圖焉其要維何謹好惡而已矣
誠以德音之正在所當好也一或不謹則鑒別
失精從而惡之者有矣溺音之邪在所當惡也
punctuated:
考試官教諭李批：「謹好惡字，提掇精采，是能斟酌輕重者，可取。」

考試官學正周批：「題意自明白，但士子筆粗氣猛，一直寫去，殊無啓發人意處。求其婉曲詳盡，能會子夏當時規戒之意者，無踰此篇，宜錄之以爲讀禮者式。」

居臨下之位，愼感下之機，賢者告時君然也。蓋音之邪正，最易感人也。然則人君之好惡，可不致其謹乎？昔子夏因魏文侯厭古樂而好新樂，故告之及此。意謂感化之邪正，雖繫於樂音，好惡之公私，實由於君上。故爲人君者，統馭四方，匪崇高以爲樂也，而臣民之觀法攸存；主宰萬姓，匪富貴以爲榮也，而風俗之轉移攸繫。以一心而應萬事，宜乎無所不謹矣，必于其先者而是務焉；以一身而萃百責，宜乎無所不愼矣，必于其要者而是圖焉。其要維何？謹好惡而已矣。誠以德音之正，在所當好也，一或不謹，則鑒別失精，從而惡之者有矣；溺音之邪，在所當惡也。
translation_en:
Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: “The handling of the words ‘be careful in one's likes and dislikes’ is excellent. This writer knows how to weigh the relative importance of things; the essay merits acceptance.”

Examiner Zhou, School Director, comments: “The meaning of the topic is clear enough in itself, but candidates write with coarse strokes and excessive force, pressing straight ahead without anything that illuminates the reader’s understanding. For subtlety and thoroughness, and for grasping the admonitory intent of Zixia’s words at the time, no essay surpasses this one. It should be included as a model for readers of the Book of Rites.”
