Occupying a position above others, one must attend carefully to the means by which one influences those below: such was the worthy man's counsel to the ruler of his day. For music, whether perverse or upright, most readily moves people. Can a ruler, then, fail to exercise the utmost care in his likes and dislikes? Formerly, because Marquis Wen of Wei disliked ancient music and preferred the new music, Zixia addressed this admonition to him. His meaning was that, although whether the transforming influence is perverse or upright depends upon the music, whether likes and dislikes are impartial or selfish ultimately depends upon the ruler. Thus, one who rules over the four quarters does not take pleasure merely in his exalted position: he is the one whom officials and people look to as their model. In presiding over the myriad families, he does not take pride merely in wealth and rank: upon him depends the transformation of customs. With one mind responding to myriad affairs, he surely ought to exercise care in everything; yet he must devote himself to what comes first. With a hundred responsibilities concentrated in his single person, he surely ought to exercise caution in everything; yet he must attend to what is essential. What is essential? Simply to be careful in his likes and dislikes. Indeed, the upright character of virtuous music makes it something that ought to be liked. Should he once fail to exercise care, his discrimination will lose its precision, and he may consequently come to dislike it. The perversity of corrupting music makes it something that ought to be disliked …

title: 正德十一年陝西鄉試錄
text:
少有不慎則取舍靡定從而好之者有矣要必
審察於情動之時明辨於樂作之際有所好焉
必擇其何者爲古何者爲新惟古樂可以脩身
而及人好斯隨之不可妄有所好以亂吾之聰
明有所惡焉必擇其何者爲溺何者爲德惟溺
音有以淫色而害德惡斯從之不可妄有所惡
以壞吾之心術審聲審音務使順吾情而悅聽
者允合乎義理之公審音審樂務俾排吾性而
厭聞者不同乎流俗之弊夫如是則本原之地
===
以端感應之機不忒謂之而已矣者以見人君
之道無過於此也今文侯聽古樂則惟恐臥聽
鄭衛之音則不知倦是好惡俱失其正而不自
知矣謂之何哉抑嘗因是而深爲文侯惜也春
秋之時去古未遠猶及見先王之樂文侯春秋
之賢君也使于此而知所好則魏其庶幾矣夫
何惑於鄭衛之音而不悟哉幸其本心之明猶
未盡蔽故對舉而怪問之似若有未安於心者
此治亂之一大幾也後世雖欲復古而先王之
punctuated:
少有不慎，則取舍靡定，從而好之者有矣。要必審察於情動之時，明辨於樂作之際。有所好焉，必擇其何者爲古，何者爲新；惟古樂可以脩身而及人，好斯隨之，不可妄有所好，以亂吾之聰明。有所惡焉，必擇其何者爲溺，何者爲德；惟溺音有以淫色而害德，惡斯從之，不可妄有所惡，以壞吾之心術。審聲審音，務使順吾情而悅聽者允合乎義理之公；審音審樂，務俾排吾性而厭聞者不同乎流俗之弊。夫如是，則本原之地以端，感應之機不忒。謂之「而已矣」者，以見人君之道無過於此也。
今文侯聽古樂則惟恐臥，聽鄭衛之音則不知倦，是好惡俱失其正而不自知矣，謂之何哉？抑嘗因是而深爲文侯惜也。春秋之時，去古未遠，猶及見先王之樂。文侯，春秋之賢君也，使于此而知所好，則魏其庶幾矣。夫何惑於鄭衛之音而不悟哉？幸其本心之明猶未盡蔽，故對舉而怪問之，似若有未安於心者。此治亂之一大幾也。後世雖欲復古，而先王之
translation_en:
…With even a little carelessness, one’s choices become unsettled, and one may consequently come to delight in it. One must therefore scrutinize the moment when feelings are stirred and distinguish clearly when music begins. When delighting in something, one must distinguish which music is ancient and which is new. Only ancient music can cultivate oneself and extend its influence to others; delight should follow accordingly. One must not delight indiscriminately and thereby confuse one’s hearing and understanding. When disliking something, one must distinguish which sounds are corrupting and which are virtuous. Only corrupting sounds incite sensual indulgence and injure virtue; dislike should follow accordingly. One must not dislike indiscriminately and thereby damage the workings of one’s heart. In examining sounds and musical tones, one must ensure that what accords with one’s feelings and pleases the ear truly conforms to impartial moral principle. In examining musical tones and music, one must ensure that what runs counter to one’s nature and is unwelcome to the ear does not share the defects of vulgar fashions. In this way, the foundation is set right [?], and the workings of stimulus and response do not err. The words “and that is all” show that the way of the ruler consists in nothing beyond this.
Now, when Marquis Wen listens to ancient music, he fears falling asleep, yet when he listens to the music of Zheng and Wei, he knows no weariness. Thus both his likes and his dislikes have departed from what is right, without his realizing it. What can one say of this? Indeed, this has often led me to feel profound regret for Marquis Wen. During the Spring and Autumn period, antiquity was not yet far distant, and one could still encounter the music of the former kings. Marquis Wen was a worthy ruler of the Spring and Autumn period. Had he known what to delight in in this matter, Wei might have come close to the ideal. Why, then, was he beguiled by the music of Zheng and Wei and unable to awaken to his error? Fortunately, the clarity of his original heart was not yet wholly obscured. Thus he juxtaposed the two kinds of music and asked about them in perplexity, seemingly still feeling some unease in his heart. This is a crucial turning point between good order and disorder. In later ages, even if people wished to restore antiquity, the former kings’ …

title: 正德十一年陝西鄉試錄
text:
樂澌滅已盡則有志者孰從而考哉噫此所以
深爲文佚惜也
故射者進退周還必中禮內志正外體直
然後持弓矢審固持弓矢審固然後可以
言中此可以觀德行矣
李宗樞
考試官教諭李　批〔辭氣清潤法度整飭之令人可愛〕
考試官學正周　批〔士子於中禮觀德處多體認不眞故文字輒繆此作見理精明發揮透徹必深於禮者錄之〕
===
記者論射原其所以中乎的著其可以驗乎賢
蓋射以觀德也然則射者致謹而後能中的寧
不可以驗其賢哉記射義者其旨如此且古者
諸侯之射也必先行燕禮以明君臣之義卿大
夫士之射也必先行鄉飲酒禮以明長幼之序
然於將射之時一進退也或及階及物秩然升
降之有節於禮乎何爭一周還也或取矢挾矢
punctuated:
樂澌滅已盡，則有志者孰從而考哉？噫！此所以深爲文佚惜也。

故射者進退周還必中禮，內志正，外體直，然後持弓矢審固。持弓矢審固，然後可以言中。此可以觀德行矣。

李宗樞

考試官教諭李，批〔辭氣清潤，法度整飭之，令人可愛。〕

考試官學正周，批〔士子於中禮觀德處，多體認不眞，故文字輒繆。此作見理精明，發揮透徹，必深於禮者，錄之。〕

記者論射，原其所以中乎的，著其可以驗乎賢。蓋射以觀德也，然則射者致謹而後能中的，寧不可以驗其賢哉？記射義者，其旨如此。且古者，諸侯之射也，必先行燕禮，以明君臣之義；卿大夫士之射也，必先行鄉飲酒禮，以明長幼之序。然於將射之時，一進退也，或及階及物，秩然升降之有節，於禮乎何爭？一周還也，或取矢挾矢，
translation_en:
…the music of the former kings has utterly vanished; where, then, can those intent on restoring it turn to investigate it? Alas! This is why one so deeply regrets the missed opportunity of Wen Yi [?; apparently Marquis Wen].

“Thus, in archery, advancing, withdrawing, and turning must all accord with ritual. The intention within must be correct and the body without upright; only then can one hold the bow and arrows carefully and firmly. Only after holding the bow and arrows carefully and firmly can one speak of hitting the target. Through this, one may observe virtue and conduct.”

Li Zongshu

Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: 〔The language and tone are clear and polished, and the composition is orderly and disciplined [?], making it delightful.〕

Examiner Zhou, Instructor, comments: 〔Candidates often fail to grasp truly the points about conforming to ritual and observing virtue, so their writing repeatedly goes astray. This composition perceives the principles clearly and incisively and expounds them thoroughly. Its author must have a profound understanding of ritual. I select it for inclusion.〕

In discussing archery, the recorder traces the grounds for hitting the target and makes clear how archery can attest to a person's worthiness. For archery serves to reveal virtue. If archers can hit the target only after exercising the utmost care, surely this can attest to their worthiness? Such is the purport of the author of “The Meaning of Archery.” In antiquity, when the feudal lords held an archery ceremony, they invariably first performed the banquet ritual to make clear the proper relationship between ruler and minister. When ministers, grandees, and servicemen held an archery ceremony, they invariably first performed the district drinking ceremony to make clear the order between elder and younger. Now, just before shooting, each advance and withdrawal—whether approaching the steps or the designated shooting position—involves an orderly ascent or descent with due measure. What contention could there be within such ritual? Each turn—whether taking up arrows or holding them at one's side…

title: 正德十一年陝西鄉試錄
text:
肅然揖讓之有容於禮乎何繆然主於內者愚
也必靜專自守而心無雜念可謂正矣動於外
者體也必戰兢自持而身無惰容可謂直矣夫
志體之內外既正而直然後執我弓矢以運夫
目力之巧必詳審而無遺持我弓矢以決夫膂
力之强必堅固而不拔巧力有不全乎弓矢之
執持既審而固然後彎弓而射則發彼有的而
可以不失其正循聲而發則舍矢如破而可以
不失其鵠正鵠有不中乎夫射者之所以中的
===
如此果何以觀德行哉蓋習燕禮於無事之時
而君臣之德行以立習鄉飲於燕安之日而長
幼之德行以脩令於大射而能中焉則夫君臣
之義諸侯得於心而見於事者可於是而驗之
矣於鄉射而能中焉則凡長幼之序卿大夫士
有諸中而形諸外者可於此而見之矣是則射
雖一藝之小而所關甚大如此聖人務焉豈無
意哉抑考弧矢之利以威天下聖人制射之初
意也又慮夫天下後世徒知尚勇力其弊必至
punctuated: 肅然揖讓之有容，於禮乎何繆？然主於內者愚也，必靜專自守，而心無雜念，可謂正矣；動於外者體也，必戰兢自持，而身無惰容，可謂直矣。夫志體之內外既正而直，然後執我弓矢，以運夫目力之巧，必詳審而無遺；持我弓矢，以決夫膂力之强，必堅固而不拔。巧力有不全乎？弓矢之執持既審而固，然後彎弓而射，則發彼有的，而可以不失其正；循聲而發，則舍矢如破，而可以不失其鵠。正鵠有不中乎？夫射者之所以中的如此，果何以觀德行哉？蓋習燕禮於無事之時，而君臣之德行以立；習鄉飲於燕安之日，而長幼之德行以脩。令於大射而能中焉，則夫君臣之義，諸侯得於心而見於事者，可於是而驗之矣；於鄉射而能中焉，則凡長幼之序，卿大夫士有諸中而形諸外者，可於此而見之矣。是則射雖一藝之小，而所關甚大如此，聖人務焉，豈無意哉？抑考弧矢之利以威天下，聖人制射之初意也。又慮夫天下後世徒知尚勇力，其弊必至
translation_en:
…with solemn composure in bowing and yielding precedence: how could this deviate from ritual propriety? Yet what governs within is the will [?; the transcription reads 愚, “folly”]. One must maintain inward stillness and concentration, keeping the mind free of distracting thoughts; this may be called correctness. What moves externally is the body. One must hold oneself with vigilant care, allowing no slackness in one’s bearing; this may be called uprightness. Once the will within and the body without are correct and upright, one takes up bow and arrows to exercise the skill of one’s eyesight, examining everything carefully and overlooking nothing. One holds bow and arrows to bring the strength of one’s arms and back to bear, remaining firm and unshakable. Could skill and strength then be anything less than complete? Once one’s grasp of bow and arrows is precise and firm, one draws the bow and shoots. The arrow has a definite mark, and one can avoid missing the target’s center. Releasing in accordance with the musical beat, one sends the arrow forth as though piercing the target, and can avoid missing the bull’s-eye. How could one fail to hit the center? Such is the means by which an archer hits the mark. But how, in fact, does this reveal virtuous conduct?

By practicing the ceremonial banquet in times free from affairs, the virtuous conduct proper to ruler and minister is established. By practicing the village drinking ceremony in days of peace and ease, the virtuous conduct proper to elders and juniors is cultivated. Now [?], if one can hit the mark at the great archery ceremony, the right relationship between ruler and minister—which the feudal lords apprehend inwardly and manifest in their actions—can thereby be verified. If one can hit the mark at the village archery ceremony, the ordering of elders and juniors—which ministers, grandees, and gentlemen possess within and express outwardly—can thereby be seen. Thus, although archery is merely one minor art, its implications are so great. Could the sages have devoted themselves to it without purpose?

Furthermore, examining the advantages of bow and arrow as a means of overawing all under Heaven, we find the sages’ original intention in instituting archery. Yet they also feared that later generations throughout the realm would know only to esteem courage and strength, and that the resulting abuses would inevitably lead to…

title: 正德十一年陝西鄉試錄
text:
於喪德故因而飾之以禮樂以養人於無事之
時使之盡志於射以立其德行而觀德選士率
不外此柰何後世教衰禮樂廢壞遂專爲武夫
之小技可勝嘆哉
第貳場
論
有子達禮樂之本
劉序
同考試官教諭陳　批　近時士子作論往往掇
拾陳語以自奇杜撰隱語以自古而論體幾壞
矣是作立意精遠引據該切且步驟舂容詞氣
鏗鏘殆乎朝祀之行韶濩之奏也見之者自
傚神會心駭矣得士如此良以自慶
同考試官教諭王　批　論場涉禮樂處動便
數百言殊無愜人意者晚得是卷力去陳言
盡脫俗調可謂禮之無體樂之無聲者矣他
日效用禮樂不其有賴乎鄉闈首選固無以易
子矣
punctuated:
於喪德，故因而飾之以禮樂，以養人於無事之時，使之盡志於射，以立其德行，而觀德選士率不外此。柰何後世教衰，禮樂廢壞，遂專爲武夫之小技，可勝嘆哉！

第貳場

論

有子達禮樂之本

劉序

同考試官教諭陳批：近時士子作論，往往掇拾陳語以自奇，杜撰隱語以自古，而論體幾壞矣。是作立意精遠，引據該切，且步驟舂容，詞氣鏗鏘，殆乎朝祀之行、韶濩之奏也。見之者自傚神會心駭矣。得士如此，良以自慶。

同考試官教諭王批：論場涉禮樂處，動便數百言，殊無愜人意者。晚得是卷，力去陳言，盡脫俗調，可謂禮之無體、樂之無聲者矣。他日效用，禮樂不其有賴乎？鄉闈首選，固無以易子矣。
translation_en:
…to the loss of virtue. Thus they embellished archery with rites and music to nurture people in times free from affairs, making them devote their minds fully to archery and thereby establish their virtuous conduct. Observing virtue and selecting worthy men alike generally proceeded through this practice. Alas, in later ages instruction declined, rites and music fell into disuse and ruin, and archery became merely a petty skill of fighting men. How could one lament this enough!

Second Session

Discourse

Youzi Understood the Foundations of Rites and Music

Liu Xu

Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: Recently, candidates writing discourses have often gathered stale expressions to make themselves appear original and fabricated obscure phrases to make themselves appear ancient, so that the discourse form has almost been ruined. This work is subtle and far-reaching in conception, comprehensive and apt in its supporting citations. Moreover, its progression is unhurried and measured, its language and cadence resonant—almost like the performance of court sacrifices or the playing of the Shao and Huo music. Those who encounter it naturally emulate it, grasp its spirit, and are astonished at heart [?]. To have found a scholar like this is truly cause for congratulating myself.

Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor: In the discourse session, passages touching on rites and music readily run to several hundred words, yet scarcely any are satisfying. Late in the proceedings I obtained this script, which vigorously casts off stale expressions and entirely escapes conventional tones. It may be called rites without outward form and music without sound. When he enters service in the future, will not rites and music have someone on whom to rely? For first selection in the Provincial Examination, there is certainly no one who could replace you.

title: 正德十一年陝西鄉試錄
text:
考試官教諭李　批　議論嚴整讀之令人起
敬佳士也錄之以式來學
考試官學正周　批　近日論體多失之卑弱
是作立意高古措詞雄健迥異衆作可愛可
愛
道非止於文也聖人以文教天下而天下
以文觀聖人道於是乎病矣故君子揭其
本以授之夫本其起于心乎道之本起於
心而弗能弗散於事夫其弗能弗散于事
===
也於是乎有文焉夫其本起于心也則固
弗止於文矣是故有度數之文而禮制焉
有聲音之文而樂作焉其本于心一也聖
人以心教天下而假之乎文其流也徒習
其文而遺其心爲吾道病君子始揭其本
以授之曰度數非禮也聲容非樂也其于
心乎心主於敬而用以和䧟不讓之禮無
聲之樂矣由是天下之人咸知道非止於
文也謂度數聲音之不足爲禮樂也將不
punctuated:
考試官教諭李批：議論嚴整，讀之令人起敬，佳士也。錄之以式來學。

考試官學正周批：近日論體多失之卑弱，是作立意高古，措詞雄健，迥異衆作，可愛，可愛！

道非止於文也。聖人以文教天下，而天下以文觀聖人，道於是乎病矣。故君子揭其本以授之。夫本其起于心乎？道之本起於心，而弗能弗散於事。夫其弗能弗散于事也，於是乎有文焉。夫其本起于心也，則固弗止於文矣。是故有度數之文而禮制焉，有聲音之文而樂作焉，其本于心一也。聖人以心教天下，而假之乎文。其流也，徒習其文而遺其心，爲吾道病。君子始揭其本以授之，曰：「度數非禮也，聲容非樂也，其于心乎？心主於敬而用以和，䧟不讓之禮、無聲之樂矣。」由是天下之人咸知道非止於文也。謂度數聲音之不足爲禮樂也，將不
translation_en:
Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: “The argument is rigorous and well ordered; reading it inspires respect. This is an outstanding scholar. We record his work as a model for future students.”

Examiner Zhou, School Instructor, comments: “Recent discourses have often suffered from a low and feeble style. This composition is lofty and antique in conception, vigorous and robust in expression, and markedly different from the other submissions. Admirable, admirable!”

The Way does not reside solely in outward forms. The sages taught the world through forms, but the people of the world judged the sages by those forms, and thus the Way suffered. Therefore the gentleman discloses its root and teaches it to them. Does not that root arise in the heart? The root of the Way arises in the heart, yet it cannot but extend into affairs. Because it necessarily extends into affairs, forms come into being. Since its root arises in the heart, it assuredly does not reside solely in forms. Thus, through the forms of prescribed measures and numbers, ritual is established; through the forms of sounds and tones, music is created. They are alike in being rooted in the heart. The sages teach the world through the heart, lending expression to it through forms. In the subsequent transmission, people merely practice the forms and neglect the heart, bringing harm to our Way. The gentleman then discloses its root and teaches it to them, saying: “Measures and numbers are not ritual; sounds and outward bearing are not music. Does not their root lie in the heart? The heart takes reverence as its governing principle and expresses itself in harmony: [the text is doubtful here] ritual without yielding precedence [?], and music without sound.” From this, all the people of the world understand that the Way does not reside solely in forms. Recognizing that measures, numbers, sounds, and tones are insufficient to constitute ritual and music, will they not …

title: 正德十一年陝西鄉試錄
text:
進進焉以求於文之外與先儒范氏曰有
子達禮樂之本愚謂有子之達其以天下
爲達也乎蓋嘗考之唐虞以上其禮制不
可知矣在春秋時夏則有夏時焉商則有
坤乾焉而杞宋莫徵惟周禮僅存於魯而
君臣交僭都城違制郊禘吶經暨于軍師
蒐狩之典昏覲朝宴之儀漸失其舊孔子
備書示譏而歎其不足觀矣至於樂之廢
墜尤有甚焉幸而僅存者惟舜之大韶周
之大武然且殘缺其稽音律歌詞多失其
序而軒宮之秩佾舞之數諸置錯陳孔子
雖嘗正之而所可知者惟翕純皦繹之節
耳然則禮樂之在當時豈特本之則無而
已哉將并其文而漸盡矣記曰無本不立
無文不行有子之達何獨遺其文而專於
其本哉蓋曰究其文而遺其本卽使盡復
上古之度數聲音固無補於禮樂之散失
也探其本而略其文則所謂制度聲音者
punctuated: 進進焉，以求於文之外與？先儒范氏曰：「有子達禮樂之本。」愚謂有子之達，其以天下爲達也乎？蓋嘗考之，唐虞以上，其禮制不可知矣。在春秋時，夏則有夏時焉，商則有坤乾焉，而杞宋莫徵。惟周禮僅存於魯，而君臣交僭，都城違制，郊禘吶經，暨于軍師蒐狩之典、昏覲朝宴之儀，漸失其舊。孔子備書示譏，而歎其不足觀矣。至於樂之廢墜，尤有甚焉。幸而僅存者，惟舜之大韶、周之大武，然且殘缺，其稽音律歌詞，多失其序，而軒宮之秩、佾舞之數，諸置錯陳。孔子雖嘗正之，而所可知者，惟翕純皦繹之節耳。然則禮樂之在當時，豈特本之則無而已哉？將并其文而漸盡矣。記曰：「無本不立，無文不行。」有子之達，何獨遺其文而專於其本哉？蓋曰究其文而遺其本，卽使盡復上古之度數聲音，固無補於禮樂之散失也。探其本而略其文，則所謂制度聲音者
translation_en:
…press ever further onward, seeking beyond outward forms? The earlier Confucian scholar Fan said, “Youzi understood the foundation of ritual and music.” In my humble view, did Youzi’s understanding not aim to bring understanding to all under Heaven? I have examined the matter: the ritual institutions of the ages of Tang and Yu and earlier can no longer be known. During the Spring and Autumn period, the Xia calendar survived from the Xia, and Kun and Qian survived from the Shang; yet neither Qi nor Song could furnish corroborating evidence. Only the rituals of Zhou still barely survived in Lu. Yet rulers and ministers alike usurped ceremonial prerogatives, city walls transgressed prescribed dimensions, and the suburban and di sacrifices departed from canonical norms [?]. Even the regulations for military forces and seasonal hunts, and the ceremonies of marriage, court audiences, and banquets, gradually lost their ancient forms. Confucius recorded these matters fully to convey his censure, and lamented that they were no longer worth observing.

The abandonment and decline of music were even more severe. All that fortunately still barely survived were Shun’s Great Shao and Zhou’s Great Wu. Yet even these were fragmentary: their musical pitches and song texts, when examined [?], had largely lost their proper order, while the arrangement of suspended instruments [?] and the prescribed numbers of dance rows were confused and misplaced [?]. Although Confucius once corrected them, what could still be known was only the progression of the music: its opening together, its harmony, its distinctness, and its continuity. Thus, as ritual and music existed at that time, was it merely their foundation that was absent? Even their outward forms were gradually disappearing.

The Record of Rites says, “Without a foundation, nothing can be established; without outward forms, nothing can be practiced.” Why, then, would Youzi’s understanding disregard outward forms and concentrate exclusively on their foundation? His point was surely this: if one investigates outward forms but neglects their foundation, even completely restoring the measures, numbers, sounds, and tones of high antiquity would do nothing to remedy the disintegration and loss of ritual and music. If one seeks their foundation while giving less attention to their outward forms, then what are called institutions, regulations, sounds, and tones…

title: 正德十一年陝西鄉試錄
text:
雖不可考吾將以義起之此有子之所以
爲達歟故其言曰禮之用和爲貴于以見
禮主于敬而不以敬拘也又曰不以禮節
之亦不可行于以見樂貴于和而不以和蕩
也敬不徒敬而拘必濟以和和不徒和而
蕩必反于敬禮樂其有興乎是故婚冠以
肅于家射飲以振于鄉朝遇會聘以序于
邦國邑圭羔鴈以贄敦璉瑚簋以禮豆介
牢席殽胾醢醢以供賓燕秩秩然井井然
===
謂之禮可也敬弗立于心焉雖不謂之禮
可也二南以歌于房雅以賦于朝廷頌以
奏于廟鍾鼓管磬以宣其聲羽旄綴兆以
狀其容咏嘆淫泆發揚蹈厲以象其功德
陶陶然怡怡然謂之樂可也和弗生于心
焉雖不謂之樂可也聖人以心教天下而
天下不能以聖人之心爲心於是乎假之
乎文故習其文者亦求其心而已矣存其
誠謹其幾神其用欽以承天輿輿以奉親
punctuated: 雖不可考，吾將以義起之。此有子之所以爲達歟？故其言曰：「禮之用，和爲貴。」于以見禮主于敬，而不以敬拘也。又曰：「不以禮節之，亦不可行。」于以見樂貴于和，而不以和蕩也。敬不徒敬而拘，必濟以和；和不徒和而蕩，必反于敬。禮樂其有興乎？是故婚冠以肅于家，射飲以振于鄉，朝遇會聘以序于邦國，邑圭羔鴈以贄，敦璉瑚簋以禮，豆介牢席、殽胾醢醢以供賓燕，秩秩然，井井然，謂之禮可也。敬弗立于心焉，雖不謂之禮可也。二南以歌于房，雅以賦于朝廷，頌以奏于廟，鍾鼓管磬以宣其聲，羽旄綴兆以狀其容，咏嘆淫泆、發揚蹈厲以象其功德，陶陶然，怡怡然，謂之樂可也。和弗生于心焉，雖不謂之樂可也。聖人以心教天下，而天下不能以聖人之心爲心，於是乎假之乎文。故習其文者，亦求其心而已矣。存其誠，謹其幾，神其用，欽以承天，輿輿以奉親。
translation_en:
…even if they cannot be ascertained, I shall establish them on the basis of what is right. Is this why Youzi may be called discerning? Thus he said: “In the practice of ritual, harmony is prized.” This shows that ritual takes reverence as its guiding principle without allowing reverence to become constricting. He also said: “Without regulating it through ritual, it cannot be put into practice either.” This shows that music prizes harmony without allowing harmony to become unrestrained. Reverence must not remain mere reverence and become constricting: it must be tempered with harmony. Harmony must not remain mere harmony and become unrestrained: it must return to reverence. Might ritual and music then flourish?

Thus marriage and capping ceremonies bring solemnity to the household; archery and communal drinking ceremonies invigorate the local community; court audiences, encounters, assemblies, and diplomatic visits establish order among the states. Settlements [?], jade tablets, lambs, and geese serve as presentation gifts; dun, lian, hu, and gui vessels serve ritual observances; offering stands, attendants [?], sacrificial animals, mats, cooked meats, sliced meats, and meat sauces [the transcription repeats “meat sauces”] supply banquets for guests. All is orderly and properly arranged: one may call this ritual. Yet if reverence is not established in the heart, one may equally refuse to call it ritual.

The “Two Southern Sections” of the Book of Odes are sung in the inner chambers; the Elegantiae are recited at court; the Hymns are performed in the ancestral temple. Bells, drums, pipes, and chime stones give expression to their sounds; feathers, yak-tail banners, and marked positions in the dance formation give shape to their outward appearance. Singing and sighing, freely flowing expression, spirited movements, stamping, and vigorous steps represent achievements and virtue. All is joyful and harmonious: one may call this music. Yet if harmony does not arise in the heart, one may equally refuse to call it music.

The sage teaches the world through his heart, but the people of the world cannot make the sage’s heart their own. He therefore resorts to outward forms. Thus those who learn these forms are simply seeking that heart. Preserve sincerity, attend carefully to the first stirrings of thought, and make its operation wondrous; reverently respond to Heaven, and serve one’s parents with respectful composure [?]…

title: 正德十一年陝西鄉試錄
text:
凛若朽索之馭六馬以臨吾民惕然尊賢
貴德而恐天下之議我也而敬於是乎立
矣抑其剛伸其柔執其中奉若而不備愉
色婉容而不作包荒以納四海於時雍而
不繼以暴折節下士而虛心以容天下之
讜言和於是乎生矣敬立則儀職儀職則
器秩器秩則典脩夫其典脩雖不謂之禮
不可也和生則言協言協則音諧音諧則
律明夫其律明雖不謂之樂不可也夫是
===
之謂有子之達其諸異乎人之達歟抑斯
達也誰其啓之孔子啓之也孔子曰言而
履之禮也行而樂之樂也夫禮非敬不履
夫樂非和不樂甚矣有子之達似聖人也
在易有之曰上天下澤履君子以辨上下
定民志又曰雷出地奮豫先王以作樂崇
德殷薦之上帝以配祖考夫曰辨曰定將
不在於敬乎曰薦曰配將不在於和乎甚
矣有子之達似聖人也在書有之曰舜命
punctuated:
凛若朽索之馭六馬，以臨吾民，惕然尊賢貴德，而恐天下之議我也，而敬於是乎立矣。抑其剛，伸其柔，執其中，奉若而不備，愉色婉容而不作，包荒以納四海於時雍，而不繼以暴，折節下士，而虛心以容天下之讜言，和於是乎生矣。敬立則儀職，儀職則器秩，器秩則典脩。夫其典脩，雖不謂之禮，不可也。和生則言協，言協則音諧，音諧則律明。夫其律明，雖不謂之樂，不可也。

夫是之謂有子之達，其諸異乎人之達歟？抑斯達也，誰其啓之？孔子啓之也。孔子曰：「言而履之，禮也；行而樂之，樂也。」夫禮非敬不履，夫樂非和不樂。甚矣，有子之達似聖人也！

在《易》有之，曰：「上天下澤，履。君子以辨上下，定民志。」又曰：「雷出地奮，豫。先王以作樂崇德，殷薦之上帝，以配祖考。」夫曰辨、曰定，將不在於敬乎？曰薦、曰配，將不在於和乎？甚矣，有子之達似聖人也！在《書》有之，曰：「舜命
translation_en:
…Approach the governance of our people with apprehension, as though driving six horses with rotten reins; vigilantly honor the worthy and esteem virtue, fearing the criticism of all under Heaven. In this way, reverence is established. Restrain hardness, extend gentleness, and hold to the mean; comply reverently without reserve [?]; maintain a cheerful expression and a gentle countenance without affectation; embrace even the uncultivated, bringing all within the Four Seas into harmonious accord without following this with violence; humble yourself before men of worth and open your mind to candid counsel from throughout the realm. In this way, harmony arises. Once reverence is established, ceremonial forms fulfill their functions [?]; once these fulfill their functions, ritual vessels are properly ordered; once the vessels are properly ordered, the prescribed observances are put in good order. When these observances are in good order, one cannot refuse to call this ritual. When harmony arises, words accord; when words accord, tones harmonize; when tones harmonize, the pitch standards become clear. When the pitch standards are clear, one cannot refuse to call this music.

This is what is meant by Youzi’s understanding. Surely it differs from the understanding of others! Yet who opened the way to this understanding? Confucius opened it. Confucius said: “To put what one says into practice is ritual; to take delight in what one practices is music.” Without reverence, ritual cannot be practiced; without harmony, music cannot bring delight. How closely Youzi’s understanding resembles that of the sage!

The Book of Changes says: “Heaven above and the lake below: Treading. Through this, the gentleman distinguishes above from below and settles the people’s aspirations.” It also says: “Thunder comes forth from the earth in stirring force: Enthusiasm. Through this, the former kings made music to exalt virtue, offering it abundantly to the Lord on High and associating their ancestors with him in the sacrifice.” Do “distinguishing” and “settling” not depend upon reverence? Do “offering” and “associating” not depend upon harmony? How closely Youzi’s understanding resembles that of the sage! The Book of Documents says: “Shun commanded…

title: 正德十一年陝西鄉試錄
text:
伯夷典禮曰夙夜惟寅直哉惟清命夔典
樂曰教胄子直而溫寬而栗夫曰直曰寅
其敬矣乎曰溫曰寬其和矣乎甚矣有子
之達似聖人也雖然有子之於禮樂僅止
於達而已達之而不能行豈聖學之所貴
哉蓋在孔門惟顏子可以當之觀其請事
四勿而不遷怒貳過則有子之所達者皆
其所身有也故孔子獨舉四代禮樂告之
惜乎有子不能行其所達如顏子也若公
===
西赤之可與賓客言而願為小相可謂行
矣而達不如有子乃若曾晳之舞雩詠歸
而不規勢利其達而不能行猶有子也嗚
呼叔孫通何人也而欲興禮樂宜魯兩生
拒之而楊子許之為大臣矣然文中子謂
孔明可興禮樂豈其然乎竊謂興禮樂者
必如孔子而後可庶幾焉者其顏子乎惜
乎有子不能行其所達如顏子也
punctuated: 伯夷典禮，曰：「夙夜惟寅，直哉惟清。」命夔典樂，曰：「教胄子，直而溫，寬而栗。」夫曰直曰寅，其敬矣乎？曰溫曰寬，其和矣乎？甚矣，有子之達似聖人也！雖然，有子之於禮樂，僅止於達而已。達之而不能行，豈聖學之所貴哉？蓋在孔門，惟顏子可以當之。觀其請事四勿，而不遷怒貳過，則有子之所達者，皆其所身有也。故孔子獨舉四代禮樂告之。惜乎，有子不能行其所達如顏子也！若公西赤之可與賓客言，而願為小相，可謂行矣，而達不如有子。乃若曾晳之舞雩詠歸，而不規勢利，其達而不能行，猶有子也。嗚呼！叔孫通何人也，而欲興禮樂？宜魯兩生拒之，而楊子許之為大臣矣。然文中子謂孔明可興禮樂，豈其然乎？竊謂興禮樂者，必如孔子而後可。庶幾焉者，其顏子乎？惜乎，有子不能行其所達如顏子也！
translation_en: …Bo Yi to oversee ritual, saying: “Day and night be reverent; be upright and pure.” He charged Kui with overseeing music, saying: “Teach the sons of the nobility to be upright yet gentle, broad-minded yet firm.” Now, do “upright” and “reverent” not signify reverence? Do “gentle” and “broad-minded” not signify harmony? How closely Youzi’s understanding resembles that of a sage! Nevertheless, Youzi’s attainment in ritual and music stopped at understanding alone. To understand them but be unable to put them into practice—could this be what the learning of the sages esteems? Among the disciples of Confucius, only Yanzi could meet this standard. Consider how he asked to put the four prohibitions into practice, and neither displaced his anger onto others nor repeated his faults: everything that Youzi understood, he embodied in his own person. Thus Confucius singled him out to instruct him in the rites and music of the four dynasties. Alas, Youzi could not put his understanding into practice as Yanzi did! As for Gongxi Chi, who was fit to converse with guests and wished to serve as a minor ceremonial assistant, he may be said to have practiced these things, but his understanding fell short of Youzi’s. Then there was Zeng Xi, who wished to sing on his way home from the rain altar, without seeking power or profit: in understanding but being unable to practice, he resembled Youzi. Alas! What sort of man was Shusun Tong, that he should wish to institute ritual and music? It was fitting that the two scholars of Lu refused him, yet Yangzi acknowledged him as a great minister. Wenzhongzi, however, said that Kongming could institute ritual and music. Could that really be so? I humbly hold that only someone like Confucius could do so. Might Yanzi have come close? Alas, Youzi could not put his understanding into practice as Yanzi did!

title: 正德十一年陝西鄉試錄
text:
擬
皇明重刋少微資治通鑑節要
頒賜廷臣謝表
趙儒
同考試官教諭陳　批〔寓莊重於駢儷斂華靡於鋪叙且惓惓忠愛若有不能盡者豈可直〕
以四六觀之
同考試官教諭王　批　我
朝
===
列聖重史之意揚厲殆盡削鐻鑿輪有難以言喻者
考試官教諭李　批〔渾厚森嚴足刻炎新疎闊之弊〕
考試官學正周　批　典則可録
臣某等言正德九年十一月日司禮監重刻
少微資治通鑑節要成伏蒙
頒賜臣等者
離照崇謙亨
宮監刻
punctuated:
擬皇明重刋《少微資治通鑑節要》頒賜廷臣謝表
趙儒
同考試官教諭陳批〔寓莊重於駢儷，斂華靡於鋪叙，且惓惓忠愛，若有不能盡者，豈可直〕以四六觀之？
同考試官教諭王批：我朝列聖重史之意，揚厲殆盡。削鐻鑿輪，有難以言喻者。
考試官教諭李批〔渾厚森嚴，足刻炎新疎闊之弊。〕
考試官學正周批：典則可録。
臣某等言：正德九年十一月日，司禮監重刻《少微資治通鑑節要》成，伏蒙頒賜臣等者。
離照崇謙亨，宮監刻
translation_en:
Draft Memorial of Thanks for the August Ming’s Reprinting of Shaowei’s Essential Selections from the Comprehensive Mirror for Aid in Government and Its Bestowal upon Court Officials
By Zhao Ru

Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor, comments: 〔“It embeds gravity in parallel prose and restrains florid ornament within its expansive narration. Moreover, its devoted loyalty and affection seem inexhaustible. How could one merely〕 regard it as four-and-six prose?”

Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor, comments: “It gives almost full expression to the intent of our dynasty’s successive sage emperors in valuing history. As with carving a bell stand or fashioning a wheel, something here is difficult to convey in words.”

Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: 〔“Substantial and imposing, it is sufficient to correct the faults of ‘blazing novelty’ [?] and loose expansiveness.”〕

Examiner Zhou, School Director, comments: “Exemplary and well regulated; worthy of recording.”

Your servants, So-and-so and the others, state: On a day in the eleventh month of the ninth year of Zhengde [1514], the Directorate of Ceremonial completed its reprinting of Shaowei’s Essential Selections from the Comprehensive Mirror for Aid in Government. We reverently received copies bestowed upon us.

Your radiance, like that of the Li trigram, exalts modesty and prosperity [?]; the palace directorate engraves …

title: 正德十一年陝西鄉試錄
text:
內廷之舊史
乾符啓巽命
朝班領中秘之新編丕闡人文永昭治鑑光
騰奎壁慶協華夷臣等誠歡誠忭稽首頓
首上言伏以時當儀鳳虞廷僅止於三謨
世值獲麟孔筆特嚴於一字辭崇簡要史
厭浮華入漢以來遡元而上作者連篇而
累牘積之充棟而汗牛學問不在多言帝
王尤貴知要蘇轍規是非於遷史頗識刪
===
繁朱熹定褒貶於光書尤爲近實續編纘
作於
憲廟書法遠宗乎素王咸便省覽尚憂浩瀚
玆節要創自前人續以宋元述由後學備
載治亂之迹深適詳略之宜然雖行于鄉
閭而未登于臺閣抑徒珍其簡帙而尚遺
其舛訛豈或時有需歟宜于今斯顯矣恭
惟
皇帝陛下
punctuated: 內廷之舊史，乾符啓巽命，朝班領中秘之新編。丕闡人文，永昭治鑑；光騰奎壁，慶協華夷。臣等誠歡誠忭，稽首頓首上言：伏以時當儀鳳，虞廷僅止於三謨；世值獲麟，孔筆特嚴於一字。辭崇簡要，史厭浮華。入漢以來，遡元而上，作者連篇而累牘，積之充棟而汗牛。學問不在多言，帝王尤貴知要。蘇轍規是非於遷史，頗識刪繁；朱熹定褒貶於光書，尤爲近實。續編纘作於憲廟，書法遠宗乎素王。咸便省覽，尚憂浩瀚。玆節要創自前人，續以宋元，述由後學，備載治亂之迹，深適詳略之宜。然雖行于鄉閭，而未登于臺閣；抑徒珍其簡帙，而尚遺其舛訛。豈或時有需歟？宜于今斯顯矣。恭惟皇帝陛下，
translation_en:
…the old history of the inner court. Heaven’s auspicious signs herald the imperial command, and the assembled court officials receive the newly printed compilation from the palace library. It grandly illuminates human culture and forever makes clear the mirror for governance; its radiance rises to the Kui and Bi constellations, and its blessings unite Chinese and foreign peoples. We, your servants, rejoice with heartfelt delight, bowing our heads to the ground and knocking our foreheads upon it, and submit these words:
We humbly reflect that, in the age when phoenixes danced in stately array, the court of Shun had only the three Counsels; in the age when the qilin was captured, Confucius’s brush exercised particular rigor over even a single word. Literary expression prizes concision and essentials; historical writing shuns florid ornament. From the Han onward, through the Yuan, writers produced chapter after chapter and tablet after tablet, accumulating enough to fill houses and make the oxen hauling them sweat. Learning does not consist in a profusion of words; emperors and kings especially prize grasping the essentials. Su Zhe examined right and wrong in Sima Qian’s history and well understood how to cut away excess; Zhu Xi fixed praise and blame in Sima Guang’s work, coming still closer to the truth. A continuation was compiled in the reign of Emperor Xianzong, its principles of historical writing tracing their distant lineage to the Uncrowned King, Confucius. These works all facilitated consultation, yet their vast extent remained a concern.
This Essentials was first compiled by earlier scholars; its continuation through the Song and Yuan was written by later scholars. It fully records the course of order and disorder and strikes a fitting balance between detail and brevity. Yet although it circulated in local communities, it had not reached the central government offices. Moreover, people merely treasured its volumes while leaving its textual errors uncorrected. Could it have been awaiting a time when it would be needed? Fittingly, it now comes to prominence. We reverently consider that Your Majesty the Emperor…

title: 正德十一年陝西鄉試錄
text:
仁恩天覆
敬德日躋重農事而耕籍田禮秩補周官之
闕振儒風而臨大學宫墻增孔聖之光寵
犬羊而振旅息民殲狐鼠而虚懷禮士天
地綱常之道勤聽納於
經幃古今治亂之因屢咨詢於史館念
先皇嘗輯脩乎篡要謂
今日宜翻刻乎少微出遺簡於秘書責錄功
於司禮收數千年之往事而萃以二長刋
===
十九史之繁文而約於一帙仰承
清賜頒及微臣嗇溢豫鳴榮逾晉錫敢不焚香
以誦篤藏脩以潤身心允期撞卷而思精
獻納以裨治化儗皐夔契稷而同道求濂
洛關閩以爲師伏願
覽玆成書式于古訓言切於政必書之几屏事
感於心或銘諸户牖某可懲而某可勸達
虞舜之四聰孰爲正而孰爲邪登周文之
三宅撫
punctuated:
仁恩天覆，敬德日躋。重農事而耕籍田，禮秩補周官之闕；振儒風而臨大學，宫墻增孔聖之光。寵犬羊而振旅息民，殲狐鼠而虚懷禮士。天地綱常之道，勤聽納於經幃；古今治亂之因，屢咨詢於史館。念先皇嘗輯脩乎篡要，謂今日宜翻刻乎少微。出遺簡於秘書，責錄功於司禮。收數千年之往事，而萃以二長；刋十九史之繁文，而約於一帙。仰承清賜，頒及微臣，嗇溢豫鳴，榮逾晉錫。敢不焚香以誦，篤藏脩以潤身心；允期撞卷而思，精獻納以裨治化。儗皐夔契稷而同道，求濂洛關閩以爲師。
伏願覽玆成書，式于古訓。言切於政，必書之几屏；事感於心，或銘諸户牖。某可懲而某可勸，達虞舜之四聰；孰爲正而孰爲邪，登周文之三宅。撫
translation_en:
…Your benevolent grace shelters all like Heaven; your reverence for virtue rises daily. Esteeming agriculture, you plow the imperial sacrificial field, supplementing through your ritual observances what is lacking in the Offices of Zhou. Promoting Confucian learning, you visit the Imperial University, adding luster to the precincts of the sage Confucius. Showing favor to the “dogs and sheep” [?], you bring the troops home and give the people respite; destroying the “foxes and rats,” you humbly honor learned men. At the Classics Mat, you diligently listen to and accept instruction on Heaven and Earth and the enduring moral relationships; at the Historiography Institute, you repeatedly inquire into the causes of order and disorder, past and present. Recalling that the late emperor once compiled the Collected Essentials [?], you declared that the Shaowei history should now be reprinted. You brought forth the surviving writings from the palace library and charged the Directorate of Ceremonial with the work of copying them. Gathering the events of several thousand years, the work combines two strengths; pruning the copious text of the Nineteen Histories, it condenses them into a single bound collection. Reverently receiving this gracious gift, bestowed even upon your humble servants, we overflow with joy and give voice to our delight [?]; the honor exceeds the gifts celebrated in the hexagram Jin, “Advance.” How could we fail to burn incense as we recite it and devote ourselves earnestly to study, thereby enriching body and mind? We shall surely close the volumes [?] and reflect, refining the counsel we offer to assist your governance and transforming influence. We aspire to follow the same Way as Gao, Kui, Xie, and Ji, and seek our teachers among the masters of Lian, Luo, Guan, and Min.
We humbly wish that you would read this completed work and take ancient teachings as your model. Words bearing directly upon government should invariably be inscribed upon your desk and screen; events that move your heart might be engraved upon your doors and windows. By discerning what warrants admonition and what warrants encouragement, extend your hearing in all four directions, as did Shun of Yu; by distinguishing the upright from the wicked, appoint men to the three categories of office, as did King Wen of Zhou. May you safeguard…

title: 正德十一年陝西鄉試錄
text:
皇圖於溥海之外而守在四夷𡨴
國祚如泰山之安而傳之萬世臣等無任瞻
天仰
聖激切屏營之至謹奉
表稱
謝以
聞
第叁場
策
第一問
劉序
===
同考試官教諭陳　批　此策於我
太祖貽謀之善與
列聖繼述之美敷答詳明歸本於取人正身深爲有見而忠愛
之意溢於言表必嘗究心
聖制而知所以行法者他日效用事業豈無可觀
同考試官教諭王　批　我
孝宗皇帝制作之美功業之盛蕩蕩難名何此策事核詞贍而
punctuated:
皇圖於溥海之外，而守在四夷；𡨴國祚如泰山之安，而傳之萬世。臣等無任瞻天仰聖、激切屏營之至，謹奉表稱謝以聞。
第叁場。策。第一問。劉序。
同考試官教諭陳批：此策於我太祖貽謀之善與列聖繼述之美，敷答詳明，歸本於取人正身，深爲有見，而忠愛之意溢於言表。必嘗究心聖制，而知所以行法者。他日效用，事業豈無可觀？
同考試官教諭王批：我孝宗皇帝制作之美、功業之盛，蕩蕩難名。何此策事核詞贍而
translation_en:
…the imperial domain beyond the vast seas, with its defenses among the barbarians of the four quarters; secure the dynasty’s tenure as firmly as Mount Tai and transmit it through ten thousand generations. We, your servants, look up to Heaven and revere Your Majesty with the utmost fervor and trembling awe. We respectfully submit this memorial to express our gratitude for Your Majesty’s hearing.
Third Session. Policy Essay. First Question. Liu Xu.
Comment by Associate Examiner Chen, Instructor: This policy essay expounds clearly and fully upon the excellence of our Taizu’s plans for his successors and the admirable way in which the successive sage emperors carried them forward. By tracing the foundations to selecting men and rectifying one’s own conduct, it shows profound insight; its devotion and loyalty overflow the words themselves. The author must have studied the imperial institutions attentively and understood how to put their laws into practice. When he enters service in the future, surely his accomplishments will be worthy of regard!
Comment by Associate Examiner Wang, Instructor: The excellence of the institutions established by our Xiaozong Emperor and the grandeur of his achievements are so vast as to defy description. How is it that this policy essay is accurate in its facts and ample in its expression, and …

title: 正德十一年陝西鄉試錄
text:
宏綱大旨鋪張殆盡其亦涵咏
聖化而有得者乎
考試官教諭李　批　善能發揚哉
聖朝制作之盛録之非徒以其文也
考試官學正周　批　有議論有斷制得士如
此主司可以慶矣
對致天下之治者存乎法守天下之法者
存乎人法者天下之公所以維持世道使
常理而不亂不可以不明也任非其人則
法不可明矣人者天地之紀所以推行典
===
法使常伸而不撓不可不擇也君不脩身
則人不可擇矣然則任人其守法之要而
脩身尤任人之本乎帝王脩吾身以立取
人之則則天下之正人君子皆吾守法之
助而天下太平之治可坐致矣執事以
先帝所脩大明會典下詢且欲求其行之之要
與本者可謂仰窺
先帝之心於是典之外矣敢據所聞以對粤自
punctuated:
宏綱大旨，鋪張殆盡，其亦涵咏聖化而有得者乎？
考試官教諭李批：善能發揚哉！聖朝制作之盛，録之非徒以其文也。
考試官學正周批：有議論，有斷制，得士如此，主司可以慶矣。
對：致天下之治者存乎法，守天下之法者存乎人。法者，天下之公，所以維持世道，使常理而不亂，不可以不明也。任非其人，則法不可明矣。人者，天地之紀，所以推行典法，使常伸而不撓，不可不擇也。君不脩身，則人不可擇矣。然則任人其守法之要，而脩身尤任人之本乎？帝王脩吾身以立取人之則，則天下之正人君子皆吾守法之助，而天下太平之治可坐致矣。執事以先帝所脩《大明會典》下詢，且欲求其行之之要與本者，可謂仰窺先帝之心於是典之外矣。敢據所聞以對：粤自
translation_en:
…its broad outlines and principal purposes are expounded almost exhaustively. Surely the writer, too, has immersed himself in the sage ruler’s transforming influence and gained understanding from it?
Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: How well he brings to light the magnificence of the institutions established by our sagely dynasty! This answer is recorded not merely for its literary merit.
Examiner Zhou, Instructor, comments: There is reasoned discussion, and there is decisive judgment. Having obtained a scholar such as this, the officials presiding over the examination may congratulate themselves.
Response: Bringing order to all under Heaven depends on laws; upholding the laws of all under Heaven depends on people. Laws embody the impartial principles of all under Heaven. They sustain the order of the world, keeping it continually well governed and free from disorder, and must therefore be made clear. If those appointed are not the right people, the laws cannot be made clear. People constitute the ordering framework of Heaven and Earth. They put statutes and laws into effect, ensuring that these remain in force without being bent, and must therefore be carefully selected. If the ruler does not cultivate himself, people cannot be properly selected. Is appointing people, then, the essential requirement for upholding laws, and self-cultivation still more the foundation for appointing people? If, as emperor or king, I cultivate myself so as to establish a standard for selecting people, then all upright men and gentlemen under Heaven will assist me in upholding the laws, and peaceful government throughout the realm can be achieved with ease. You, the examining officials, have condescended to question us about the Collected Statutes of the Great Ming (Da Ming huidian), compiled under the late emperor. In seeking also the essential requirements and foundations for putting it into practice, you may be said to have reverently discerned the late emperor’s intentions beyond the text of these statutes. I venture to respond on the basis of what I have learned. Beginning from…

title: 正德十一年陝西鄉試錄
text:
堯命四仲舜咨九官禹乘典則湯立誓訓
逮周武王則又有周官周禮之書總天下
之務而分列六職故稽古正名莫善於成
周孔子所謂郁郁乎文而從之者也自周
以下秦廢先王之制妄事紛更漢因秦人
之舊而一切尚簡雖唐有六典之式宋定
會要之制以為近之要皆雜以人欲而未
純乎天理無足論也我
太祖高皇帝既定天下乃因周制初作諸司職
===
掌分列六曹而又纂輯
皇明祖訓大明集禮洪武禮制禮儀定式
神謨廟斷誠有以高出唐虞三代之上而陋漢
唐宋於下風者也百餘年來吏習民安化
成俗定
列聖嗣服謹守成筭無事紛更誠有如執事所
云者第以頒布日久簡帙散失郡邑學校
未覩其全求治者猶憾焉我
孝宗敬皇帝特命儒臣悉發中秘所藏諸書而
punctuated:
堯命四仲，舜咨九官，禹乘典則，湯立誓訓。逮周武王，則又有《周官》《周禮》之書，總天下之務而分列六職，故稽古正名，莫善於成周，孔子所謂「郁郁乎文」而從之者也。自周以下，秦廢先王之制，妄事紛更；漢因秦人之舊，而一切尚簡。雖唐有《六典》之式，宋定《會要》之制，以為近之，要皆雜以人欲而未純乎天理，無足論也。
我太祖高皇帝既定天下，乃因周制，初作《諸司職掌》，分列六曹，而又纂輯《皇明祖訓》《大明集禮》《洪武禮制》《禮儀定式》。神謨廟斷，誠有以高出唐虞三代之上，而陋漢唐宋於下風者也。百餘年來，吏習民安，化成俗定。列聖嗣服，謹守成筭，無事紛更，誠有如執事所云者。第以頒布日久，簡帙散失，郡邑學校未覩其全，求治者猶憾焉。我孝宗敬皇帝特命儒臣悉發中秘所藏諸書而
translation_en:
…Yao appointed the four Zhong; Shun consulted the nine officials; Yu adhered to established canons and rules [?]; and Tang established oaths and instructions. By the time of King Wu of Zhou, there were also the books Offices of Zhou and Rituals of Zhou, which brought together the affairs of the realm and apportioned them among six functions. Thus, in examining antiquity and rectifying names, none surpassed the accomplished Zhou order—the order of which Confucius said, “How splendid its culture!” and which he chose to follow. After Zhou, Qin abolished the institutions of the former kings and recklessly introduced changes. Han inherited Qin’s arrangements and favored simplicity in everything. Although Tang had the standards of the Six Canons and Song established the institutional provisions of the Collected Essentials, which might be considered close to the ancient model, they were all ultimately adulterated with human desires and fell short of the purity of Heaven’s principle. They do not merit discussion.
After our Emperor Taizu Gao had pacified the realm, he followed Zhou institutions and first compiled the Duties of the Various Offices, arranging them under the Six Ministries. He further compiled the Ancestral Instructions of the August Ming, the Collected Rituals of the Great Ming, the Hongwu Ritual Institutions, and the Established Forms of Ritual and Ceremony. His sagacious plans and court decisions truly surpassed those of the ages of Yao and Shun and the Three Dynasties, making Han, Tang, and Song seem paltry by comparison. For more than a hundred years, officials became practiced in their duties and the people lived in peace; moral transformation took effect and customs became settled. Successive sage emperors inherited the throne and scrupulously preserved established plans, refraining from needless alterations, just as you have said. Yet, because so much time had passed since these works were promulgated, their volumes had become scattered and lost. Schools in prefectures and counties had not seen them in their entirety, a matter of continuing regret to those seeking good government. Our Emperor Xiaozong Jing specially ordered his scholarly officials to bring forth all the books held in the palace’s secret collections and…

title: 正德十一年陝西鄉試錄
text:
叅以新舊事例分韻而類萃之於是乎大
明會典成焉固將詔萬世
聖子神孫以守
祖宗之法亦萬世臣子以知職分之常其於
聖祖之制豈不大有補乎愚嘗伏讀是書而事
事爲之籌矣革元之政罷中書而任六曹
此
太祖高皇帝設官之法誠合成周之制矣或以
爲政權必有所歸故
===
太宗文皇帝初選儒臣俾居内閣而三學士之
任隆焉黜詩賦而崇經義此
太祖高皇帝取士之制誠得夫朱熹之所議矣
或以爲通才宜無不兼故
太宗文皇帝初選進士俾讀秘書而庶吉士之
名立焉海陸二運古今之通行也然覆溺
之禍推輓之勞有所未宜則會通之河創
自勝國而成於我
朝誠萬世之利也律令二書
punctuated:
叅以新舊事例，分韻而類萃之，於是乎《大明會典》成焉。固將詔萬世聖子神孫以守祖宗之法，亦萬世臣子以知職分之常。其於聖祖之制，豈不大有補乎？愚嘗伏讀是書，而事事爲之籌矣。
革元之政，罷中書而任六曹，此太祖高皇帝設官之法，誠合成周之制矣。或以爲政權必有所歸，故太宗文皇帝初選儒臣，俾居内閣，而三學士之任隆焉。黜詩賦而崇經義，此太祖高皇帝取士之制，誠得夫朱熹之所議矣。或以爲通才宜無不兼，故太宗文皇帝初選進士，俾讀秘書，而庶吉士之名立焉。海陸二運，古今之通行也。然覆溺之禍、推輓之勞，有所未宜，則會通之河，創自勝國而成於我朝，誠萬世之利也。律令二書
translation_en:
…and collated them with old and new precedents, arranging them by rhyme and gathering them into categories. Thus the Collected Statutes of the Great Ming was completed. Its purpose was surely to instruct the sagely sons and divine grandsons of all future generations to preserve the laws of their ancestors, and also to enable subjects of all future generations to understand the enduring duties of their stations. Did it not greatly supplement the institutions of the sagely founder? I have humbly read this book and considered each matter in it.
In reforming Yuan government, the Central Secretariat was abolished and responsibility entrusted to the Six Ministries. This was Emperor Taizu Gao’s method of establishing offices, and it truly accorded with the institutions of the Zhou at its height. Some, however, held that governmental authority must have a central locus. Thus Emperor Taizong Wen initially selected Confucian officials to serve in the Grand Secretariat, and the responsibilities of the three Academicians became weighty. Rejecting poetry and rhapsodies while honoring the exposition of the Classics was Emperor Taizu Gao’s system for recruiting officials, and it truly realized what Zhu Xi had advocated. Some, however, held that men of comprehensive talent should encompass every field of learning. Thus Emperor Taizong Wen initially selected metropolitan graduates (jinshi) to study books in the imperial collection, and the designation of Hanlin Bachelor (shujishi) was established. Transport by sea and by land has been customary from antiquity to the present. Yet the disasters of capsizing and drowning, and the toil of pushing and hauling, made these methods unsuitable in some respects. The Huitong Canal, begun under the preceding dynasty and completed under our dynasty, is truly a benefit for all generations. The two books of penal laws and administrative ordinances…

title: 正德十一年陝西鄉試錄
text:
祖宗之良法也然事以時異例隨世更有所未
便則條例之頒刋於
孝宗之朝而斷自
聖心又一時之宜也邊置寧夏等鎮塞設紫荆
等關疆圉固矣然近年以來數有小警愚
則以爲重分閫之權革監軍之令而積穀
練兵堅壁清野可以收不戰之功也三分
城守以資護衛七分屯種以積芻糧勞逸
均矣然極邊之地多有未闢愚則以爲宜
===
尋古人之迹合諸家之議而相土立營因
田積穀可以省遠輸之勞矣然此特據明
問而舉其槩耳乃若究其大全豈可以言
盡乎故愚甞謂典之所載者法也非典之
所能載者法外意也伊欲舉其法而不失
其意不在於任人乎天下之人有正有邪
視君身以爲進退故君身正則正人進正
人進則典法彰而雍熙太平之治可保於
無疆矣孔子告魯君曰爲政在人取人以
punctuated:
祖宗之良法也。然事以時異，例隨世更，有所未便，則條例之頒刋於孝宗之朝，而斷自聖心，又一時之宜也。邊置寧夏等鎮，塞設紫荆等關，疆圉固矣。然近年以來，數有小警，愚則以爲重分閫之權，革監軍之令，而積穀練兵，堅壁清野，可以收不戰之功也。三分城守，以資護衛；七分屯種，以積芻糧，勞逸均矣。然極邊之地，多有未闢，愚則以爲宜尋古人之迹，合諸家之議，而相土立營，因田積穀，可以省遠輸之勞矣。
然此特據明問而舉其槩耳。乃若究其大全，豈可以言盡乎？故愚甞謂典之所載者，法也；非典之所能載者，法外意也。伊欲舉其法而不失其意，不在於任人乎？天下之人，有正有邪，視君身以爲進退。故君身正，則正人進；正人進，則典法彰，而雍熙太平之治可保於無疆矣。孔子告魯君曰：「爲政在人，取人以
translation_en:
…are excellent laws handed down by our imperial ancestors. Yet circumstances differ with the times, and precedents change with the age. Where existing provisions proved unsuitable, regulations were promulgated and printed during the reign of Emperor Xiaozong, their determination proceeding from his sagely judgment. This, too, was an appropriate response to the needs of its time. Garrisons such as Ningxia were established along the frontier, and passes such as Zijing were set up at strategic barriers, securing the borders. Yet in recent years there have repeatedly been minor alarms. In my humble opinion, by strengthening the authority of regional commanders, abolishing the arrangements for army supervisors, stockpiling grain and training troops, strengthening fortifications and clearing the countryside of supplies, we could achieve success without battle. Three-tenths of the troops defend the walls to provide protection, while seven-tenths cultivate military farms to accumulate fodder and grain: toil and ease are thus equitably apportioned. Yet much land on the outermost frontier remains uncultivated. In my humble opinion, we should follow the precedents of the ancients, combine the proposals of various authorities, inspect the land to establish encampments, and accumulate grain through cultivation. We could thereby spare ourselves the labor of transporting supplies over great distances.
These, however, are merely broad outlines offered in response to your illuminating questions. How could words exhaust the subject in its entirety? Thus I have often said in my humble judgment: what the statutes record is the law; what the statutes cannot record is the intent beyond the law. If one wishes to put the law into effect without losing its intent, does this not depend upon appointing the right people? Among the people of the realm are the upright and the depraved; they look to the ruler’s own conduct in deciding whether to advance into office or withdraw. Thus, when the ruler himself is upright, upright men advance; when upright men advance, the statutes and laws are made manifest, and harmonious, flourishing, and peaceful government can be preserved forever. Confucius told the ruler of Lu: “The conduct of government depends upon men; selecting men depends upon…”

title: 正德十一年陝西鄉試錄
text:
身而濂溪周敦頤亦曰純心要矣用賢急
焉愚敢以是爲
聖天子獻
第二問
劉仕
同考試官教諭潘　批〔祭祀之問士人類多直書策目是篇獨能於上下數千年之禮考據不遺斟酌攸當博古通今無與爲儔者矣〕
考試官教諭李　批〔有考證有識見禮場之〕
===
考試官學正周　批〔拈出禮緣人情以義起策也〕
〔歸結良是〕
禮議於歷代者無一定之見禮制於
當代者有一定之規蓋歷代之議互有得失
當代之制適乎中正惟其互有得失故衆言
易以淆而紛然不一惟其適乎中正故百
世不能易而較若畫一然則
punctuated:
身。」而濂溪周敦頤亦曰：「純心要矣，用賢急焉。」愚敢以是爲聖天子獻。

第二問
劉仕
同考試官教諭潘批〔祭祀之問，士人類多直書策目，是篇獨能於上下數千年之禮，考據不遺，斟酌攸當，博古通今，無與爲儔者矣。〕
考試官教諭李批〔有考證，有識見，禮場之。〕
考試官學正周批〔拈出禮緣人情，以義起策也。〕〔歸結良是。〕

禮議於歷代者，無一定之見；禮制於當代者，有一定之規。蓋歷代之議，互有得失；當代之制，適乎中正。惟其互有得失，故衆言易以淆，而紛然不一；惟其適乎中正，故百世不能易，而較若畫一。然則
translation_en:
…one’s own person.” Zhou Dunyi of Lianxi also said: “Purifying the heart is essential; employing the worthy is urgent.” I venture to offer these words to His Sagely Majesty.

Second Question
Liu Shi

Comment by Associate Examiner Pan, Instructor: 〔In answering the question on sacrifices, most candidates merely write directly about the topics listed in the policy question. This essay alone examines the rites of several thousand years comprehensively, leaving nothing uninvestigated and weighing everything appropriately. In its broad knowledge of antiquity and understanding of the present, it has no equal.〕

Comment by Examiner Li, Instructor: 〔It offers textual verification and discerning judgment. [The remaining phrase, 禮場之, is unclear.] [?]〕

Comment by Examiner Zhou, School Instructor: 〔It singles out the principle that rites follow human feelings and begins the policy essay with this meaning [?].〕〔The conclusion is very sound.〕

Ritual as debated throughout successive dynasties admits of no single settled view; ritual as instituted by the present dynasty has definite standards. For the debates of successive dynasties contain both sound and unsound judgments, whereas the institutions of the present dynasty accord with balance and correctness. Precisely because those debates contain both sound and unsound judgments, their many pronouncements readily become confused, proliferating without agreement. Precisely because the present institutions accord with balance and correctness, they cannot be changed even after a hundred generations and are manifestly uniform. If this is so, then…

title: 正德十一年陝西鄉試錄
text:
當代之禮又豈歷代之所可望哉執事以古
今之禮下詢承學愚敢不悉心以對粤夫
舜初攝位肆祭群神洛甫告成肇稱殷禮
祭祀之典誠禮之大者也且以郊祭言之
分祭天地之說見於周禮而率循於秦漢
合祭天地之說定於新室而復行於唐宋
要之以合祭爲當也三年一郊乃漢武帝
之陋習六年一郊乃宋眞宗之鄙見然而
歷代行之秦則分祭漢則分祭新室則合
===
祭光武則分祭唐復合祭宋亦合祭而地
之時祭自是鮮舉此非郊祭之沿革者乎
以蜡祭言之鄭玄所叙有八蜡而無百穀
橫渠所叙有百穀而無昆蟲要之以橫渠
爲是也記言八蜡不通所以謹民財蓋因
其年不順成使民節費也子貢觀蜡而曰
一國之人皆若狂蓋未知百日之蜡一日
之澤也然而歷代行之夏曰清祀殷曰嘉
平周曰大蜡秦始謂之臘尋更曰嘉平漢
punctuated:
當代之禮又豈歷代之所可望哉？執事以古今之禮下詢承學，愚敢不悉心以對？粤夫舜初攝位，肆祭群神；洛甫告成，肇稱殷禮。祭祀之典，誠禮之大者也。
且以郊祭言之，分祭天地之說見於《周禮》，而率循於秦漢；合祭天地之說定於新室，而復行於唐宋。要之，以合祭爲當也。三年一郊，乃漢武帝之陋習；六年一郊，乃宋眞宗之鄙見。然而歷代行之，秦則分祭，漢則分祭，新室則合祭，光武則分祭，唐復合祭，宋亦合祭，而地之時祭自是鮮舉。此非郊祭之沿革者乎？
以蜡祭言之，鄭玄所叙有八蜡而無百穀，橫渠所叙有百穀而無昆蟲。要之，以橫渠爲是也。《記》言：「八蜡不通，所以謹民財。」蓋因其年不順成，使民節費也。子貢觀蜡而曰：「一國之人皆若狂。」蓋未知百日之蜡、一日之澤也。然而歷代行之，夏曰清祀，殷曰嘉平，周曰大蜡，秦始謂之臘，尋更曰嘉平，漢
translation_en:
…How, then, could the rites of past dynasties aspire to equal those of the present dynasty? You, sir, have graciously questioned us students about rites ancient and modern. How could I, ignorant though I am, fail to devote my whole mind to answering? When Shun first assumed the regency, he offered sacrifices to the assembled spirits; when Luo had just been completed, grand rites were first performed. Sacrificial observances are indeed among the greatest matters of ritual.
To speak first of the suburban sacrifices: the doctrine of sacrificing separately to Heaven and Earth appears in the Rites of Zhou and was generally followed under the Qin and Han. The doctrine of sacrificing jointly to Heaven and Earth was established under the Xin dynasty and revived under the Tang and Song. In sum, joint sacrifice is the proper practice. Holding a suburban sacrifice once every three years was an unsatisfactory custom of Emperor Wu of Han; holding one every six years reflected the limited understanding of Emperor Zhenzong of Song. Yet, as successive dynasties practiced these rites, the Qin sacrificed separately, as did the Han; the Xin sacrificed jointly; Emperor Guangwu sacrificed separately; the Tang again sacrificed jointly, as did the Song. Thereafter, seasonal sacrifices to Earth were seldom performed. Is this not the history of continuity and change in the suburban sacrifices?
To speak of the zha harvest sacrifice: Zheng Xuan’s account includes eight recipients of the zha sacrifice but omits the hundred grains; Hengqu’s account includes the hundred grains but omits insects. In sum, Hengqu’s account is correct. The Record of Rites says: “The eight zha sacrifices are not universally performed, so as to conserve the people’s resources.” This means that, when the year’s harvest has not ripened successfully, the people are made to economize. Zigong watched the zha sacrifice and said: “The people of the entire state all seem mad.” He did not yet understand the ‘hundred days of zha sacrifice’ [?] and the bounty of a single day. Yet successive dynasties practiced it under different names: the Xia called it Qingsi, ‘Pure Sacrifice’; the Yin called it Jiaping, ‘Excellent Peace’; and the Zhou called it Dazha, ‘Great Harvest Sacrifice.’ The Qin first called it La, then soon renamed it Jiaping. The Han…

title: 正德十一年陝西鄉試錄
text:
復曰臘而魏晉以來皆有其禮此非蜡祭
之變更者乎前古帝王不可無崇德之祀
也宋藝祖則制爲五等之饗可謂忠厚之
至矣但品第之間亦有可議若進曹操於
成康漢文之列次朱溫於景武玄憲之間
不幾於倒置乎一代功臣不可無大烝之
祀也宋寧宗則建崇德昭勳之閣可謂恩
禮之篤矣但去取之際亦有可疑若岳武
穆之忠烈而不録史彌遠之憸邪而得與
===
不幾於錯亂乎伏惟我
國家於郊
天一祭惟最謹焉蓋
國初天下甫定禮制未備即建圜丘于鍾山
之陽以冬至日祭
天建方丘于鍾山之北以夏至日祀地而中都
亦有南北丘之制十年春始定合祀之禮
列聖相承率皆合祀每歲親祀如儀仍以歲首
行之夫前古
punctuated:
復曰臘，而魏晉以來皆有其禮，此非蜡祭之變更者乎？前古帝王不可無崇德之祀也，宋藝祖則制爲五等之饗，可謂忠厚之至矣。但品第之間亦有可議，若進曹操於成康漢文之列，次朱溫於景武玄憲之間，不幾於倒置乎？一代功臣不可無大烝之祀也，宋寧宗則建崇德昭勳之閣，可謂恩禮之篤矣。但去取之際亦有可疑，若岳武穆之忠烈而不録，史彌遠之憸邪而得與，不幾於錯亂乎？
伏惟我國家於郊天一祭，惟最謹焉。蓋國初天下甫定，禮制未備，即建圜丘于鍾山之陽，以冬至日祭天；建方丘于鍾山之北，以夏至日祀地。而中都亦有南北丘之制。十年春，始定合祀之禮，列聖相承，率皆合祀，每歲親祀如儀，仍以歲首行之。夫前古
translation_en:
…again called it la; and from the Wei and Jin onward, all dynasties maintained this rite. Were these not changes in the zha harvest sacrifice? The emperors and kings of antiquity must receive sacrifices honoring their virtue. The founding emperor of the Song therefore established five grades of sacrificial offerings: this may be called the utmost in generosity and consideration. Yet aspects of the ranking remain open to question. For example, Cao Cao was elevated to the company of Kings Cheng and Kang and Emperor Wen of the Han, while Zhu Wen was placed among Jing, Wu, Xuan, and Xian. Did this not verge on turning the proper order upside down? A dynasty’s meritorious ministers must receive the great winter sacrifice. Emperor Ningzong of the Song therefore established the Chongde Zhaoxun Pavilion, honoring virtue and displaying merit: this may be called profound imperial favor and ritual regard. Yet the exclusions and inclusions remain open to doubt. Yue Wumu, despite his loyalty and valor, was not recorded, while the crafty and wicked Shi Miyuan gained admission. Did this not verge on utter confusion?
I humbly observe that our dynasty exercises the greatest care in the suburban sacrifice to Heaven. At the dynasty’s founding, when the realm had only just been pacified and the ritual institutions were still incomplete, a Round Mound was immediately built south of Zhongshan, where sacrifices were offered to Heaven on the winter solstice. A Square Mound was built north of Zhongshan, where sacrifices were offered to Earth on the summer solstice. The Central Capital, Zhongdu, likewise had southern and northern sacrificial mounds. In the spring of the tenth year, the rite of joint sacrifice was first established. The successive sage emperors have inherited this practice, all generally offering the joint sacrifice. Each year they personally perform the sacrifice according to the prescribed ceremonies, continuing to hold it at the beginning of the year. Now, in antiquity…

title: 正德十一年陝西鄉試錄
text:
天地多主分祀而我
國家獨主合祀蓋斷自
聖祖裁乎義而行之者矣何嘗拘拘于漢唐之
陋習哉至於蜡祭尤有説焉蓋八蜡之神
有先嗇焉而先嗇者八神之主也禮云主
先嗇而祀司嗇是已
國初以
郊廟社稷先農俱為大祀每歲祭先農遂耕
籍田以后稷氏配先農即先嗇后稷即司
===
嗇也
列聖登極之初而行耕籍田禮則親祭每歲以
孟春上戊日遣官致祭夫上古八蜡一皆
通祭而我
國家專祭先農裁自
聖祖酌乎禮而舉之者矣又何嘗區區于秦隋
之弊俗哉
國初於歷代帝王擇其有德于民者若伏羲
女媧以降凡三十五帝而皆追以崇德之
punctuated:
天地多主分祀，而我國家獨主合祀，蓋斷自聖祖，裁乎義而行之者矣。何嘗拘拘于漢唐之陋習哉？至於蜡祭，尤有説焉。蓋八蜡之神有先嗇焉，而先嗇者，八神之主也。禮云：「主先嗇而祀司嗇。」是已。
國初，以郊廟社稷先農俱為大祀，每歲祭先農，遂耕籍田，以后稷氏配。先農即先嗇，后稷即司嗇也。列聖登極之初，而行耕籍田禮，則親祭；每歲以孟春上戊日遣官致祭。夫上古八蜡，一皆通祭，而我國家專祭先農，裁自聖祖，酌乎禮而舉之者矣。又何嘗區區于秦隋之弊俗哉？
國初，於歷代帝王，擇其有德于民者，若伏羲、女媧以降，凡三十五帝，而皆追以崇德之
translation_en:
…Heaven and Earth were generally worshipped separately, whereas our dynasty alone favors their joint worship. This was a decision made by the sagely founder, who judged what was right and put it into practice. When did he ever bind himself to the inferior practices of the Han and Tang? There is still more to say about the year-end zha sacrifice. Among the eight deities worshipped in this sacrifice is the First Husbandman, who is chief among them. The Book of Rites says, “Give precedence to the First Husbandman and sacrifice to the Overseer of Husbandry.” This is precisely what it means.
At the beginning of our dynasty, the suburban sacrifices and those to the ancestral temple, the altars of Soil and Grain, and the First Farmer were all classified as Great Sacrifices. Each year, sacrifice was offered to the First Farmer, followed by the ploughing of the ritual field, with Hou Ji receiving sacrifice as the associated deity. The First Farmer is the First Husbandman, and Hou Ji is the Overseer of Husbandry. When the successive sage emperors performed the ceremony of ploughing the ritual field at the beginning of their reigns, they offered the sacrifice in person. Each year, on the first wu day of the first month of spring, an official is dispatched to offer sacrifice. In high antiquity, all eight deities of the zha sacrifice were worshipped together, whereas our dynasty sacrifices specifically to the First Farmer. This was determined by the sagely founder, who weighed ritual principles and instituted the practice. When did he ever confine himself to the defective customs of the Qin and Sui?
At the beginning of our dynasty, from among the emperors and kings of successive ages, those who had benefited the people through their virtue were selected: thirty-five rulers in all, from Fu Xi and Nü Wa onward. All were posthumously accorded rites honoring their virtue…

title: 正德十一年陝西鄉試錄
text:
祀而無德者不與焉其視宋藝祖之倒置
無序者不亦甚異矣乎
國初於
當代功臣取其有功于時者若徐達常遇春
而下凡十有二人而皆報以大烝之祀而
無功者不與焉其視宋寧宗錯亂無别者
不亦有間矣乎雖然禮緣人情而立者也
不近人情不可以爲禮禮以義而起者也
不合於義不可以爲禮今
===
國家
郊祀
上帝蜡祭先農追崇帝王享答功臣稽古制禮
損益百王之法斟酌儒先之見蓋所謂緣
人情以義起者也傳曰質諸鬼神而無疑
百世以俟聖人而不惑愚敢以爲我
聖祖頌書曰至治馨香感于神明黍稷非馨明
德惟馨愚敢以爲
今日獻謹對
punctuated:
祀，而無德者不與焉。其視宋藝祖之倒置無序者，不亦甚異矣乎？

國初於當代功臣，取其有功于時者，若徐達、常遇春而下，凡十有二人，而皆報以大烝之祀，而無功者不與焉。其視宋寧宗錯亂無别者，不亦有間矣乎？雖然，禮緣人情而立者也，不近人情，不可以爲禮；禮以義而起者也，不合於義，不可以爲禮。

今國家郊祀上帝，蜡祭先農，追崇帝王，享答功臣，稽古制禮，損益百王之法，斟酌儒先之見，蓋所謂緣人情以義起者也。傳曰：「質諸鬼神而無疑，百世以俟聖人而不惑。」愚敢以爲我聖祖頌。書曰：「至治馨香，感于神明。黍稷非馨，明德惟馨。」愚敢以爲今日獻。謹對。
translation_en:
…sacrifices honoring their virtue, while those without virtue were excluded. Compared with the inverted and disorderly arrangements of Emperor Yizu of Song, was this not very different indeed?

At the founding of the dynasty, among the meritorious servants of the age, those who had rendered service in their time were selected: Xu Da, Chang Yuchun, and others below them, twelve men in all. All were recompensed with offerings at the great winter sacrifice, while those without merit were excluded. Compared with the confused arrangements of Emperor Ningzong of Song, which made no distinctions, was there not a considerable difference? Nevertheless, ritual is established in accordance with human feelings; what does not accord with human feelings cannot constitute ritual. Ritual arises from righteousness; what does not conform to righteousness cannot constitute ritual.

Today our dynasty sacrifices to the Lord on High at the suburban altar, offers the zha sacrifice to the First Farmer, posthumously honors emperors and kings, and makes sacrificial offerings to recompense meritorious servants. It examines antiquity to establish ritual, modifying the practices of the many former kings and weighing the views of earlier Confucian scholars. This surely exemplifies what is meant by following human feelings and proceeding from righteousness. The transmitted text says: “Test it before the ghosts and spirits, and there is no doubt; await a sage a hundred generations hence, and there is no uncertainty.” I humbly venture to offer these words in praise of our sagely founder. The Book of Documents says: “The fragrance of perfect government moves the spirits. It is not millet that is fragrant; luminous virtue alone is fragrant.” I humbly venture to present these words to the throne today. Respectfully submitted in reply.

title: 正德十一年陝西鄉試錄
text:
第三問
管律
同考試官訓導林　批〔道學一策蓋主六經之子泛然應之殊無該括獨此篇不拘拘問目〕
〔而自得問者之意學識優於人遠矣〕
同考試官教諭黄　批〔關中故實條荅無遺尤能斷其義而不惑蓋積學待問者〕
考試官教諭李　批〔五策俱優此篇尤能具悉道學之所自録之以槩其餘〕
===
考試官學正周　批〔願學孔子最是其不固于問自者乎〕
道隱於天地自伏羲始發其藴道散於六
經至孔子始折其衷蓋六經所以載道也
其藴始發於伏羲其衷則折于孔子若求
道而不本之六經不流於異端之差繆則
涉於諸家之邪僻求之愈勤而道愈遠矣
善求道者其必知所持循也歟末學生長
關中景仰前哲固甞遡其道學之源矣竊
punctuated:
第三問
管律
同考試官訓導林批〔道學一策，蓋主六經之子，泛然應之，殊無該括。獨此篇不拘拘問目，而自得問者之意，學識優於人遠矣。〕
同考試官教諭黄批〔關中故實，條荅無遺，尤能斷其義而不惑，蓋積學待問者。〕
考試官教諭李批〔五策俱優，此篇尤能具悉道學之所自，録之以槩其餘。〕
考試官學正周批〔願學孔子，最是其不固于問自者乎？〕
道隱於天地，自伏羲始發其藴；道散於六經，至孔子始折其衷。蓋六經所以載道也，其藴始發於伏羲，其衷則折于孔子。若求道而不本之六經，不流於異端之差繆，則涉於諸家之邪僻，求之愈勤而道愈遠矣。善求道者，其必知所持循也歟！末學生長關中，景仰前哲，固甞遡其道學之源矣。竊
translation_en:
Third Question
Guan Lü

Associate Examiner Lin, Assistant Instructor, comments: 〔The policy question on the Learning of the Way chiefly concerns the “masters of the Six Classics” [?]. General responses fail to encompass its substance. This essay alone does not confine itself narrowly to the question’s particulars, but independently grasps the questioner’s intent. Its learning and insight far surpass those of others.〕

Associate Examiner Huang, Instructor, comments: 〔The historical precedents of Guanzhong are answered point by point, with nothing omitted. Especially commendable is his ability to judge their significance without confusion. He is evidently one who has accumulated learning in readiness for questioning.〕

Examiner Li, Instructor, comments: 〔All five policy essays are excellent. This one gives a particularly full account of the origins of the Learning of the Way. We include it to convey the quality of the others.〕

Examiner Zhou, School Instructor, comments: 〔His wish to emulate Confucius is most commendable. Is this perhaps why he does not confine himself to the question [?]?〕

The Way lay hidden in Heaven and Earth; only with Fuxi did its latent meaning begin to be revealed. The Way was dispersed throughout the Six Classics; only with Confucius was its proper balance established. For the Six Classics are the means by which the Way is conveyed. Its latent meaning was first revealed by Fuxi, and its proper balance was established by Confucius. If one seeks the Way without grounding oneself in the Six Classics, one will either drift into the errors of heterodox teachings or become entangled in the perverse deviations of the various schools. The more diligently one seeks it, the farther away the Way becomes. Surely those who seek the Way well must know what to uphold and follow!

I, a humble student, was born and raised in Guanzhong. In admiration of the worthy thinkers of earlier times, I have indeed traced the origins of their Learning of the Way. I humbly…

title: 正德十一年陝西鄉試錄
text:
承明問下及敢試陳之葢洪荒之世斯道
尚隱於渾淪人文未昭於天下聖神起而
繼天立極以開萬世道學之源是豈偶然
之故哉夫當混沌初闢之時茹毛飲血之
日政尚結繩何有於文字乎惟伏羲生感
華渚之異以木德而王也仰觀俯察始畫
八卦以通神明之德以類萬物之情而文
字於是乎著矣其曰畫卦取則於河圖亦
一時理數之相感耳若無河圖之出道其
===
能終藏乎然文字雖著何有於制作乎迨
少昊生感華渚之祥以金德而王也無感
不通建鼓制磬以通山川之風以作大淵
之樂而制作於是乎立矣其曰作樂有感
於鳳鳥亦一時神物之相契耳若無鳳鳥
之至道其能終秘乎繼而至于有周文王
之爲君也澤及枯骨而來諸侯之歸因卦
繫辭以見因羑里也然羑里不因而吉凶
消長之理其能外聖人之心乎周公之爲
punctuated: 承明問下及，敢試陳之。葢洪荒之世，斯道尚隱於渾淪，人文未昭於天下，聖神起而繼天立極，以開萬世道學之源，是豈偶然之故哉？夫當混沌初闢之時，茹毛飲血之日，政尚結繩，何有於文字乎？惟伏羲生感華渚之異，以木德而王也，仰觀俯察，始畫八卦，以通神明之德，以類萬物之情，而文字於是乎著矣。其曰畫卦取則於河圖，亦一時理數之相感耳。若無河圖之出，道其能終藏乎？然文字雖著，何有於制作乎？迨少昊生感華渚之祥，以金德而王也，無感不通，建鼓制磬，以通山川之風，以作大淵之樂，而制作於是乎立矣。其曰作樂有感於鳳鳥，亦一時神物之相契耳。若無鳳鳥之至，道其能終秘乎？繼而至于有周，文王之爲君也，澤及枯骨而來諸侯之歸，因卦繫辭，以見因羑里也。然羑里不因，而吉凶消長之理，其能外聖人之心乎？周公之爲
translation_en:
…Having received your illuminating question, graciously extended to me, I venture to set forth an answer. In the primeval age, this Way still lay hidden within undifferentiated chaos, and human culture had not yet shone forth throughout the world. The divine sages arose to carry on Heaven’s work and establish the supreme standard, thereby opening the source of learning about the Way for all subsequent ages. Could this possibly have happened by chance? When primordial chaos first opened, in the days when people ate flesh with its hair and drank blood, government still relied on knotted cords. What writing could there have been?

Fuxi’s birth was prompted by a marvel at Huazhu, and he ruled through the potency of Wood. Looking upward and examining downward, he first drew the Eight Trigrams, thereby communicating with the powers of the spirits and classifying the characteristics of the myriad things. Writing thus became manifest. As for the claim that he took the River Chart as his model in drawing the trigrams, this was merely a mutual response between principle and numerical pattern at that particular moment. Had the River Chart never appeared, could the Way have remained hidden forever?

Yet although writing had become manifest, what institutions and cultural creations were there? Shaohao’s birth was prompted by an auspicious sign at Huazhu, and he ruled through the potency of Metal. He responded to every stimulus without impediment. He erected drums and fashioned stone chimes to give expression to the airs of mountains and rivers and to perform the music of the Great Abyss (Dayuan). Institutions and cultural creations were thus established. As for the claim that the phoenix inspired his creation of music, this was merely a conjunction with a divine creature at that particular moment. Had the phoenix never arrived, could the Way have remained concealed forever?

Then came the Zhou. As ruler, King Wen extended his beneficence even to dry bones, bringing the feudal lords to offer their allegiance. He appended statements to the hexagrams because he was imprisoned at Youli [?]. Yet had he not been imprisoned at Youli, could the principles of good and ill fortune, waning and waxing, have lain outside the sage’s mind? As for the Duke of Zhou’s service as …

title: 正德十一年陝西鄉試錄
text:
相也保輔幼君而來流言之謗因爻繫辭
以避居東都也然東都不避而進退存亡
之道其能出聖心之外乎若呂望著鷹揚
之勇以佐武王伐商於其即位也進以敬
怠義欲之戒貞人主之心學也此蓋得於
海濱垂釣之時武王納之如轉圜而銘諸
几席觴豆困其所也横渠悟性學之非而
從二程以講道於其學徒也示以訂頑砭
愚之訓眞造道之格言也此蓋得於精思
===
力踐之餘程子謂其啓爭端而更爲東銘
西銘信其然也至若吾夫子六經之删述
爲萬世之準繩於穆公悔過之誓乃附之
經而備録其辭蓋欲以示戒不以伯而有
所嫌取言不廢於人之意也平王黍離之
詩乃降之風而不入於雅蓋傷其東遷不
以王而有所諱正名必考實之之意也禮
足以固人肌膚筋骸也故夫子曰立於禮
而張子以學禮爲先誠得聖人之旨而善
punctuated:
相也，保輔幼君而來流言之謗，因爻繫辭，以避居東都也。然東都不避，而進退存亡之道，其能出聖心之外乎？若呂望著鷹揚之勇，以佐武王伐商，於其即位也，進以敬怠義欲之戒，貞人主之心學也。此蓋得於海濱垂釣之時，武王納之如轉圜，而銘諸几席觴豆，困其所也。横渠悟性學之非，而從二程以講道，於其學徒也，示以訂頑砭愚之訓，眞造道之格言也。此蓋得於精思力踐之餘，程子謂其啓爭端，而更爲《東銘》《西銘》，信其然也。
至若吾夫子六經之删述，爲萬世之準繩。於穆公悔過之誓，乃附之經而備録其辭，蓋欲以示戒，不以伯而有所嫌，取言不廢於人之意也。平王《黍離》之詩，乃降之風而不入於雅，蓋傷其東遷，不以王而有所諱，正名必考實之之意也。禮足以固人肌膚筋骸也，故夫子曰：「立於禮。」而張子以學禮爲先，誠得聖人之旨而善
translation_en:
…as minister, he protected and assisted the young ruler, only to incur slanderous rumors. He appended explanations to the hexagram lines on the occasion of his withdrawal to the eastern capital. Yet had he not withdrawn there, could the principles of advancing and retiring, preservation and destruction, have lain beyond the sage’s mind? Lü Wang displayed the valor of a soaring hawk in assisting King Wu’s campaign against Shang. When the king ascended the throne, he presented admonitions concerning reverence and indolence, righteousness and desire, thereby setting the ruler’s learning of the mind on a correct course. These insights were surely gained while he fished by the seashore. King Wu accepted them as readily as turning a round object and inscribed them on his tables, mats, drinking cups, and food vessels, “constrained in their place” [?]. Hengqu [Zhang Zai] recognized errors in his study of human nature and followed the two Cheng brothers in discussing the Way. To his students he offered the teachings “Correcting Obstinacy” and “Curing Folly”—truly maxims for attaining the Way. These surely arose from deep reflection and earnest practice. Master Cheng said that their titles invited contention and renamed them the Eastern Inscription and Western Inscription. This was indeed so.
As for our Master’s editing and exposition of the Six Classics, these established standards for all ages. He included Duke Mu’s oath of repentance in the Classic of Documents and recorded its wording in full, intending to offer a warning. He did not disdain it because its author was a hegemon: his intention was to accept worthy words without rejecting them on account of the speaker. The poem “The Millet Grows Luxuriant” (Shu li), concerning King Ping, he relegated to the Airs rather than including it among the Odes. This expressed grief at the eastward transfer of the capital; he did not conceal the matter out of deference to the king. His intention was that rectifying names must involve examining the realities they designate. Ritual is sufficient to give firmness to a person’s skin, flesh, sinews, and bones. Thus the Master said, “Take your stand through ritual.” Master Zhang made learning ritual the first priority, truly grasping the sage’s intent and excelling…

title: 正德十一年陝西鄉試錄
text:
於敎學者乎樂足以養人德性氣質也故
夫子曰成於樂而唐太宗謂緣物設敎何
其發言之易而果於非聖人乎噫不有伏
羲則斯道之藴曷自而發不有孔子則折
衷之義何從而明是二聖人者大有功於
斯道大有功於群聖大有功於天下萬世
也秦穆唐皇姑所不論然少昊文王周公
太公張子之數聖賢皆崛起關中倡明道
學正三秦之桑梓所當景仰而慨慕者也
===
今日所願學者則孔子焉耳蓋學六經即
所以學孔子學孔子即所以學先哲其始
也雖不專取善於一鄉其終也一鄉之善
亦不外是而可以得矣妄意如斯未知執
事肯與其進而敎之否乎
第四問
王準
考試官敎諭李　批〔豪傑之事非豪傑不能〕
悉此篇於古人氣節之高處獨能據成說而
punctuated:
於敎學者乎？樂足以養人德性氣質也，故夫子曰：「成於樂。」而唐太宗謂緣物設敎，何其發言之易，而果於非聖人乎？噫！不有伏羲，則斯道之藴曷自而發？不有孔子，則折衷之義何從而明？是二聖人者，大有功於斯道，大有功於群聖，大有功於天下萬世也。秦穆、唐皇姑所不論，然少昊、文王、周公、太公、張子之數聖賢，皆崛起關中，倡明道學，正三秦之桑梓所當景仰而慨慕者也。今日所願學者，則孔子焉耳。蓋學六經，即所以學孔子；學孔子，即所以學先哲。其始也，雖不專取善於一鄉；其終也，一鄉之善亦不外是，而可以得矣。妄意如斯，未知執事肯與其進而敎之否乎？
第四問
王準
考試官敎諭李，批〔豪傑之事非豪傑不能〕悉。此篇於古人氣節之高處，獨能據成說而
translation_en:
…was he not skilled in teaching? Music is sufficient to nourish a person’s moral nature and temperament. Thus the Master said, “One is perfected through music.” Yet Emperor Taizong of the Tang spoke of devising instruction according to external things: how lightly he spoke, and how rashly he criticized the sage! Ah! Without Fuxi, how could the hidden riches of this Way have been revealed? Without Confucius, how could the principles for weighing and adjudicating teachings have become clear? These two sages rendered great service to this Way, to all the sages, and to the world for countless generations. Let us set aside Duke Mu of Qin and the Tang emperor for now. Yet those sages and worthies—Shaohao, King Wen, the Duke of Zhou, the Grand Duke, and Master Zhang—all rose to prominence in Guanzhong and promoted and elucidated the Learning of the Way. They are precisely those whom people native to the Three Qin region ought to revere and ardently admire.
The one whom I wish to emulate today is Confucius alone. Studying the Six Classics is the means of emulating Confucius; emulating Confucius is the means of emulating the wise men of the past. Although at the outset one does not draw goodness exclusively from a single locality, in the end the goodness of that locality also falls within this learning and can thereby be attained. Such are my presumptuous thoughts. I do not know whether you, honored sir, would be willing to encourage my progress and instruct me.
Fourth Question
Wang Zhun
Comment by Examiner Li, Instructor: “Only a hero can fully comprehend heroic deeds. In considering the heights of moral courage and integrity attained by men of antiquity, this essay alone is able to draw upon established interpretations and…”

title: 正德十一年陝西鄉試錄
text:
低昂之三秦豪傑非子而誰耶
考試官學正周　批　士氣一策正以觀諸士
子夙昔所養何如耳子能據經折傳敷答詳
明且議論英發志節軒昂正大之氣溢於言
表曾中所養槩可見已他日當大任而不撓
所志者必子也高薦高薦
天下之大節士不可以不全天地之正氣
士不可以不養夫成仁取義士大夫之大
節也至大至剛天地間之正氣也士節不
===
全固無以扶綱常而矯時弊士氣不養又
無以配道義而塞天地矣安望其立天下
之大節而無愧哉此節義之所以不可失
而士之正氣不可不養也執事發策而以
士氣下詢是蓋以完節正氣期待承學也
顧愚踵人何足以當之雖然亦嘗讀曾子
大勇之說誦天祥正氣之歌而知其槩矣
請爲執事陳之吾儒之在天下節欲其高
毋或挫于利害氣欲其正毋或餒于私邪
punctuated:
低昂之。三秦豪傑，非子而誰耶？

考試官學正周，批：士氣一策，正以觀諸士子夙昔所養何如耳。子能據經折傳，敷答詳明，且議論英發，志節軒昂，正大之氣溢於言表，曾中所養，槩可見已。他日當大任而不撓所志者，必子也。高薦！高薦！

天下之大節，士不可以不全；天地之正氣，士不可以不養。夫成仁取義，士大夫之大節也；至大至剛，天地間之正氣也。士節不全，固無以扶綱常而矯時弊；士氣不養，又無以配道義而塞天地矣。安望其立天下之大節而無愧哉？此節義之所以不可失，而士之正氣不可不養也。執事發策，而以士氣下詢，是蓋以完節正氣期待承學也。顧愚踵人，何足以當之？雖然，亦嘗讀曾子大勇之說，誦天祥正氣之歌，而知其槩矣。請爲執事陳之。吾儒之在天下，節欲其高，毋或挫于利害；氣欲其正，毋或餒于私邪，
translation_en:
…weighing their relative merits. Among the outstanding men of Sanqin, who could it be but you?

Comment by Examiner Zhou, School Instructor: This policy question on the moral spirit of scholars is intended precisely to reveal what the candidates have cultivated over the years. You use the classics to adjudicate the transmitted accounts, and your response is detailed and clear. Moreover, your arguments are brilliant and vigorous, your aspirations and integrity lofty; an upright and magnanimous spirit shines through your words. What you have cultivated within [?] can largely be discerned. Surely you will be one who shoulders great responsibilities in the future without wavering in his resolve. Highly recommended! Highly recommended!

Scholars must preserve intact the great moral integrity of the world; scholars must nurture the upright vital force of Heaven and Earth. Fulfilling benevolence and choosing righteousness constitute the great moral integrity of scholar-officials; that which is supremely vast and supremely firm is the upright vital force between Heaven and Earth. Without intact integrity, scholars certainly cannot uphold the cardinal bonds and constant virtues or remedy the abuses of the age. Without nurturing their vital force, they likewise cannot accord with the Way and righteousness and fill Heaven and Earth. How, then, could one expect them to uphold the world’s great moral integrity without shame? This is why integrity and righteousness must not be lost, and why scholars must nurture their upright vital force.

You, honored examiners, have set a policy question and deigned to inquire about the moral spirit of scholars. Surely this means that you expect us students to preserve our integrity and rectify our vital force. But how could I, a foolish follower of others [?], measure up to this expectation? Nevertheless, I have read Zengzi’s account of great courage and recited Tianxiang’s Song of Upright Vital Force, and have come to understand its broad outlines. Allow me to set them forth for you. As Confucian scholars living in this world, we must aspire to lofty integrity, never allowing it to be broken by considerations of advantage or harm; we must aspire to upright vital force, never allowing it to be enfeebled by selfishness or perversity…

title: 正德十一年陝西鄉試錄
text:
然後天下之事或可有爲庶幾昼漏之心
僅能無愧處則爲君子出則爲名臣矣我
思古人具有成迹魯仲連處六國而不帝
秦據當時而言亦可謂高士也孔斌特許
爲次是乃求全之說豈確論乎王蠋耻事
二君而死於齊據其事而言誠可謂忠臣
也樂毅乃封其墓實表盡忠之節其知己
乎皇甫規慕黨錮之皆賢故以不與爲辱
而自言其竟無所坐者乃桓帝厭夫梁遂
===
之多亦足以見直道之未必難容也尹和
靖憤程學之見攻故以學程自任而不出
其强有所命者乃高宗嘉其恬退之節亦
可以見公道之終不能廢也呂獻可以熙
寧碩輔三見黜而不悔方之偺王猾夏之
子文特三已不愠頗相類耳人品之優可
槩言而無别邪邵堯夫以洛川隱逸兩被
召而不起方之長於德行之子騫其堅辭
費宰亦猶是耳出處之正何異世而同符
punctuated: 然後天下之事，或可有爲，庶幾昼漏之心僅能無愧，處則爲君子，出則爲名臣矣。我思古人，具有成迹。魯仲連處六國而不帝秦，據當時而言，亦可謂高士也。孔斌特許爲次，是乃求全之說，豈確論乎？王蠋耻事二君而死於齊，據其事而言，誠可謂忠臣也。樂毅乃封其墓，實表盡忠之節，其知己乎？皇甫規慕黨錮之皆賢，故以不與爲辱而自言。其竟無所坐者，乃桓帝厭夫梁遂之多，亦足以見直道之未必難容也。尹和靖憤程學之見攻，故以學程自任而不出。其强有所命者，乃高宗嘉其恬退之節，亦可以見公道之終不能廢也。呂獻可以熙寧碩輔，三見黜而不悔，方之偺王猾夏之子文，特三已不愠，頗相類耳。人品之優，可槩言而無别邪？邵堯夫以洛川隱逸，兩被召而不起，方之長於德行之子騫，其堅辭費宰，亦猶是耳。出處之正，何異世而同符
translation_en:
…Only then may one accomplish something in the affairs of the world and perhaps just manage to remain free of shame in one’s heart [?]. In retirement one will be a gentleman; in office, an eminent minister. When I consider the men of antiquity, all have left recorded deeds.

Lu Zhonglian lived in the time of the Six States and refused to acknowledge Qin’s ruler as emperor. Judged by the circumstances of his time, he may indeed be called a man of lofty principles. Kong Bin, however, accorded him only second place. This is a demand for perfection: can it be a sound judgment? Wang Zhu considered it shameful to serve two rulers and died in Qi. Judging by his deeds, he truly deserves to be called a loyal minister. Yue Yi raised a mound over his grave, thereby honoring his integrity in giving his utmost loyalty. Was he not one who understood him?

Huangfu Gui admired the worthiness of those subjected to the party proscriptions. He therefore regarded his exclusion from their number as a disgrace and declared himself implicated. That he was ultimately charged with no offense was because Emperor Huan had tired of the multitude associated with Liang Sui [?]. This also suffices to show that upright conduct need not always be difficult for those in power to tolerate. Yin Hejing resented the attacks on Cheng’s teachings. He therefore took it upon himself to study Cheng and declined to enter office. That Emperor Gaozong nevertheless pressed an appointment upon him was because he admired his integrity in quiet retirement. This, too, shows that impartial justice cannot ultimately be suppressed.

Lü Xianke, an eminent minister of the Xining era, was dismissed three times without regret. Compare him with Ziwen, who served a ruler who presumptuously claimed kingship and assailed the Xia states [?]: Ziwen merely showed no resentment when dismissed three times, and in this respect they were rather alike. But can their excellence of character be discussed indiscriminately, without distinguishing between them? Shao Yaofu, a recluse of Luochuan, twice received summonses but did not take office. Compare him with Ziqian, who excelled in virtuous conduct: his firm refusal to become steward of Fei was much the same. In the rectitude of their choices to serve or retire, how is it that men of different ages accord so closely…

title: 正德十一年陝西鄉試錄
text:
邪清直一節終始不變傅侍郎之堅貞如
此謂之金玉君子夫豈不宜風度凝遠瀟
然塵表胡侍講之超脫如此擬之大冬松
栢夫何不可張說之黨呂宗元忠幾受誣
矣宋璟自欲叩閣而力諍實則有以激之
其名義至重數言至今讀之猶可以寒姦
諛之骨魏徵之與李絳諫臣所當法者田
錫為人梗介而寡合實則有以慕之其封
跡悉焚一事自今觀之又足以愧虛夸之
===
心龔勝之守死善道薛方之貞而不諒郭
欽蔣詡之好遯不污之數人者行若不同
其耻立莽朝皆可謂清名之佳士矣李業
之飲藥而死貫貽之漆身為癩任永馮信
之託以青盲之數子者迹雖少殊其不受
述命皆可謂苦節之古人矣當陛謁而不
屈周黨尚志誠為可嘉然而子陵之年尊
德卲實則過之若以黨而並子陵是無異
爝火之光於日月之側也諜起兵而興
punctuated: 邪？清直一節，終始不變，傅侍郎之堅貞如此，謂之金玉君子，夫豈不宜？風度凝遠，瀟然塵表，胡侍講之超脫如此，擬之大冬松栢，夫何不可？張說之黨呂宗，元忠幾受誣矣。宋璟自欲叩閣而力諍，實則有以激之。其「名義至重」數言，至今讀之，猶可以寒姦諛之骨。魏徵之與李絳，諫臣所當法者。田錫為人梗介而寡合，實則有以慕之。其封跡悉焚一事，自今觀之，又足以愧虛夸之心。龔勝之守死善道，薛方之貞而不諒，郭欽、蔣詡之好遯不污，之數人者，行若不同，其耻立莽朝，皆可謂清名之佳士矣。李業之飲藥而死，貫貽之漆身為癩，任永、馮信之託以青盲，之數子者，迹雖少殊，其不受述命，皆可謂苦節之古人矣。當陛謁而不屈，周黨尚志，誠為可嘉。然而子陵之年尊德卲，實則過之。若以黨而並子陵，是無異爝火之光於日月之側也。諜起兵而興
translation_en:
…so? Pure and upright, constant in his integrity from beginning to end: such was the steadfastness of Vice Minister Fu. Was it not fitting to call him a gentleman of gold and jade? Composed and lofty in bearing, serenely beyond the dusty world: such was the detachment of Expositor-in-waiting Hu. Why should he not be likened to pines and cypresses in deepest winter?

Through Zhang Shuo’s siding with Lü Zong [?], Yuanzhong nearly suffered a false accusation. Song Jing himself wished to approach the palace pavilion and remonstrate forcefully; indeed, he had cause to be stirred to action. His few words, “Reputation and moral duty are of the utmost importance,” can still, when read today, chill the bones of treacherous flatterers. Wei Zheng and Li Jiang were men whom remonstrating officials ought to emulate. Tian Xi was unbending and principled, finding few with whom he could agree; indeed, he had reason to admire them. Viewed from our own day, the single episode in which all his sealed writings [?] were burned is enough to shame hearts given to empty boasting.

Gong Sheng held fast to the good Way unto death; Xue Fang was steadfast without being bound by petty fidelity; Guo Qin and Jiang Xu delighted in withdrawal and remained undefiled. These men may have differed in conduct, but in their shame at serving at Wang Mang’s court, all may be called worthy gentlemen of unsullied reputation. Li Ye drank poison and died; Guan Yi lacquered his body to simulate leprosy; Ren Yong and Feng Xin pleaded blindness.
