Though these men’s actions differed somewhat, in refusing appointments from Gongsun Shu, all may be called men of antiquity who upheld their integrity through hardship.

When granted an imperial audience, Zhou Dang would not bow: his determination to uphold his aspirations was certainly commendable. Yet Ziling, venerable in years and eminent in virtue, in truth surpassed him. To rank Dang alongside Ziling would be no different from placing the light of a torch beside the sun and moon. When word came of troops being raised to revive [?] …

title: 正德十一年陝西鄉試錄
text:
復履謙勸王誠爲可取然而杲卿之指衣
示意實則倡之若以履謙而比杲卿是無
異置蚓竅之鳴於律呂之調也剛與柔而
殊科明道之見安石不閧出一危言疑若
近於柔矣而安石之怒自此乎折則玆柔
也秖所以爲剛也是剛也非曾子所謂大
勇者乎敬與慢而異路伊川之於哲宗必
欲坐講近和疑若涉於慢矣而不忍簡賢
之名出於吾君則玆慢也適所以爲敬也
===
是敬也豈景丑氏之所謂敬者乎之數子
者凜然大節與山斗而爭高浩然正氣塞
乾坤而並大皆所謂一時之豪傑者也若
欲求其可議者則顏杲卿其人也觀其
攻歐陽脩之賢而太迫降安祿山之後而
始奮吹毛求疵是則爲可議已若欲求其
最者則子騫堯夫兩程其人也觀其講明
聖學承續道統是則不可尚已愚生之所
師法者不在玆乎茍曰姑舍是而別有所
punctuated:
復。履謙勸王，誠爲可取，然而杲卿之指衣示意，實則倡之。若以履謙而比杲卿，是無異置蚓竅之鳴於律呂之調也。剛與柔而殊科，明道之見安石，不閧出一危言，疑若近於柔矣；而安石之怒自此乎折，則玆柔也，秖所以爲剛也。是剛也，非曾子所謂大勇者乎？敬與慢而異路，伊川之於哲宗，必欲坐講近和，疑若涉於慢矣；而不忍簡賢之名出於吾君，則玆慢也，適所以爲敬也。是敬也，豈景丑氏之所謂敬者乎？之數子者，凜然大節，與山斗而爭高；浩然正氣，塞乾坤而並大，皆所謂一時之豪傑者也。
若欲求其可議者，則顏杲卿其人也。觀其攻歐陽脩之賢而太迫，降安祿山之後而始奮，吹毛求疵，是則爲可議已。若欲求其最者，則子騫、堯夫、兩程其人也。觀其講明聖學，承續道統，是則不可尚已。愚生之所師法者，不在玆乎？茍曰姑舍是而別有所
translation_en:
…restoration. Lüqian’s urging the king [?] was indeed commendable; yet Gaoqing’s pointing to his robe to convey his meaning had in fact set the example. To compare Lüqian with Gaoqing would be like placing the sound from an earthworm’s burrow alongside music attuned to the pitch standards.
Firmness and gentleness belong to different categories. When Mingdao met Anshi, he did not loudly utter a single stern word [?], and thus seemed close to gentleness. Yet Anshi’s anger was thereby checked: this gentleness was precisely his means of being firm. Was this firmness not what Zengzi called great courage? Respect and disrespect follow different paths. In dealing with Emperor Zhezong, Yichuan insisted on lecturing while seated, in an atmosphere of closeness and harmony [?], and thus seemed to verge on disrespect. Yet he could not bear that his sovereign should acquire a reputation for slighting worthy men: this apparent disrespect was precisely his means of showing respect. Could such respect be what Jing Chou meant by respect? These men’s awe-inspiring integrity rivaled the height of Mount Tai and the Northern Dipper; their vast upright spirit filled Heaven and Earth and matched their greatness. All were what one calls outstanding men of their age.
If we seek someone among them open to criticism, Yan Gaoqing is that man. Consider how he pressed too harshly in attacking the worthy Ouyang Xiu [?], and only roused himself after surrendering to An Lushan. If one insists on blowing aside the hair to find a blemish, these things could indeed be criticized. If we seek the finest among them, Ziqian, Yaofu, and the two Cheng brothers are the men. Consider how they elucidated the learning of the sages and carried forward the transmission of the Way: in this they cannot be surpassed. Is it not here that I, an unworthy student, find my models? If one were to say that we should set these aside for the moment and seek something else…

title: 正德十一年陝西鄉試錄
text:
取以邪名非惟生之所羞恐亦執事之所
不與也抑愚於此又有說焉士固不可以
無正氣矣而培養生成之方則在於義故
曰是集義所生者非義襲而取之也士氣
固當以自養矣而鼓舞化導之方則又在
於上故曰周之士也貴秦之士也賤爲士
者能用孟子之說以自養在上者能用揚
子之說以作士則士之全正氣而完大節
者將不可以勝紀矣世道之重輕顧不亦
===
將有賴邪愚之聞于師友者如此茲以之
復執事幸相與正之
第五問
楊經
同考試官訓導彭 批 禦戎備邊正今日急務
此作歷陳制馭之本備禦之策纖悉無遺而
經略大法又類長旁溢出人意表甚士之然
抱經濟之才者歟
考試官教諭李 批 終塲策士詳答多拙於
punctuated:
取以邪名，非惟生之所羞，恐亦執事之所不與也。抑愚於此又有說焉：士固不可以無正氣矣，而培養生成之方則在於義，故曰：「是集義所生者，非義襲而取之也。」士氣固當以自養矣，而鼓舞化導之方則又在於上，故曰：「周之士也貴，秦之士也賤。」爲士者能用孟子之說以自養，在上者能用揚子之說以作士，則士之全正氣而完大節者，將不可以勝紀矣。世道之重輕，顧不亦將有賴邪？愚之聞于師友者如此，茲以之復執事，幸相與正之。

第五問
楊經

同考試官訓導彭批：禦戎備邊，正今日急務。此作歷陳制馭之本、備禦之策，纖悉無遺，而經略大法又類長旁溢，出人意表，甚士之然，抱經濟之才者歟？

考試官教諭李批：終塲策士，詳答多拙於
translation_en:
…make a choice on the basis of an improper reputation [?]. Not only would this shame me, your student; I fear it would also meet with your disapproval. Yet I have something further to say about this. A scholar certainly cannot lack upright vital force, and righteousness is the means of nurturing and developing it. Thus it is said: “It is produced by accumulating righteousness, not acquired through an isolated act of righteousness.” Scholars must indeed cultivate their own moral spirit, but the means of inspiring, transforming, and guiding them also rests with those above. Thus it is said: “The scholars of Zhou were esteemed; the scholars of Qin were held cheap.” If scholars can apply Mengzi’s teaching to their own cultivation, and those above can apply Master Yang’s teaching to invigorating scholars, then scholars who preserve their upright vital force and maintain their integrity in great matters will become too numerous to record. Would not the standing of the moral order also depend upon this? Such is what I have learned from teachers and friends. I now offer it in reply to you and hope that you will help correct it.

Fifth Question
Yang Jing

Comment by Associate Examiner Peng, Assistant Instructor: Resisting the Rong and preparing the frontier’s defenses are precisely the urgent tasks of today. This essay sets out in succession the foundations of controlling them and the measures for defensive preparedness, omitting not even the smallest detail. Its broad principles of strategic management also extend abundantly in all directions [?], exceeding expectations. Surely this is a scholar possessed of the ability to govern and bring order to the world [?]!

Comment by Examiner Li, Instructor: In testing scholars through policy questions in the final session, detailed answers are often clumsy in …

title: 正德十一年陝西鄉試錄
text:
陳言略者率直書問目是豈主司策士之意
哉此策宏博詳切識達時務且中無一長語
足厭豈三秦豪傑之士乎
考試官學正周　批〔不泛不略具見經濟之才策士中之佳者也〕
對制馭有大本而後可以言待戎之道備禦
有大具而後可以言安邊之策蓋待戎不
專務乎威強而在於制馭之者有其本安
邊不專恃乎攻戰而在於備禦之者有其
===
具苟於此不立其本於無事之日而飭其
具於有事之時吾恐內脩之治既不足以
消其桀驁強梗之心外攘之威又不足以
折其兇暴侵凌之氣其何以圖治安而除
禍亂也歟執事秋闈發策而以制戎備邊
下問豈以是二者爲承學關輔之大患鄉
邦之急務也然亦耿耿有懷久矣敢不悉
心以對慨自干羽之化湮而烽燧之警熾
夷狄之禍起矣且夷狄者一氣所生不可
punctuated:
陳言，略者率直書問目，是豈主司策士之意哉？此策宏博詳切，識達時務，且中無一長語足厭，豈三秦豪傑之士乎？
考試官學正周，批〔不泛不略，具見經濟之才，策士中之佳者也。〕
對：制馭有大本，而後可以言待戎之道；備禦有大具，而後可以言安邊之策。蓋待戎不專務乎威強，而在於制馭之者有其本；安邊不專恃乎攻戰，而在於備禦之者有其具。苟於此不立其本於無事之日，而飭其具於有事之時，吾恐內脩之治既不足以消其桀驁強梗之心，外攘之威又不足以折其兇暴侵凌之氣，其何以圖治安而除禍亂也歟？執事秋闈發策，而以制戎備邊下問，豈以是二者爲承學關輔之大患、鄉邦之急務也？然亦耿耿有懷久矣，敢不悉心以對？慨自干羽之化湮，而烽燧之警熾，夷狄之禍起矣。且夷狄者，一氣所生，不可
translation_en:
…hackneyed statements; those who answer briefly generally just copy out the questions. Can this be what the presiding officials intend in examining candidates through policy questions? This policy essay is broad in scope, detailed and pertinent, and displays a discerning understanding of current affairs. Moreover, it contains not a single tedious, superfluous phrase. Might its author be an outstanding man of Sanqin?
Examiner Zhou, an Instructor, comments: 〔Neither vague nor cursory, it fully reveals a talent for governing. Its author is among the best of those examined through policy questions.〕
Response: Only when control rests upon a firm foundation can one discuss the way to deal with the Rong; only when defense possesses the essential means can one discuss policies for securing the frontier. Dealing with the Rong does not depend solely upon force and strength, but upon having a foundation for controlling them. Securing the frontier does not depend solely upon offensive warfare, but upon possessing the means of defense. If one fails to establish this foundation in peaceful times and puts the means in order only when trouble arises, I fear that domestic good government will be insufficient to quell their rebellious and obstinate disposition, while the power to repel them abroad will likewise be insufficient to break their fierce and aggressive spirit. How, then, can one seek order and security and eliminate calamity and disorder?
You, honored officials, have set policy questions for the autumn examination and graciously asked about controlling the Rong and defending the frontier. Is this because you regard these two matters as grave concerns for us students of the Guanfu region [?] and urgent tasks for our native land? These matters have indeed weighed upon my mind for a long time. How could I dare not devote my whole attention to answering?
Alas, since the civilizing influence of the dance with shields and feathers faded away and warning beacon fires blazed ever more fiercely, the calamities inflicted by the Yi and Di have arisen. Furthermore, the Yi and Di are born of the same vital force, and cannot…

title: 正德十一年陝西鄉試錄
text:
以翦而滅也五方異族不可以臣而畜也
以在己之强弱爲去留視中國之盛衰爲
叛服先王知其然惟圖內脩之治以立外
攘之威端治本以正朝廷圖治功以脩德
業飭治具以立紀綱初不計彼之盛衰以
爲我之有無此固制馭夷狄之大本先儒
論之詳矣姑請借漢爲諭而略爲執事陳
之且漢高興業撫全盛之資孝武繼世負
雄武之略當是時也群策獻謀群力効勇
===
加以材良精於休養士馬强於富庶大與
平城之師屢致攘却之舉彼二君者非不
欲其稽首闕庭以雪其侵侮之憤納款邊
塞以遂其喜功之心也然而白登之圍一
合而中國之威靈以喪幕南王庭雖絕而
海內之虛耗已極揆諸先王制馭戎狄之
道其得失何如也迨至哀帝之時何時也
治弛於內脩攉移於外戚其威强視之高
武之世固萬萬不侔矣而匈奴單于乃上
punctuated:
以翦而滅也，五方異族，不可以臣而畜也。以在己之强弱爲去留，視中國之盛衰爲叛服。先王知其然，惟圖內脩之治，以立外攘之威；端治本以正朝廷，圖治功以脩德業，飭治具以立紀綱。初不計彼之盛衰，以爲我之有無。此固制馭夷狄之大本，先儒論之詳矣。姑請借漢爲諭，而略爲執事陳之。
且漢高興業，撫全盛之資；孝武繼世，負雄武之略。當是時也，群策獻謀，群力効勇。加以材良精於休養，士馬强於富庶，大與平城之師，屢致攘却之舉。彼二君者，非不欲其稽首闕庭，以雪其侵侮之憤；納款邊塞，以遂其喜功之心也。然而白登之圍一合，而中國之威靈以喪；幕南王庭雖絕，而海內之虛耗已極。揆諸先王制馭戎狄之道，其得失何如也？迨至哀帝之時，何時也？治弛於內脩，攉移於外戚，其威强視之高武之世，固萬萬不侔矣。而匈奴單于乃上
translation_en:
…be cut down and exterminated; the different peoples of the five regions cannot be kept as subjects. They withdraw or remain according to their own strength or weakness, and rebel or submit according to the prosperity or decline of the Central Kingdom. The former kings understood this. They sought only to put internal government in order, thereby establishing the authority needed to repel external enemies. They set the foundations of government aright to rectify the court, pursued effective government by cultivating virtue and its works, and put the instruments of government in order to establish discipline. They never made their own preparations depend upon the enemy’s prosperity or decline. This is indeed the great foundation for controlling the peoples beyond the realm, which earlier Confucian scholars have discussed in detail. Allow me to draw an illustration from the Han and briefly set it before you.
When Gaozu of Han founded his enterprise, he commanded the resources of a flourishing realm; when Emperor Xiaowu succeeded to the throne, he possessed bold martial strategies. At that time, men of counsel offered plans, and men of strength displayed their courage. Moreover, able men were brought to excellence through nurture and recuperation [?], while soldiers and horses grew strong through wealth and abundance. A great army was raised at Pingcheng [?], and repeated campaigns were undertaken to drive the enemy back. These two rulers certainly wished the enemy to bow their heads to the ground before the imperial court, thus assuaging their anger at incursions and insults, and to tender submission at the frontier, thus satisfying their desire for achievement. Yet once the encirclement at Baideng closed, the awe-inspiring authority of the Central Kingdom was lost. Although the royal court south of the desert was eliminated, exhaustion and depletion within the realm had reached their utmost extent. Judged against the former kings’ way of controlling the Rong and Di, how should these successes and failures be assessed? And when we come to Emperor Ai’s reign, what sort of time was it? Internal government had grown lax, and power had shifted to the imperial maternal and marital relatives [?]. Its authority and strength were incomparably inferior to those of Gaozu’s and Emperor Wu’s reigns. Yet the chanyu of the Xiongnu then submitted…

title: 正德十一年陝西鄉試錄
text:
書願朝奉執國珍賛謁稽首前日狼貪虎
噬之人今與鵷班鷺序之列高武所願欲
而不得見者顧見之哀帝之世則是禦戎
之道所以制馭於無事之日者不專事於
外攘而在於脩內治不必勤遠略而貴於
謹邇圖亦甚明矣洪惟
聖朝汛掃胡元肅清區宇雕題垂髻之俗一旦
復而為禮樂衣冠之區誠有以立萬世之
功雪百王之耻矣柰何邇年以來蠢玆遺
===
醜頗肆猖獗尚勞盛秋之戍頗勤中夏之
師而今時將以為有事耶抑無事耶昔賈
誼以漢之全盛而太息山濤以晉之外寧
而有憂然則今日之事蓋不能不勞執事
之慮也且今日所恃以威敵者兵也兵則
單弱而不振焉所恃以養兵者食也食則
匱乏而不給焉何以言之蓋
國初之選邊兵編戍之檄衛有定額未聞有不
足之兵今也戈矛之士白籍相雜行列之
punctuated:
書願朝，奉執國珍，賛謁稽首。前日狼貪虎噬之人，今與鵷班鷺序之列。高武所願欲而不得見者，顧見之哀帝之世。則是禦戎之道，所以制馭於無事之日者，不專事於外攘，而在於脩內治；不必勤遠略，而貴於謹邇圖，亦甚明矣。
洪惟聖朝汛掃胡元，肅清區宇，雕題垂髻之俗，一旦復而為禮樂衣冠之區，誠有以立萬世之功，雪百王之耻矣。柰何邇年以來，蠢玆遺醜，頗肆猖獗，尚勞盛秋之戍，頗勤中夏之師。而今時將以為有事耶？抑無事耶？昔賈誼以漢之全盛而太息，山濤以晉之外寧而有憂。然則今日之事，蓋不能不勞執事之慮也。
且今日所恃以威敵者，兵也；兵則單弱而不振焉。所恃以養兵者，食也；食則匱乏而不給焉。何以言之？蓋國初之選邊兵，編戍之檄，衛有定額，未聞有不足之兵。今也戈矛之士，白籍相雜；行列之
translation_en:
…a letter requesting to attend court, bearing the treasures of his realm, to be announced in audience and bow his head to the ground. Those who formerly were rapacious as wolves and ravenous as tigers now took their places in the ordered ranks of court officials. What Emperors Gao and Wu had desired but never witnessed was instead witnessed in Emperor Ai’s reign. Thus the way to defend against the frontier peoples and keep them under control in times of peace is abundantly clear: it consists not solely in repelling them abroad, but in cultivating good government at home; it requires no strenuous pursuit of distant strategies, but prizes careful planning for what lies close at hand.
We reverently reflect that our sagely dynasty swept away the alien Yuan and purged the realm. Lands marked by the customs of tattooed foreheads and hanging topknots were suddenly restored to the rites, music, dress, and headgear of civilized society. Truly, this established an achievement for all ages and erased the humiliation of a hundred reigns. Why, then, have these vile remnants stirred in recent years and become so rampant, still requiring arduous garrison service at the height of autumn and repeated military exertions in midsummer? Should the present be considered a time of trouble, or a time of peace? In the past, Jia Yi sighed deeply when the Han was at the height of its prosperity, and Shan Tao harbored anxieties when the Jin enjoyed outward tranquility. Surely present affairs cannot but demand the concern of you gentlemen in authority.
Moreover, what we rely upon today to overawe the enemy is our troops; yet our troops are weak and fail to recover their strength. What we rely upon to sustain those troops is grain; yet grain is scarce and supplies are insufficient. Why do I say this? At the dynasty’s founding, when frontier troops were selected, the orders assigning garrison service prescribed a fixed quota for each guard, and one never heard of a shortage of soldiers. Today, among the men bearing spears and lances, there is an admixture of names on irregular registers [?]; the troops in the ranks…

title: 正德十一年陝西鄉試錄
text:
師逃亡中半加以衣廩不足以厚其生賞
犒不足以激其勸兵之不足有由然也
國家之備邊儲會計之條歲有常數未聞有
不足之食今也師旅之興日繁而營田頗
廢饑饉之害相仍而賦稅浸虧加以冗食
之兵張顧待哺守庾之吏費出無經食之
不足有由然也夫兵者國之爪牙兵之不
足養之無道也食者國之元氣食之不足
生之無道也茲欲兵足而司戎兵者無單
===
弱之慮愚謂兵不在益惟在養之而已矣
能公選閱以存精銳嚴清理以實營伍厚
衣廩以安其生優犒賞以作其氣而又統
御之得人則養之有道三表五餌之術不
必用而兵無不足矣抑欲食足而司儲餉
者無匱乏之憂愚謂賦不必加在生之而
已矣能廣營田以開其源裁冗食以節其
流征斂有制而逋負之必覈費出有經而
侵漁之必究而又經理之得人則生之有
punctuated:
師，逃亡中半，加以衣廩不足以厚其生，賞犒不足以激其勸，兵之不足有由然也。
國家之備邊儲，會計之條，歲有常數，未聞有不足之食。今也師旅之興日繁，而營田頗廢；饑饉之害相仍，而賦稅浸虧。加以冗食之兵張顧待哺，守庾之吏費出無經，食之不足有由然也。夫兵者，國之爪牙；兵之不足，養之無道也。食者，國之元氣；食之不足，生之無道也。
茲欲兵足，而司戎兵者無單弱之慮，愚謂兵不在益，惟在養之而已矣。能公選閱以存精銳，嚴清理以實營伍，厚衣廩以安其生，優犒賞以作其氣，而又統御之得人，則養之有道，三表五餌之術不必用，而兵無不足矣。抑欲食足，而司儲餉者無匱乏之憂，愚謂賦不必加，在生之而已矣。能廣營田以開其源，裁冗食以節其流，征斂有制而逋負之必覈，費出有經而侵漁之必究，而又經理之得人，則生之有
translation_en:
…of the troops in the ranks, half have deserted. Moreover, clothing and grain allowances are insufficient to provide them with an adequate livelihood, and rewards and bounty are insufficient to spur their efforts. The shortage of troops thus has its causes.
In the state's provision of frontier reserves, the accounting regulations prescribe fixed annual amounts; formerly, one never heard of a shortage of provisions. Now military mobilizations grow more frequent by the day, while cultivation on military farms has largely fallen into neglect. Famines follow one upon another, while tax receipts steadily diminish. Moreover, supernumerary soldiers consuming rations look about with mouths agape, waiting to be fed, while the officials in charge of the granaries disburse supplies without established rules. The shortage of provisions thus has its causes. Soldiers are the state's claws and teeth; their insufficiency arises from failure to maintain them properly. Provisions are the state's vital energy; their insufficiency arises from failure to produce them properly.
If we now wish to have sufficient troops, so that those in charge of military affairs need not worry about depleted and weakened forces, I humbly submit that the answer lies solely in maintaining the troops, rather than increasing their numbers. If selection and inspection are conducted impartially to retain the best soldiers, and the rolls are rigorously checked and put in order to fill the ranks; if clothing and grain allowances are made ample to secure their livelihood, and bounty and rewards generous to raise their spirits; and if, furthermore, suitable men are placed in command, then the troops will be maintained properly. There will be no need to employ the techniques of the “three demonstrations and five baits,” and there will be no shortage of troops.
Again, if we wish to have sufficient provisions, so that those in charge of reserves and military supplies need not worry about shortages, I humbly submit that taxes need not be increased: the answer lies simply in producing provisions. If cultivation on military farms is expanded to increase the source of supply, and supernumerary ration recipients are reduced to limit its outflow; if tax collection is regulated and arrears invariably examined, while disbursements follow established rules and embezzlement and extortion are invariably investigated; and if, furthermore, suitable men are entrusted with management, then the production of provisions will have…

title: 正德十一年陝西鄉試錄
text:
道九貢九賦之法可不必厚而食無不足
矣如此則戰勝守固又何夷狄之足患乎
雖然此特因明問所及而畧陳其槩耳而
愚生鄉邦之慮欲言之悃猶有望於執事
者夫夷狄之爲患延寧甘肅三邊爲急腹
裏之藩衛延寧二鎮爲重故虜騎深入每
由於安定二邊備之所當嚴也愚欲脩濬
牆塹以固邊防可乎守備單怯莫甚於花
馬池廣武營一帶處之所當預也愚欲增
===
設衛所以壯邊兵可乎靈州環慶之要衝
土人之無統紀久矣愚欲經理靈夏以安
內附可乎韋州虜寇所出没保障之無特
賴甚矣愚欲整飭韋州以遏外侵可乎撤
東勝而就延綏以一面而遮千里北虜之
患莫能禦矣愚欲俟富强之餘復守東勝
因河爲固可乎然此實備禦之良法亦非
草茅之私議也故特爲執事終篇陳惟執
事其亟圖之謹對
punctuated: 道，九貢九賦之法可不必厚，而食無不足矣。如此，則戰勝守固，又何夷狄之足患乎？雖然，此特因明問所及而畧陳其槩耳。而愚生鄉邦之慮、欲言之悃，猶有望於執事者。夫夷狄之爲患，延寧甘肅三邊爲急；腹裏之藩衛，延寧二鎮爲重。故虜騎深入，每由於安定二邊，備之所當嚴也。愚欲脩濬牆塹以固邊防，可乎？守備單怯，莫甚於花馬池廣武營一帶，處之所當預也。愚欲增設衛所以壯邊兵，可乎？靈州環慶之要衝，土人之無統紀久矣。愚欲經理靈夏以安內附，可乎？韋州虜寇所出没，保障之無特賴甚矣。愚欲整飭韋州以遏外侵，可乎？撤東勝而就延綏，以一面而遮千里，北虜之患莫能禦矣。愚欲俟富强之餘，復守東勝，因河爲固，可乎？然此實備禦之良法，亦非草茅之私議也。故特爲執事終篇陳，惟執事其亟圖之。謹對。
translation_en:
…in the proper way, the levies prescribed under the nine categories of tribute and the nine categories of taxation need not be heavy, and provisions will be sufficient. With this accomplished, we shall win in battle and hold firm in defense: what cause would there then be to fear the barbarians?

Nevertheless, I have merely outlined these matters in response to the subjects covered by your illuminating question. As for my concern for my native region and my sincere desire to speak, I still have hopes of you, sir. In confronting the barbarian threat, the three frontier commands of Yansui, Ningxia, and Gansu are the most urgently important; as shields for the interior, the two garrisons of Yansui and Ningxia carry the greatest weight. Enemy cavalry penetrating deep into our territory regularly come through the two frontier sectors of An and Ding [?]; here defenses must be stringent. Might we repair the walls and deepen the moats to strengthen the frontier defenses? Nowhere are the defenses weaker than along the stretch encompassing Huamachi and Guangwu Camp; arrangements there must be made beforehand. Might we establish additional guards and battalions to strengthen the frontier forces?

At the strategic points of Lingzhou, Huan, and Qing, the local inhabitants have long lacked organized control. Might we put the affairs of Lingzhou and Ningxia in order to keep those who have submitted to our rule at peace? Weizhou is a place where enemy raiders come and go, and its defenses grievously lack anything dependable [?]. Might we put Weizhou’s defenses in order to check incursions from outside? Since withdrawing from Dongsheng and falling back on Yansui, we have attempted to screen a thousand li with a single defensive front, leaving us unable to ward off the threat from the northern barbarians. Might we, once sufficient wealth and strength have been attained, resume the defense of Dongsheng and rely on the Yellow River as a natural fortification?

These are, indeed, sound methods of defensive preparation, not merely the private opinions of a man outside official service. I therefore present them especially to you at the close of this essay, hoping that you will urgently consider them. Respectfully submitted in reply.

title: 正德十一年陝西鄉試錄
text:
陜西鄉試録後序
正德丙子〔楚〕不敏獲與閱陜
西之士焉讀其文而歎夫河
嶽之英之異也又歎夫士之
多不勝取也於是擇其尤者
而取之如額焉祇録之以貢
于
===
上蓋録其士及其文及夫執事者
焉兹鄉試録之所由名也夫
録士以貢者何賓興之也故
燕而後興使録者勸未及者
知企而勉焉我
聖祖酌古立法蓋如此其作人也
不既多績矣乎夫士也生有
punctuated:
陜西鄉試録後序

正德丙子，〔楚〕不敏，獲與閱陜西之士焉。讀其文而歎夫河嶽之英之異也，又歎夫士之多不勝取也。於是擇其尤者而取之如額焉，祇録之以貢于上。蓋録其士及其文及夫執事者焉，兹鄉試録之所由名也。

夫録士以貢者何？賓興之也。故燕而後興，使録者勸，未及者知企而勉焉。我聖祖酌古立法，蓋如此其作人也，不既多績矣乎？夫士也，生有
translation_en:
Postface to the Record of the Shaanxi Provincial Examination

In the bingzi year of the Zhengde reign [1516], I, 〔Chu〕, though lacking ability, had the privilege of participating in the examination of Shaanxi’s scholars. Reading their compositions, I marveled at the extraordinary talents nurtured by its rivers and mountains. I also lamented that the scholars were so numerous that we could not select them all. We therefore chose the most outstanding among them, filling the prescribed quota, and respectfully recorded them for presentation to the Emperor. This records the scholars, their compositions, and the officials conducting the examination: hence its name, Record of the Provincial Examination.

Why record scholars for presentation to the Emperor? To honor them as guests and advance them. Thus they are feasted before being advanced, so that those recorded receive encouragement, while those who have not yet succeeded learn to aspire and exert themselves. Our sagely founding emperor drew upon antiquity in establishing these regulations: such was his way of nurturing talent. Has it not already yielded abundant results? As for scholars, their birth has…

title: 正德十一年陝西鄉試錄
text:
自習有業舉有序錄之故弗
得而弗詳也夫陜西之域幅
員萬里今屬之藩司非鄉矣
曰鄉試云者仍鄉舉之舊也
故士之未試也必於鄉考德
而論行焉錄則曰鄉舉之人
也曰鄉舉之人者謂所錄皆
===
一鄉之士也使由此而進則
其爲國士爲天下士爲百世
士亦存乎人焉耳錄其文者
何謂士之所錄者在是也蓋
以言觀之也言可以觀人乎
哉言也者心之聲也心有邪
正則言有是非昧道之人其
punctuated:
自，習有業，舉有序，錄之故弗得而弗詳也。夫陜西之域，幅員萬里，今屬之藩司，非鄉矣。曰鄉試云者，仍鄉舉之舊也。故士之未試也，必於鄉考德而論行焉。錄則曰鄉舉之人也。曰鄉舉之人者，謂所錄皆一鄉之士也。使由此而進，則其爲國士、爲天下士、爲百世士，亦存乎人焉耳。
錄其文者何？謂士之所錄者在是也，蓋以言觀之也。言可以觀人乎哉？言也者，心之聲也。心有邪正，則言有是非。昧道之人，其
translation_en:
…origins, their studies have a particular pursuit, and their selection follows an established order; thus the record of them cannot but be detailed. The territory of Shaanxi extends over ten thousand li. It now falls under the Provincial Administration Commission and is no mere local community. Calling this the Provincial Examination preserves the old practice of selection through local communities. Thus, before scholars sit the examination, their virtue must be assessed and their conduct appraised in their own communities. The record accordingly calls them men recommended by their local communities. This designation means that all those recorded are scholars of a particular locality. If they advance from this point, whether they become scholars distinguished within the state, throughout the realm, or across a hundred generations rests with the individuals themselves.
Why record their writings? Because these are the basis upon which the scholars are selected: they are judged through their words. Can words be used to judge a person? Words are the voice of the heart. As the heart may be deviant or upright, so words may be wrong or right. Those who are ignorant of the Way, their…

title: 正德十一年陝西鄉試錄
text:
辭晦畔道之人其辭支談道
之人其辭張褻道之人其辭
侮知道之人其辭暢體道之
人其辭醇有道之人其辭時
時也者待扣而應無弗醇暢
者也夫行有九德惟言也亦
然寛而栗柔而立直而溫獨
===
不可言察之哉此又察諸言
意之表者也故觀其文察其
心由是而論其賢否焉斯庶
幾矣其或不然則吾有司之
不明非士之罪也孟子曰我
知言又曰聽其言也人焉廋
哉蓋謂是耳故錄其文即所
punctuated: 辭晦；畔道之人，其辭支；談道之人，其辭張；褻道之人，其辭侮；知道之人，其辭暢；體道之人，其辭醇；有道之人，其辭時。時也者，待扣而應，無弗醇暢者也。夫行有九德，惟言也亦然：寛而栗，柔而立，直而溫，獨不可言察之哉？此又察諸言意之表者也。故觀其文，察其心，由是而論其賢否焉，斯庶幾矣。其或不然，則吾有司之不明，非士之罪也。孟子曰：「我知言。」又曰：「聽其言也，人焉廋哉？」蓋謂是耳。故錄其文，即所
translation_en: …their words are obscure. Those who depart from the Way speak evasively; those who merely talk of the Way speak grandiloquently; those who profane the Way speak irreverently; those who understand the Way speak lucidly; those who embody the Way speak with purity; and those who possess the Way speak as the occasion requires. Speaking as the occasion requires means responding when prompted, always with purity and lucidity. Conduct has nine virtues, and speech likewise: generous yet firm, gentle yet resolute, upright yet warm. Can these not also be discerned through speech? This, moreover, involves discerning what lies beyond the words and their meaning. Thus, by examining their compositions and discerning their hearts, we may judge whether they are worthy, and thereby come close to a sound assessment. Should this fail, the fault lies in the lack of discernment of us responsible officials, not in the candidates. Mengzi said, “I understand words.” He also said, “Listen to his words: how can a person conceal himself?” This, surely, is what is meant. Thus, recording their compositions is precisely the means by which…

title: 正德十一年陝西鄉試錄
text:
以錄其行也道也德也又將
以夷考之也徒文也乎哉錄
止於若干篇者不勝錄也所
謂擇其尤者耳錄及于執事
之人者何也謂錄士其責也
錄之行得失不可掩已得則
成其功否則來之議又否則
===
朝野非笑之而譴亦隨之矣
他日士大有功於名教千載
而下有論其世者譬猶和于
玉隋于珠同不泯矣苟為反
是則士也人將穢之而亦何
顏哉書曰舉能其官惟爾之
能稱匪其人惟爾不任亦謂
punctuated:
以錄其行也、道也、德也，又將以夷考之也，徒文也乎哉？錄止於若干篇者，不勝錄也，所謂擇其尤者耳。錄及于執事之人者，何也？謂錄士，其責也。錄之行，得失不可掩已。得則成其功，否則來之議，又否則朝野非笑之，而譴亦隨之矣。
他日士大有功於名教，千載而下有論其世者，譬猶和于玉、隋于珠，同不泯矣。苟為反是，則士也，人將穢之，而亦何顏哉？《書》曰：「舉能其官，惟爾之能；稱匪其人，惟爾不任。」亦謂
translation_en:
…thereby recording their conduct, their Way, and their virtue, and also providing a means to examine these closely. Could this be merely a record of literary compositions? The record is limited to a certain number of pieces because it is impossible to record them all: this is what is meant by selecting the most outstanding. Why does the record also include those who administered the examination? Because selecting scholars is their responsibility. Once the record circulates, their successes and failures cannot be concealed. If they have chosen rightly, their achievement is established; otherwise, they invite criticism [?]; worse still, they will be censured and ridiculed at court and throughout the country, and punishment will follow.
If, in days to come, these scholars make great contributions to moral teaching, those who discuss their age a thousand years hence will remember the officials together with them, just as He is remembered for his jade and Sui for his pearl: neither will fade from memory. If the reverse should occur, people will regard these scholars with contempt—and what face will the officials themselves have left? The Book of Documents says: “If those you recommend are capable of fulfilling their offices, that is your ability; if those you commend are not the right men, you are unequal to your responsibility.” This likewise means…

title: 正德十一年陝西鄉試錄
text:
是耳於戲執事者於士相闗
如是哉玆其所以録也玆其
所以望於二三子者不淺也
二三子大河秦華之英也二
南之遺民也後乎周公召公
張子而覺焉者也行且仕矣
可不奮哉子夏曰仕而優則
===
學學而優則仕此要言也古
之人所以加于人者無他焉
學與仕相資焉而已矣後之
人脩其天爵以要人爵旣得
人爵棄其天爵故學而仕者
皆然仕而學者未之多聞也
夫學也或非古人之學而仕
punctuated: 是耳。於戲！執事者於士相闗如是哉！玆其所以録也，玆其所以望於二三子者不淺也。二三子，大河秦華之英也，二南之遺民也，後乎周公、召公、張子而覺焉者也。行且仕矣，可不奮哉？子夏曰：「仕而優則學，學而優則仕。」此要言也。古之人所以加于人者，無他焉，學與仕相資焉而已矣。後之人脩其天爵以要人爵，旣得人爵，棄其天爵。故學而仕者皆然，仕而學者未之多聞也。夫學也，或非古人之學，而仕
translation_en: …that is all. Alas! Such is the close connection between those administering the examination and the scholars! This is why this record has been compiled, and why our expectations of you gentlemen are far from slight. You gentlemen are the outstanding talents of the great river, Qin, and Mount Hua; you are heirs to the people of the Two Southern Sections of the Book of Odes, and men who have come to understanding after the Duke of Zhou, the Duke of Shao, and Master Zhang. You will soon enter official service: can you fail to exert yourselves? Zixia said: “When official service leaves strength to spare, study; when study leaves strength to spare, enter official service.” These are essential words. The ancients surpassed others for no other reason than that their learning and official service supported one another. Later men cultivate their heavenly nobility—their moral virtues—to obtain human nobility, or official rank; once they have obtained human nobility, they abandon their heavenly nobility. Thus those who study and then enter office all behave this way, while one seldom hears of those who continue to study after entering office. As for their learning, it may not be the learning of the ancients; and their official service…

title: 正德十一年陝西鄉試錄
text:
亦或非其仕矣又從而偏廢
焉則夫道不明而治不善也
亦何怪哉愚於是爲二三子
願焉必也學而入政仕而典
學使先王之道於吾身見之
而吾心之極時萬時億者其
淵也夫如是則學無不至道
===
亦大行固將與河嶽同流峙
焉而周召之徒不得專美於
先矣所謂由此而進爲天下
士爲百世士者此也執事者
嘗選於衆而獻之不亦有榮
乎哉不亦庶幾託以不泯乎
哉以愚從執事者之後是故
punctuated: 亦或非其仕矣。又從而偏廢焉，則夫道不明而治不善也，亦何怪哉？愚於是爲二三子願焉：必也學而入政，仕而典學，使先王之道於吾身見之，而吾心之極，時萬時億者，其淵也夫！如是，則學無不至，道亦大行，固將與河嶽同流峙焉，而周召之徒不得專美於先矣。所謂由此而進爲天下士、爲百世士者，此也。執事者嘗選於衆而獻之，不亦有榮乎哉？不亦庶幾託以不泯乎哉？以愚從執事者之後，是故
translation_en: …and service in office, too, may fail to be what it should be. If one then neglects either learning or service, what wonder is it that the Way remains obscure and government is poor? I therefore venture to express this wish for you gentlemen: you must proceed from learning to government and, while serving in office, devote yourselves to learning, so that the Way of the former kings becomes manifest in your own persons. The utmost reach of our hearts, extending through ten thousand and a hundred million ages, would be its deep source [?]. If this is accomplished, learning will attain its fullest extent, and the Way will prevail widely. You will assuredly flow like the rivers and stand like the mountains; the likes of the dukes of Zhou and Shao will no longer enjoy unrivalled distinction among your predecessors. This is what it means to advance from here to become scholars of significance to all under Heaven and to a hundred generations. Those conducting this examination have selected you from among the multitude and presented you: is this not an honor? May they not also hope to entrust to you something that will never perish? Since I follow after those conducting this examination, therefore…

title: 正德十一年陝西鄉試錄
text:
望於二三子者不淺也是故
於二三子不敢不告也
直隷河間府河間縣儒學教
諭李楚謹序
punctuated:
望於二三子者不淺也，是故於二三子不敢不告也。
直隷河間府河間縣儒學教諭李楚謹序。
translation_en:
…my hopes for you gentlemen are far from slight. For this reason, I dare not fail to convey these words to you.
Li Chu, Instructor in the Confucian School of Hejian County, Hejian Prefecture, Zhili, respectfully composed this preface.
